I should have been packed properly and the inside should have been thoroughly stuffed with paper and also wrapped in paper so that it could make the long journey from China.  I contacted the vendor and they wanted pictures  so that they can see what was done wrong.  I thought they wanted to see how they can improve their packaging for future shipments.  The vendor told me to "WASH the hat" and all the creases and dents will come out.  I'm  not stupid.  This is not my first hat and I know better.  This hat needs to be professionally steamed and reblocked to restore the shape. That needs a special wood head form that matches the shape of the hat, a special technique and a person that knows what they are doing.  I was planning to wear this to church for Christmas Eve.  Now I have to find someone who can reblock the hat without causing further damage and not charge me an arm and a leg to do it.  Amazon gave me a courtesy credit to help defray the cost of having it reblocked because the hat itself is very nice, but this vendor deserves zero stars in my opinion,
summary: Vendor shipping department and customer service are worthless

reviewText: Is it super accurate in calculating distance ran?  Could anything that works like this ever be?  It's accurate enough.  But that is not the most useful feature anyway. YOU CAN INSTANTLY SEE IF YOUR PACE IS DROPPING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Are you a serious runner?  Do you want to hit your mark on a long distance run, especially an unmarked run? This is your coach riding next to you telling you to pick it up! When I head out on a run I already know how far I'm going and know what pace I want to run.  I use this device to keep me me on pace. I also like the auto-logging of my runs using the online features.  Finish your run plug it into your computer and get some instant gratification from it showing you how you hit your marks.  I use to write down what I did on a calendar. Now, WOW, look at a whole year of running on your computer screen!  Look at several years.  From a guy who's been a serious runner for over 40 years, it is wonderful.  Get a little pouch to hold the sensor in non-Nike+ shoes.  I usually wear a regular running watch to show my overall time and splits (if i'm on a marked course) and the sports band on my other wrist with the pace feature selected.  Con: It is hard or impossible to see at night (no back light) so depends on how many street lights on your route.

reviewText: I bought this as one of the holiday lightning deals for under $7.  It was a quick reaction purchase and after looking around and using it for a bit I think there might be better options available.  The balaclava does provide moderate resistance to the elements.  I bought it for hiking and general outdoor use so snow mobile users might want something a bit heavier.  I also like the length as it is long enough to slide under your layers, keeping out any drafts.  The balaclava is also pretty compact, which is nice for me because I like to keep it in my outdoor jacket.My gripe (and thus 3 stars) with the product comes from the opening.  The way it sits on my face leaves more room above the eyes than I would want.  It also angles up too sharply once you cover your nose.  The picture shows a nice flat line over the face creating a peanut sort of shape.  In reality it immediately angles up and rests uncomfortably close to your eyes.  The one size fits all tag should always raise a red flag.  This one fits best if you leave your nose exposed, but then you are kind of defeating the point.  Overall, I still prefer it to having to carry a scarf and beanie, but it definitely has some flaws.

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

A male friend of ours who runs his own dojo also found it very helpful because he could relate first hand to the journey of the teachers and the struggles they experienced in setting up and establishing a dojo.  He also found it insightful because it gave him a deeper understanding the struggles that females have in developing and expressing the art.

description: Unfazed by the scientific age, pashmina shawls are hand spun the same way it has been done for centuries. The hairs are gathered from the Himalayan goat called Hircus, which lives at high altitudes, 12 to 14000 feet in the mountains. The Pashmina is gathered by hand, stored and combed by nomadic herders. The threads are hand woven on handlooms over a silk wrap, which gives the fabric resilience. Once the fabric is loomed, each piece is hand dyed in open vats. Afterwards it is given to the different craftsmen for hand-embroidery, beading and /or printing. They are very soft and luxurious in feel. reviewText: The Casio Pathfinder is a great watch.  The titanium band/case is very durable and even though titanium tends to scratch easy, I havent noticed any scratches on the band yet and its been through hell.  I found out while traveling that I had to calibrate the altimeter a lot, which can be a problem if you dont know what altitude you are at to begin with cause then you cant calibrate it.  The compass tends to be accurate and that can be a useful feature to the outdoors type.  Im currently deployed in afghanistan and I hope I never need to rely on my watch to get me back t base but its good to have back-ups.  As far as the temp/barometer go Im not so sure.  The temperature gets thrown off by your body heat, but if you take it off and let it acclimatized then you can get a more accurate reading.  I dont know how to read barometric pressure, but Im sure once I figure that out it could become useful.  The worldtime feature helps a lot esp when Im traveling around the world but still need to know the times back home and my destination.  Atomic time keeping keeps your watch accurate so you never need to worry about setting it yourself.  Over all its a great watch, very light weight (it will surprise you), and will last you a long time.  I realized the solar power feature charges pretty fast and there a battery meter that will let you know well before hand that it needs recharging.  Im outside a lot so it tends to stay fully charged. This watch if definitely worth the cost.

reviewText: This watch is much lighter than you would think on viewing the photos.  It is striking in its appearance, though quite large so perhaps best suited to those with larger wrists.  The titanium band has a nice feature in that the back of the watch is stiff at the initial links so as to prevent slippage around the wrist.  It will likely be necessary to have the strap adjusted and you'll probably need to visit a jeweler or watch repair shop to have it done because it's next to impossible without the specialized tools needed.The watch itself is feature-rich, but the instructions take time to decipher.  Be prepared to have to calibrate the sensors or there will be variance.  The solar powered battery works as advertised, but don't expect a full charge unless you leave it in a window in the sun or under a lamp for a few hours.  It will maintain current charge levels simply based on available light when worn in regular daytime conditions.My only complaint (aside from the inadequacy of the instruction manual) is that the volume of the tones used is quite low and doesn't appear to be adjustable, e.g., alarm, timer, hourly chime, etc....  That said, it's not an atomic watch so you'll need to adjust time based on applicable timezone, i.e., it won't set automatically via radio signals.  The same watch with this feature costs about $50 or so more at the time I purchased and, unless you travel frequently, may not be worth the extra cost.Overall, it's an excellent watch that represents great value when you consider style and features relative to cost.  I would recommend this to anyone who wants something a little more useful than a standard timepiece.

reviewText: I had been accustomed to walking 2 miles a day a few times a weeks, but needed a new pair of good walking shoes. After reading all the glowing reviews for this shoe, I decided to splurge for a pair. I am a 8.5 shoe size and I ordered a size 8.5 and they are a good fit, but if I wore thick socks, they would be on the small side. They are super comfortable and really feel like you are walking on dry sand (heal sinks in/down and your arch is supported). The cushion in the middle of the shoe sole feels really good on my arches, and like others who have reviewed MBT's shoes, you can feel them working more muscles than in regular shoes. The only reason I did not give this shoe 5 stars is because after only one mile of walking in them: blisters! And yes, I wore socks (goldtoe, in fact). Look closely at the heal of the shoe; it is angled in towards the Achilles tendon and, to me, seems like a huge design flaw. Why would the "unshoe" be designed in a way that pinches your heal like crappy sneakers do? Now I can only wear them for short distances and, I guess, wait for them to break in (?). Or maybe my feet are just weird... Anyone else out there have this heal-pinch problem?

reviewText: While your humble author always knows what time it is, in the proverbial sense, I am not always chronologically calibrated to The Man's time keeping devices. The world does not begrudge me for this. How can the sun shine at any other time than it's supposed to? How can a bird be too late to soar the skies? Does the ringing of an hourly bell determine when the blossoms bloom? Surely not. Thusly, how my manager Rhonda seems to think that it should mandate the allocation of my highly valuable time and skills, is baffling to me. I digress. In an effort to remain employed and woefully under-appreciated as a stocker at the local grocers, I invested in this, the finest of time pieces from Casio. It has a daily alarm option that has no doubt been helpful in attaining the goal of waking up on time to appease my very fundamentally unhappy employer. What loveless scorn has wrought such hurt upon you Rhonda? If it were not for your poor hygiene, generally unpleasant demeanor and woefully negligible posterior, I might undertake the endeavor of giving you a glimpse into a life filled with carnal love that is truly worth living. I digress once again. I feel it unfair that my necessity to obtain dividends should disrupt the slumber patterns of my various nightly companions. Therefore the light included with the chronograph allows me to discreetly educate myself of the time and prepare myself for the coming day while I compose my particular paramour a sonnet of sensuality to satiate her longing desire for my obsequious nature in the most intimate of manners in my absence. I assure you, this is my final digression. We all must make sacrifices to obtain what we want most, and if your sacrifice includes needing to know what apocryphal designations on an imaginary timescale correspond to when your bus will be departing, such as I do at this moment, then this Casio F-91W will satisfy your exigencies.

reviewText: This watch doesn't do everything, and it doesn't do everything it does do perfectly.  But it works well enough to be useful.  If you're looking to replicate the smartphone experience on your wrist, pick a different smartwatch.  But if you want something that will move some of the more mundane tasks off your smartphone and into a more readily accessible location, this is a good buy.As another reviewer has said, DO NOT pay more than $150 for this watch--if it's priced above that, you're just lining the pockets of a third-party reseller.  If Amazon isn't selling it, just go to getpebble.com.My job requires me to use a six-digit passcode on my iPhone (or carry a separate device for work emails).  The Pebble lets me triage emails and text messages to see whether it's worth pulling my phone out of my pocket.  Over the course of a day and a hundred emails, that's a pretty significant time saver.  That, in itself, would make this worthwhile for me.Having weather on the watchface (which will require you to download one of the multitude of watchfaces that offer this feature--I like Modern and Futura Weather) has also been great over the course of a blustery spring during which the temperature has been swinging like a drug-addled pendulum.  That said, I'd like the feature a lot better if it were drawing from a better source.  The watchface apps draw from, I believe, an open-source weather site that, for Washington D.C. and for the last couple of weeks, at least, has been between five and ten degrees off the actual temperature.  Still, having a ballpark and knowing if it's raining outside reduce the number of mornings I have to schlep back up to my apartment to get an umbrella.Your mileage may vary on the apps, but I have yet to find one that's terribly useful.  The Runkeeper companion screen (it's not really an app) is pretty useful for keeping track of how long, how far, and how fast you're running, if you're into that sort of thing.Pebble Cards has promise, but it's brutally slow.  Yelp seems decent except that I usually want more information than could fit on a watch face so I use my phone for that anyway.  Still, since app development uses a pretty common language and Pebble is all about experimentation and homebrew software, I expect we'll start seeing some clever uses of the tech over the next year.Also, it strikes me as borderline ridiculous that there's no built-in battery monitor--you will want to install one in one of your eight slots first thing.  The battery life has been decent--4-5 days seems to be about the limit for a charge, and I usually just charge it every other night.Again, make sure you understand what it can and can't do up front.  If you go in with reasonable expectations, the Pebble won't disappoint.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

description: The original Neoprene Eyewear Retainer -- patented in 1978 -- remains one of Croakies' most popular models. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: This is a Chinese $5 watch masquerading as a $50 watch. Even though it looked impressive and kept time well when I first started wearing it, I just tossed mine into the trash after attempting to replace the SR626SW battery for the first time, because its general condition after little more than a year of light use was so bad that I didn't want to spend $3 to $5 for a new watch cell.Here's a list of things I found to be objectionable or unacceptable:* The body is made of painted pot metal.  It is bulky and heavy, and the finish is easily damaged.* The stainless steel back is difficult to remove, as the notch for prying it off is obstructed by part of the watch case.  Damage to the case finish is unavoidable and to the o-ring is likely.  Due to the pot metal body, which corrodes fairly easily, water resistance after reassembly is unlikely to be achieved.* The spring pin tips are made of soft, annealed steel that deformed easily even while I attempted to disengage them to remove the strap and gain access to the watch back.  From perspiration and occasional washing of the strap, the innards of the spring pins on my watch had rusted to the point of no longer functioning.  Even a drop of Kroil penetrating oil was unable to bring them back to life.* The adjusting stem is nickel-plated brass, and on mine the plating was completely gone.* The "crystal" appears to be soft soda-lime glass, easily scratched.* For the size of the watch body, the Japanese movement inside is tiny, and the watch battery is puny, giving it short service life.  A larger movement could have accommodated a larger battery with longer life.About the only thing worth salvaging was the nylon webbing/Velcro watch band.  Perhaps I can pair it with a nice digital watch instead.  The band alone would probably sell for at least $5 as a replacement item.Even though the watch looked good when new, I would try to get it on a 60% or greater discount and expect it to be a disposable item.  I bought mine at Big 5 Sporting Goods when it was on sale for just under $20.

reviewText: I have several rubber watches and was attracted to the appearance and the functions of this particular watch.  I have a Brietling Aerospace Chronometer and the Momentum has the same functions at 1/10th the cost.I have had it about 2 weeks now and took it on a hiking trip to Glacier National Park.  It works fine, although navigating through the functions is not easily done as with a Timex or Casio with similar functions.  You have to read the manual to figure out how to set and work it.  The pros as i see it are: appearance, functions including multiple alarms, chromo, timer, world time and both digital and analog format.  Additionally synchronizing the analog and digital functions is easily done once you figure out how it works.  The cons (the reasons I gave this 4 stars instead of 5) are: difficulty/confusion in setting the watch and an unreadable night light function.  The night light backlights the led and makes it hard to read.  It would be a much better function if they just turned on the led lights without the backlight.  Otherwise it seems to be ok but that is with only two weeks experience with the watch.  It does have an energy saving capability where you can turn off the digital led and have it come back on automatically which seems to work well but I don't have any idea how long the battery will last with and without this capability.  All in all not a bad watch for the price.

description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: These boots appear to be well made and tough, while at the same time they fit perfectly and are very comfortable with a nice big toe box. I have an off-label purpose for them: I live in the California foothills and take my dogs for long walks every day in rough terrain that includes a reservoir, lots of hills, rocky slopes, dust in summer and mud in winter, foxtails and Velcro burrs at least half the year, and rattlesnakes. Ordinary hiking shoes and boots get penetrated by the rouge-fine dust and the foxtails, attract the burrs like magnets, and provide little-to-no protection against the rattlesnakes. These high-topped rubber boots, though never intended for hiking, give me exactly the walking gear I need for my daily excursions through tall dry grass and into the shallows with my dogs. I can't say yet how long the boots will put up with the kind of flexing associated with walking up hills and around steep slopes, but I can say that they aren't pinching or causing blisters. They aren't made to breathe so my feet get pretty hot but--with hiking socks over thin socks--they don't rub anywhere, and hot is better than all my alternatives. I fold my jeans around my ankles and pull the outer sock over the fold to keep the socks from walking down my heel and that works fine with these boots. They have a comfortable sole insert, though I will probably replace that with some orthotic cushioning. Good product, good price!

Sure I've owned eighty plus dollar athletic shoes, some being more durable with possibly slightly more comfortable and greater support, but....It reminds me of a story. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I know that the thermometer on this watch will vary according to my body temp. That being said, with it off my arm, it still seems to vary randomly. The altimeter and barometer seem to have this same problem too. I set it for my house altitude, and the next day, it is 40-60 feet off. The hands block the view of the digital display often. And my biggest complaint is that the digital time display is the smallest digits on the screen. It should be the largest. The watch is also huge, forget wearing it under long sleeves. I have been a fan of Casio watches for years, and their reliability is great, this one looks to be built very tough, and I'm sure it will last, but I am hesitant to wear it often since it is so big.It does have some good points: when in temp/baro or temp/altitude mode, it reads every few seconds for several minutes, then slows readings after several minutes to save battery life. The backlight works well. The analog hands have glow-in-the-dark feature that works well. The band is comfortable.I wish it had the feature of an old 20-year-old Casio thermometer watch- on and off-wrist modes. Unfortunately, that watch did not allow you to adjust the offsets, but it still made an attempt to counter the temperature difference while wearing it versus off-wrist. What would be nice is an adjustable on & off-wrist mode offset.I may just need to play with the offsets to get it to read more accurately. All three readings can be adjusted independently. I have used it in water, and not a leak has been found.All in all, I was going to return this for a smaller Casio watch, but my return period has expired.

reviewText: I purchased this watch last week and used it on an adult game and 2 tournament games.  The watch works well.  I like the single noise beep reminder at 30' and 15'.  The stoppage time clock feature is neat and I'm sure it'll come handy.  Great watch for the price.Two minor annoying things:1. When the countdown reaches 30 seconds, the watch beeps 10 times 4 short beeps.  It feels like it lasts for the full 30 seconds and it's an overkill; one series of 4-5 beeps would probably be enough.  The instructions state that pushing any button will stop the alarm.  I tried pushing the screen light button (right below the screen) but it didn't stop the sound.2. In a puzzling feature, the countdown timer can be set up to 99 minutes.  As most of us referees work games of varying length, the process of resetting the watch from 45' to 30' (like going from a U18 to a U12 game) requires scrolling all the way to 99 then from 1 to 30.  It seems trivial but it's unnecessary as anything longer than 45' in soccer is waste.

reviewText: This is the second Suunto Core watch I've owned. The last one I bought 'used' and after a good year and a half to two years of steady use, it gave up the ghost after an ongoing fight with some sort of moisture problem (it had it when I bought it). It was also plagued by frustratingly brief battery life, perhaps a symptom of the moisture issue somehow. Frankly, I was surprised it lasted as long as it did based upon its apparent ailment.Before it met its demise, I had purchased a nice Timex Expedition which had all of the same features but which was a little chunkier and squarish. I like the Timex and it fared well in Japan, India, and Nepal. However, it lacks the polish of the Suunto. I've had other friends with Suuntos who have nothing but good to say about them. So in spite of being a little put off by the first watch, I found a great deal on my new Suunto Core (Lava - it's actually quite a subtle color) and scooped it up.It's been a solid month since I received it now. I enjoy all of the same features of my old Suunto but, as it is brand sparky new, I have none of the moisture issues. This thing works like a champ. I've already had it out in sub-freezing temps, pouring rains, and out and about in the Guadalupe Mountains. I'd have to say that the altimeter is reasonably accurate and the compass is every bit as good as a liquid sealed version from Silva. I wear it nearly everyday while training and it looks just as good in the office environment.In short, I'm pleased to say that I highly recommend the Suunto Core to anyone who is serious about their outdoor adventure.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Marmot Women's Ama Dablam Jacket
description: The women's Marmot Ama Dablam is named after a Himalayan mountain, and is designed to keep you comfortably warm -- while traveling light -- in just such a setting. The durable down jacket offers maximum warmth with minimum weight, with enough urban style to transition to the city streets.FeaturesLightweight, super-warm down jacket100% polyester DWR ripstop main material100% polyester embossed WR lining800 fill goose down insulationAttached, adjustable down-filled hoodVertical front chest pocket for quick access to small essentialsInside zip stuff sack pocket allows you to stuff jacket into its own pocketElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherZippered handwarmer pocketsAdjustable Velcro and elastic cuffs for comfort and adjustabilityAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion in arms without jacket riding up28.5-inch center back lengthMarmot DownMarmot often says that "down is in our DNA." The company was founded in 1974 as a manufacturer and seller of premium down jackets, vests, and sleeping bags, and continues to use fine quality goose down for its insulated outdoor products. Mountaineers and outdoor enthusiasts the world over rely on Marmot down gear for warmth, comfort, and sometimes survival.Down quality is determined by fill power and durability, which is dependent upon the age and maturity of the bird and the processing of the down. The best down comes from larger, more mature birds and goose down is generally better than duck down. More mature goose down has larger filament clusters than less mature goose down and these clusters, when grouped, provide many more trapped air pockets and therefore provide better insulation. To maximize the effectiveness of the down clusters, proper processing of the down -- sorting, washing, and drying -- is required to open them up.Higher fill power means higher loft, better insulation, lighter weight, and greater durability. Marmot tests all of its down for content, cleanliness, species, and fill power, guaranteeing minimum fill power for all down clothing and sleeping bags.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

Where they dropped the ball is, there is a large continuous stitching that starts at one knee, comes up the thigh slightly inward, continues across the pelvic region, then back down the other side to the other knee. It also has an identical one on the backside. This appears to bring the inner thigh panels, and crotch panels, and bind them to the front and rear leg panels. Herein lies the problem.The location of the stitch and the fact that it is continuous rather than stopping and starting again at the leg/pelvic crease, renders these useless for any type of fitness where you would require to squat or lunge in any fashion.Every other pair of compression tights I have has the legs, and crotch, butt and inner thigh, all independent from each other to allow maximum movement and functionality, with no restriction point.These 110 tights are basically for sitting and recovering only.  If I were to squat down rapidly, they would explode and I would be naked. :)I was under the impression that these were able to be used as fitness tights, then you can immediately insert the ice packs and begin recovering right away. That is how its pitched and presented. They even come with a thermal bag for the ice packs to be taken with you to use right after whatever you do. That is not entire true.Bottom line. I am returning them due to their limited application. I can't see spending $200+ on them. If you are only looking to walk, light jog etc... and or just use them to sit around in then they are great. If you want to do anything vigorous in them, make sure you wear underwear in case you blow em out in public.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I used Polar HR monitors for years. They worked fine but they were expensive and battery replacement required mailing both the strap and the watch to an authorized repair place, paying money, and being without them for two weeks or so. The last time my Polar battery failed I bought an IsoKinetics HR monitor. That just didn't work. I ended up returning it with the help of Amazon (IsoKinetics didn't want it back until Amazon "encouraged" them.) With my fingers crossed I bought this Timex one. It's more expensive than the IsoKinetics but much cheaper than a Polar. Fortunately this one works fine. I've used it about eight times now. The first time or two the chest strap didn't make good enough skin contact but after it got some sweat on it it started working. (Polar is the same in this regard.) The display is big and clear enough to read at a glance while running. The buttons work fine. The wrist unit is convenient enough to put on and take off. It's fairly nice looking but big. The reading seems accurate. You can replace the chest strap battery yourself. The wrist unit battery can be replaced by a local watch repair store (you don't have to mail it somewhere). Two shortcomings compared to Polar: the reading isn't detected by some exercise machines that will detect Polar readings, and it has no extra features (no average HR, max HR, zone, etc.). You can display the duration of the current workout or the time of day by pushing a button, but that's the extent of its "features". Overall I'm very happy to give up the features in return for the substantially lower price. When I started with Polar years ago I used all the features just to entertain myself during the boring job of working out but after I got used to the features I stopped using them. What I really need is just to know my heart rate during exercise and this Timex model does that job very well.
summary: No extra features but works fine.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. reviewText: The overboots themselves are great. Pull all you want, they will stretch right over most of the boots you are wearing. Snug, secure, comfortable, and will last as long as several pairs of the cheap PVC boots. That's time saved going back to the supply warehouse. That is unless you have some oversized work boots to go into them.With most of my standard sized boots (Wolverine, Bass, etc) in 13W (approx 13 to 13-1/4" sole length), these slip on and off just fine.The problem is with my Thorogood 13W steel Moc toe wedge boot, which is a copy of a Red Wing 1907. I think Thorogood simply used their sz 14 lasts to make these, as the sole measures 13-7/8" from end to end (rolling the ruler along the sole). The steel Moc toes simply add to the bulk.The day I decided to get a pair of these (based on recommendations), I was wearing my smaller-soled Wolverines boots. I placed my boot on the measuring display on the side of the box, as well as the Treds measuring decal on the floor at the building supply store, and the measurement showed my boots were well under the max measuring line to use the L/XL sized overboots (odd choice for a boot size, since they also have an XL and XXL). The store didn't carry the XL or XXL, and I knew of only one other store in the county that carried this brand of overboots. Thought they would fit the same on all of my boots. After a couple of uses, though, I realize they just aren't going to work with the larger-soled Thorogood boots, as I discovered when I tried the overboots on them later.I love the Thorogood work boots; it's just that they're too big to fit into these overboots without a ton of effort to get them on and are nearly impossible to get off once forced on. I went back to the supply store and compared the Thorogood boots to the measuring display on the floor and box, and they came up just a hair width below the max measuring line for the L/XL size.I will look for the XL, one size up, for use with these boots or other Moc toe / steel toe boots, on the off chance they too are oversized. Wasn't really planning on getting two pairs, but thats what I am going to have to do. Fortunately, I will get plenty of use out of these pouring concrete, whichever workboots I'm wearing.At the Treds.com website (I discovered after the fact), they have a sizing chart (not available at the retailer I went to; they only had the put-your-shoe-on-the-line sticker on the floor, plus the measuring marks on the product box). The chart shows that a sole length of 13 1/4 - 13 3/4" should use the L/XL, 13 3/4 - 14 1/2" should use XL, and 14 1/2 - 15 1/2" should use XXL. Wish I had that info before I purchased the smaller pair. Now I will end up with two pairs.Finding the XL version here at Amazon takes a bit of work, though. A standard "Treds over shoe / boot" search doesn't show the XL model in the results. The seller who markets most of the other sizes here doesn't advertise the XL, and it is instead listed at Amazon under another title... "Treds XL Over the Shoe 17" Slush Boot", part number 17853, ASIN B001I014I8.If you wear longer 13's or 14's workboots, or larger, definitely try these on for size if possible, because they may not fit well.Note: These are not lined. I didn't find that a problem. Just thick, solid stretchy rubber.Update: Received the XL sized overboots, and they work perfectly with the larger workboots. Just FYI.
summary: Sizing Issues - Know your Workboot size...

description: The women's Marmot Ama Dablam is named after a Himalayan mountain, and is designed to keep you comfortably warm -- while traveling light -- in just such a setting. The durable down jacket offers maximum warmth with minimum weight, with enough urban style to transition to the city streets.FeaturesLightweight, super-warm down jacket100% polyester DWR ripstop main material100% polyester embossed WR lining800 fill goose down insulationAttached, adjustable down-filled hoodVertical front chest pocket for quick access to small essentialsInside zip stuff sack pocket allows you to stuff jacket into its own pocketElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherZippered handwarmer pocketsAdjustable Velcro and elastic cuffs for comfort and adjustabilityAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion in arms without jacket riding up28.5-inch center back lengthMarmot DownMarmot often says that "down is in our DNA." The company was founded in 1974 as a manufacturer and seller of premium down jackets, vests, and sleeping bags, and continues to use fine quality goose down for its insulated outdoor products. Mountaineers and outdoor enthusiasts the world over rely on Marmot down gear for warmth, comfort, and sometimes survival.Down quality is determined by fill power and durability, which is dependent upon the age and maturity of the bird and the processing of the down. The best down comes from larger, more mature birds and goose down is generally better than duck down. More mature goose down has larger filament clusters than less mature goose down and these clusters, when grouped, provide many more trapped air pockets and therefore provide better insulation. To maximize the effectiveness of the down clusters, proper processing of the down -- sorting, washing, and drying -- is required to open them up.Higher fill power means higher loft, better insulation, lighter weight, and greater durability. Marmot tests all of its down for content, cleanliness, species, and fill power, guaranteeing minimum fill power for all down clothing and sleeping bags.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

reviewText: I've had a Vector for 20 years and have not been able to kill it. Changed the battery many times. Skiing, hiking, trekking, snorkeling, running. It's great. I bought an X-Lander just for the metal case, but if it wasn't around, I'd get another Vector. After all that time, the only things wrong were that the liquid in the face bubble evaporated (it was there until two years ago)and the bezel compass markings have worn a bit.The X-Lander is just very cool looking with the metal case, a better rubber wristband, wider and a better keeper. I think this has taken the Vector's place as my favorite. The functions are identical and I know the settings already.However, THIS IS NOT FOR ACTIVE DUTY PERSONNEL OR ANYONE IN THE FIELD FOR LONG PERIODS. I was in Costa Rica for a week, and used insect repellant daily. The repellant softened the plastic of the battery to the point where the impressed lettering wore away and I could scratch the surface with my fingernail. The rest of the case and the strap were fine. I called Suunto about it and they told me that the manual says not to expose the watch to chemicals. I replied that soldiers and Marines use insect repellant much of the time, and that they should make the cover from Aluminum as they do the case. Apparently, this fell on deaf ears. They are sending me a replacement cover. I noticed in their accessories that they sell replacement covers, which are also available on Amazon here, so this seems to be their solution. But the case and plastic strap were not at all affected, just the battery cover. So, caveat emptor if you're going into jungle with mosquitoes around.My old Vector goes to my daughter.Amazon is my favorite vendor hands down. However, I would look at EMS for this watch. They have a lifetime warranty on their items. If it fails at 10 years, they'll replace it.
summary: Great looking but NOT A MILITARY WATCH.
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: This is a solid Timex heart rate monitor (HRM).PROS...Lots of functions and very easy to use, especially if you are familiar with Timex watches.  The large display makes it very easy to read, even while exercising. Plus, you can adjust what (HR or time) is the large number in the middle.  Another review gave it one star because of the size.  I like that it is big, easy to read and best of all, it feels like it is built well.  Most of the Polar HRMs I have seen, feel like they are made with cheap material that will break/wear out easily.  A button on my previous Polar RS300X broke into.  I have had excellent luck with other Timex watches and am expecting the same for this one.CONS...The TIMEX HRMs use a different transmit frequency than other HRMs.  I have used two others (Polar and Omron) and they used the same frequency, so I could interchange the strap/transmitter or watch and it would work.  Also, the spin bikes at the gym were set to the same frequency as the Polar HRMs, probably because they are more prevalent. One minor complaint is that the transmitter and the watch take different batteries.  Both are common, but it would be nice if they were the same.  Finally, do not get this HRM if you want something petite. This is a big HRM, but I like it that way.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: This is the 3rd Timex Women's Ironman Watch I've owned. The first one was the smaller version and I found the buttons hard to press when I was swimming laps at the pool. The band broke after about 2-3 years of CONSTANT use and abuse. This one, my third one, has worked beautifully. I have noticed, like other reviewers, that the band gets dirty easily. The white resin band seems to soak up the blue coloring from my jeans and it is a stubborn stain. My other colored resin bands did not have this issue.Still, this is one of my favorite things I own. I know, it's simple, but it's great. It's reliable, easy to use, simple and versatile. I use this watch for timing fitness laps (run/bike/swim), I use it as a kitchen timer, I use it as an alarm clock, oh, and as a watch too. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: I've had my Pebble for week now - and I'm only moderately happy with it.  Pros:  works great with Runkeeper and enables you to read texts and emails plus there are many watchfaces available.  Cons:  difficult to charge - the charging cable barely attaches to the watch, easily scratchable face, short battery life for what it does, cheap-looking and plasticky build, band is sized medium and is cheaply made, and you can't adjust many settings.  Biggest con for me is how easily it scratches - my watchface was scratched in the first few hours of wearing it.  *****************************  Edited to Add  *************************Please take note that the actual Amazon purchases tend to be somewhat less glowing reviews then the other reviews here.  I am not saying that the other reviews are trumped up reviews - but there seems to be a noticeable difference.  This device, in my opinion, is and was simply not ready to go final but the developers pushed it out anyway.  Heck, you can't even check the battery level until the battery level is so low that it needs an immediate charge.  **********************  Added DEC 29 2013  ************************I still use my Pebble - especially with Runkeeper - but I continue to have problems with using the proprietary charging cable.  I think it was just poorly thought out, and wonder if it wasn't an attempt to force people to buy accessories when they lose their charging cable.  A standard micro SD charging port would've been much, much better.***************************  Added JAN 11 2014  ******************************I have had my Pebble now for another 10 days or so and wanted to add some more comments.  I had to raise my rating from 3-star to 4-star because I have learned a lot more about the Pebble in the last 10 days.  It has proven to be very useful and I wear it from the time I get up until the time I go to bed.  One key point to make is - if you are using an Android phone - then I highly recommend, as others have recommended, that you download the Pebble Notifier for the watch.  This will enable you to see at least some of your email text from most of the email clients on your phone.  Oddly enough, perhaps for privacy reasons, the stock Pebble notifier only worked with Gmail on my Android phone.  Notifier also let's you add in things like alarms and many other app choices once it is installed.  If Pebble had simply used a more scratch resistant face, and a better battery charging method, then this would be a five-star product as far as I'm concerned.  And I note with great interest, that the new Pebble Steel will come with a Gorilla Glass face and a new charging connector - imagine that!!  I certainly can't take credit for their design changes - but I have to say that honest reviews here on Amazon are probably at least glanced at by companies producing products.
summary: Some usefulness but too many downsides
