title: Suunto Men's SS014809000 Core Outdoor Matrix Regular Black Watch
description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. reviewText: I own several Casio Watches and this is my second Pathfinder, I own a PAG-80, and this model, so far I'm loving it. The weight as many titanium watch is very light. I read on Casio and some Blogs that the calibration of the sensor is more fast and accurate, but honestly I see no difference with my 80.  If you want to have a good ambient temperature reading you have to remove it from your wrist and set it aside for 10 min, and it will display a reading very close to a classic thermometer (I have done it).  Even though it incorporates more Time Zones than previous models, Casio haven't yet include Venezuelan (CARACAS) time that is -4.30 GMT so for me, World time is useless. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: The Fossil Abacus AU5005 is handy crutch for those of us whom suffer from the digital organizers chain and ball sickness. However, it does not replace a plam pilot completely. The screen size makes it readible for scheduling and todo lists, but I would not recommend it for reading ebooks. The size is still a real plus and its attachment, fashioned after a watch, makes for a convient look. The touch screen with new Jot style writing makes for much more natural wiriting as well as unlimited expandibilty for interfacing. The fact that is a computer sporting the 66mhz Motorola Fireball processor and 8 MB of RAM allows for miniture computing. The watch is more than just another mis-shapen palm pilot, it is a revolation and a major gadget attraction. The few draw backs include small screen size, short battery life (on average two days), still black and white, and lacks wireless fuctionality outside of IrDA. On the plus side, this watch is very stylish, makes for the most convient palm pilot yet, has a built-in rechargable lithium-ion battey, and sports a nifty built-in stylus. Overall I give the Fossil Abacus AU5005 4 out of five stars for convience and portability, leaving it a star shy from perfect for lack of color and wireless connectivity.
summary: Perfect product, However not a complete replacement.

reviewText: Here are my two-cents on durability:  I'm ready to retire my first pair (several small holes and tears) after more than a year of service.  I am a year-round bike commuter (using standard pedals with toe clips) and wear these not only when it is raining/wet, but also when the temp. is below 30f (I live in Chicago, so that's most days in the winter.)  I'm guessing I got about 120-140 one-way, eight-mile trips out of them... and could have gotten more had I not walked around in them so much. The booties are thin enough not to be hot in the summer, and the fact that they are wind-proof helps a surprising amount in keeping the feet warm in the winter.  Like any other piece of cycling gear, I didn't expect them to last forever... but they kept my feet comfortable and dry for about 25 cents per one-way trip.  I think that's pretty reasonable.

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I bought this watch to replace the Suunto vector that I have owned for 14 years.  It had finally started to leak and was no longer operational.  i have always liked Casios although I have never owned a triple sensor.  I paid close to $300 for it and it showed up in great condition and very timely.  Some of the features have left me missing the Suunto brand and I may switch back.  There are too many modes to scroll through to get through them all.  I have a whole sunset sunrise screen and a snooze alarm screen.  Really?  Is this a needed feature?  My Suunto had a light that could be turned on and it would stay on for an extended amount of time and even let you scroll through other screens to say set your alarm for the next day while lying in your sleeping bag after a long day.  The Suunto had a robust plastic body that shed plenty of bumps and drops without losing color.  The Casio seems to have a painted metal bezel that may chip and begin to show a worn look after a few adventures.  Lastly, it is atomic and keeps exact time, so for those of us that like to set the watch ahead to be on time, no such luck.  It tells the time it is told.  I do think hope that the solar feature will keep the battery going strong for a much longer time than the Suunto which was one of its cons.  Maybe the long light time on the Suunto comes with that price.  Bottom line, I still have a few test days left before I have to make a decision whether or not I will keep it.  Thank you Amazon.
title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: 90% of the problems with this watch are from poorly educated product users who don't take the time to understand how it works.  These ARE 90% accurate out of the box and I just ran a half marathon with 96.8% accuracy.  (Watch said 13.52 as apposed to 13.1 miles).  These are NOT 100% accurate, but for 59 dollars they are a steal compared to the $200-$400 dollar gps units from garmin.  These are an excellent value.  They can be recalibrated as many times as you  need.  Treadmills are not accurate so you can not compare to treadmill distance.  You must compare to an actual track.Now for the bad.  My fiance and myself both have the sportbands.  She is now on her 3rd while I'm still on my first.  Together we have logged over 1,000 miles and I don't know if it was a fluke or what.  I have no problems with their durability while my fiance may feel otherwise.  However, on each account she has been able to return the product for a replacement at no cost.The website is a little slow, but has not been so slow as for me to really count it as a con.  They have sent out emails and promotional material saying how they are working on the website to greatly improve it and add features.One thing not mentioned in the reviews is how great the website is.  It keeps track of details of every run you ever ran.  Allows you to challenge friends, play "tag", and join challenges.  It is also very informative for the novice runner.On a side note, I currently run in Saucony shoes, and the little pockets work great when not running in Nike's.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: This watch does it's primarily function as a watch, but do not expect good barometer or thermometer. I do not want to say that they are inaccurate -- they are, but look, are you seriously going to use barometer and thermometer on your hand? The thermometer is very biased by the hand temperature and cannot be accurate by design, unless you put your watch off for a long period of time to know the temperature. The baropmeter on your hand depends on altitude. If you are going to compare pressure at your home and at your workplace -- it is not a good idea, because they are possibly not on the same height and maybe in another place. So, do not think, that you are going to get weather forecast at any location you are at.But, in the other hand, if you measure pressure in the evening and make a second measurement at the morning at the same place -- the readings will be accurate. If you put off the watch in the evening before go to sleep, you can check the morning temperature and decide, are you going to go out of your sleeping bag today, or not. Altimeter is working perfectly also, if you understand how it works.And the watch function is good -- I have less than +0.3 second per day, there is an alarm clock there (very quiet also), world clock and so on like timers or a stopwatch. The additional modes are not realy handy, but, without other options -- why not.Personally, I used this watch for sports and outdoor activity. The resin is resisted agaisnt swet, but also is non-porous, so I need to ajust position of the watch from time to time, my skin become too wet under the strap. Perhaps I need to change it to nylon.And yes, for the price, this watch is awesome.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Before I placed my order I emailed Maxiaids and asked if there was a size chart and was told there wasn't.  The rep suggested that small size is for children and I should order large size for adults.  The two items I ordered arrived promptly.  However they are not the same as what was shown in the pic.  First, in the pic shown on the website, the height of the lenses measuring from top to bottom looks like 1" (1-1/4" at the most), and of rectangular or oblong shape.  The ones I received are 2" in height, and of square shape.  Second, it is too wide to fit behind my two different pairs of glasses and my husband's two different pairs.  Third, the part that was supposed to sit on top of the nose-pads is way too small to even fit.I contacted Maxiaids through Amazon and was instructed to use the return label that was included in the original package to return the items.  When I told Maxiaids that there wasn't a return label, I was then advised to return the items at my own expense.  When I asked if I would be reimbursed the total amount of my order plus the return postage, I was told that "upon examining your (my) returned merchandise, if we (Maxiaids) find that it is materially different than the item as advertised, you (I) will  be refunded for the postage costs".  I was also told in an earlier email that "your (my returned) item must be in brand-new and resellable condition".Should Maxiaids have not known exactly what was shipped when the order was filled, without having to examine the returned items?  Does that mean there are different versions?  Since a return label was never included in the original package, my assumption is that Maxiaids has no intention of paying for any return postage at all.  I also needed to open one package to try it on so the one returned item could be deemed not "brand new" and not in "resellable condition".It's not worth my time to go through the trouble of going to the post office and paying for postage to return the items because I may very likely end up getting  no refund at all.  My past purchases from Amazon included small ticket items (e.g. audio Y cable splitter from Technology Galaxy - excellent customer service for returning/exchanging a $2.90 item) and not too small items (e.g. MacBook Pro) and I was most happy with its service and products. description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. Also features a digital thermometer. Menu-based user interface in English, German, French and Spanish. 2 year warranty.

title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

title: The Astrolabe Watch - Navigator's Dream Watch
description:
Two time zones, a 24-hour time indicator, date, current time and Astrolabe!

The Astrolabe was developed at Greek school in Alexandria about 160 B.C. by Hipparchus. Great scientific strides forward at that time were the result of combining the Greek sciences with Babylonian mathematics. This was made possible by the conquests of Alexander the Great who established a vast empire throughout the Mediterranean. From that point in history, the Astrolabe was known to scholars and was used as a slide rule of the Heavens.

Direction, time, angles, and the position of the celestial bodies could all be calculated. When Prince Henry the Navigator established his seafaring fleet, he began using the Astrolabe to navigate the ships. For many years this gave the Portuguese the exclusive ability to navigate open waters, which the other countries could not do. When Sir Francis Drake raided ports along the South American coast he was forced to flee from the Spanish ships. Drake attached a Portuguese ship and took its navigator hostage to guide him on his round the world voyage, thus avoiding the Spanish Fleet.

All the great voyagers in the age of exploration navigated with the Astrolabe, including Columbus, Magellan, and Drake. About 1391 Chaucer wrote his Treatise on the Astrolabe for his son. 

The primary use of the mariner's Astrolabe was to find the latitude of a ship at sea. In use, the Astrolabe a mariner would use is suspended (above eye level) and the altitude of the sun or a star above the horizon is measured using a rotating disc. The measurement is taken when the sun or star is at its maximum altitude. The star's declination of the sun's declination for the day can be found from an almanac. The latitude is then found by solving the equation latitude=(90 degrees - measured altitude)+declination. The term (90 degrees - altitude) is called the zenith distance.

Astrolabe is not a very accurate navigational instrument and errors of several degrees in latitude were common.

description: The Trinity Knot is the simplest of the Celtic knots. The Celts were very familiar with the idea of the trinity. There were many things in their culture that came in threes; the three stages of womanhood (maid, mother, crone) and the three elements (earth, fire, water) are two good examples of this. reviewText: I purchased my Pebble in Dec. 2013 for $99 on sale on Amazon. Six months ago, the Pebble was in its infancy and not quite ready for prime time. Pebble has come a long way since then. They added a locker feature so you can park apps that don't fit in the 8 available slots. They made it easy to configure settings for the watch faces and  Pebble watch apps. This requires the watch to be shut down and restarted. Test messages from the app still work but for some reason the real ones stop flowing. Have to restart 2X times a week usually.2. Decreased battery life after ver. 2.XX of the firmware. I need to recharge the watch every 2 days now.3. Started getting "your watch is not configured for messages" errors in the app out of the blue. Watch was was paired with BT and BT-LE. Nothing would make that message go away so I had to do a factory reset.4. Current version of the iOS app leaves geo-fencing on all the time.5. reviewText: A tough review to write because i really have mixed feelings about this watch.I love the look and design, and all of the features work as advertised.I also own a SUUNTO Ambi2 that I use primarily for trail running and often as my everyday watch. So I'm familiar with the concept, quality, quirks and features of SUUNTO watches.The watch's band/strap material is very comfortable but only for about an hour at a time.  After that it becomes very clammy and sticky, and I am constantly twisting the watch around to scratch my skin below.My only other issue is the glare on the display. This does not exist on the Ambit2, which is highly visible under practically any lighting conditions. The Core Crush on the other hand becomes very difficult to read with the slightest amount of light, and you will spend a bit of time finding an angle that lets you read the display.The watch functions perfectly and I have no concerns about durability.  I'd hate to swap out the band because the color really gives it a lot of personality. But the reality is my wife has probably inherited a watch that I will use less and less over time.
title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I like this watch a lot. It has its flaws, but for the price, its pretty great. Originally I used my phone to track distances with one of the many available apps, but I don't like carrying my phone around and it also drains my battery pretty badly. This is a pretty great option for those of us who don't want to spend 150+ for a GPS watch.The good parts:It tracks mileage pretty accurately AFTER calibration. I ran 2.5 miles on a track the first night I had this watch to calibrate it. The initial reading (before going in to calibrate) had me at 2.93 miles. Clearly it was pretty far off. However, the next weekend I ran an organized 5k race and wore the watch. It tracked me at 3.13 miles, which is probably pretty spot on when you figure in a little bit weaving on the race course.Its cheap. Like I said, if you want a GPS enabled watch, you'll be spending AT LEAST 150 bucks, probably far more if you go for one of the more advanced Garmin models. They're great watches, I'm just not a place where I can afford that.The Nike+ website is awesome. All of your data is easily imported to the Nike+ site and you can see your entire run in detail. Its awesome, I get detailed feedback and it keeps a history of my runs for no extra charge.The bad:There's no backlight. I assume this was done to converse battery life (which I can't attest to due to not running more than 5 or so miles with it), but it sucks for night runners. If you don't run in a relatively well lit area, you'll be doing a fair amount of squinting.The face orientation is kind of awkward. The watch is very slim, which looks nice, but also puts the face at a perpendicular angle to the average person. It makes it much harder to see what your current distance or time is while running. You can't just do a quick glance.All in all, I think its worth the price. However, if you want to spend more, there are better options out there.
summary: For the price, its really hard to beat.

reviewText: The description on Amazon is very sparse and does not (as of this writing) explain the sizing method of this item.  The item boasts a removable insole and a somewhat stretchable heel loop.  By including the insole, you can reduce 1/2 size, or by stretching the heel strap, you can increase the size.  Thus it is supposed to be adjustable.Sounds great.  Problem is, the insole (if you need it, like I do, in order to get the fit right) immediately starts slipping out of the back of the shoe with every step you take. Notice that there is just open space at the lowest part of the heel, and that's where the insole starts to protrude -- by several inches after taking 30 or 40 steps.So I have the following choices: (a) constantly shove the insoles back in or (b) remove them permanently and tolerate a looser fit or (c) glue the insoles in permanentlyNonetheless for the price, the comfort, and being able to take out the trash in the rain, etc. you can't complain.  But you have to get lucky on the fit, as the adjustable feature really just doesn't work.I am updating this review after a few months with a somewhat higher rating.  Despite them being a loose fit, because the price is so low and because it is a unique product, I decided to keep them.  It is a great convenience being able to slip them on without stooping over, and still have it not flop like a flip-flop sandal.  I only wish the maker would bite the bullet and start producing half-sizes, so that all of us can have the size we were meant to have.
summary: Great features for the dollar, but alleged size adjustment not as simple as they make it sound

reviewText: As a teacher, I wanted a digital watch because I like to know exactly how much time I have left before the bell rings.  I chose this one because I also wanted an ALL black watch that looked stylish in a mannish way.  I've had this watch for a few months now, I think, and here are my thoughts:1. I know it has a lot of functions, but the only ones I really care about are the time, the date, and the light.  As others have said, the light could be brighter, but that doesn't bother me that much.  I only use the watch at school in the day time.  It keeps good time, and I love knowing exactly how many SECONDS I have left to each class. All the other many functions are actually kind of annoying.  There being four buttons on the sides, sometimes random buttons get pressed and go to some other function like the stop watch, and I have to fumble around with the buttons to get the watch to show the time again.  So if you want a simple watch, this might not be for you.  If you want extra functions like the stop watch and an alarm (I think, because now at 11PM every night, the watch beeps for like 10 seconds), then you will like this watch!2. It IS quite bulky.  I am petite (5'1) with arms that are pretty proportionate to my height, and I think the watch LOOKS good, but it actually hurts the bone that sticks out at the wrist (don't know what that bone's called).  Plus, when I wear certain long-sleeved jackets that are kind of tight or has buttons at the wrist, I can't pull the sleeve over the watch because it's so big.  Can get a little annoying.Overall, I still like this watch.  It does look really good, and it does the job.  But if I could have the same look with less functions and maybe just a tiny bit smaller in size, it would be perfect.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I owned a pair of Shape-Ups and was considering buying another pair to match more of my workout clothes when I came across these. It turns out this brand and its concept predates Shape-Ups considerably, and I believe they are better shoes, too.This works well as a toning shoe, as does the similar Skechers Shape-Up. However, MBT shoes were not created to give people more of a workout as they do their everyday walking around; they were created for comfort and for less stress on key joints.My primary interest in these shoes was that they were comparable to Shape-Ups but were a better brand, but I have to say I have really come to respect this brand, its mission, and its products. Unlike Shape-Ups, MBT makes shoes for a variety of occasions, even work and dress shoes, to serve those who really need the joint relief this style of shoe provides. I don't have joint pain, but I do have muscle pain in my back and a once-shattered tailbone that is still not perfectly healed. Standing - not just walking - in these shoes forced me to engage my core rather than slump back onto my hips and spine. While that itself wore on me after awhile, I did notice improved posture and less pressure on my lower back and tailbone.I have to say that I haven't worn these in quite awhile, as I began to have fewer and fewer opportunities to wear sneakers or casual dress of any kind. The relief for me personally was not so great that I sought out times to switch to these shoes, and while dress shoes are made by MBT, my need was not great enough for me to invest in a wardrobe full of these. However, that is not the fault of the product and thus I give it a 5-star rating for quality of brand, selection of styles, and effectiveness of the product.Price would be a sticking point. These are expensive. To that I say, if you need them, you need them and they're worth it. If you're looking into the toning shoe fad and aren't sure how you feel about it, pick up a $65 pair of Skechers Shape-Ups and then upgrade if you really love the concept.UPDATE: I've been wearing my MBTs for about four days now, and today I had to wear heels all day, then I slipped on boat shoes when I got home. Lying down for a little bit, my spine felt like it had been hammered on both ends. My back muscles felt cramped and my tailbone felt like it had been smacked with a frying pan. I'm going to have to say that yeah, these are extremely comfortable and they must do wonders for your posture.
summary: Do your spine and joints a favor! (Better than Shape-Ups!)

The ends tightly grip your glasses frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.Details12 inches long (each side), with 3.2-millimeter thicknessUV-resistant, molded MIDDI ends fit medium framesTough woven climbing rope with adjustable black bead91% nylon, 6% rubber, and 2% plasticNo contact above earbowWashableMade in the USAAbout CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

reviewText: I'm using it with a jailbroken iphone5.Some apps I have on it are smartwatch+ (jailbroken version)pebbleauthspoonPackagesswimioand a busapp for my campus shuttle serviceNotifications work great on an iphone as long as what you want on your watch is the same as what you want to see on your phone's notification centre. Otherwise it might be a little too much buzzing for your liking for example if you want a notification to show up without any buzzing like some whatsapp group notifications you're out of luck.The apps mostly work great and allows me to generate one time authentication codes for services supported by google's authenticator app, check into foursquare with spoon. Smartwatch+ allows me to see if I've got mail or texts and control my music all without having to remove my phone from my pocket.The coolest app would be swimio which allows me to track my laps in the pool. As an avid swimmer it is a great app if it actually makes it out of beta. Now it is still a little finicky and doesn't track my laps without any errors yet.As my phone is jailbroken it allows me to have notifications muted on the watch if I'm using the phone or removes the need for any passcode if my watch is within range of my phone which I think is a great feature.I get lots of notifications everyday and with all that buzzing it still manages to last 4 days on average before charging is requiredUltimately if you're willing to spend some time setting up your watch and are using an android or jailbroken iphone I would highly recommend this to you. It may not be super revolutionary yet but I think for less than $150 the amount of utility it provides is worth the price. If you're on an unjailbroken iphone you might get reduced utility but I would say that it is still a good buy. It is definitely the ecosystem to beat for smartwatches out there at this point of time.The only thing I feel is poor about this watch is the material of the face. It is highly prone to scratches as such being plastic. Hence I would highly recommending putting on some protection the moment you wear it.

reviewText: It is a great quality shoe, but it runs half a size small so size up from you normal size.
title: DMT Prisma 2 Shoe - Men's
description: The DMT Prisma 2 comes in two different sole styles. One has four-hole mounting for Speedplay cleats; the version we have here has a three-hole mounting for Look-style cleats. This is undoubtedly the more popular style, as even Speedplay users can utilize this mounting pattern with an adapter plate.The Prisma uses a dial system to hold the foot in the shoe. There's a lot to love in the dial. One adjustment per shoe is easy and fast. Also, with one adjustment, the entire upper is tightened equally at the same time; better for evenly distributing pressure. Turn the rotor clockwise, it tightens. Turn it counter-clockwise by 45-degrees, and the cable releases. There are three sectors that the cable wraps around: the upper, middle, and lower foot.DMT wraps your feet in other ways as well. The upper is made from what's called a 'slip last' meaning the upper is effectively constructed from one piece of mesh and wrapped around the last before being secured below the board. There are no seams to rub against your foot, and it allows the upper to conform very easily. Both mean greater comfort. There's microfiber on top of the mesh in places to reduce stretch to zero, but even with the microfiber on top of the mesh, the shoe breathes very well. At the back of the shoe, the external heel cup is deep and soft and holds your heel securely. The tongue is made of microfiber and is padded to better disperse any pressure that might come from the cable lace.They have also upgraded the insole this year to their heat-moldable ASL model. It looks like the standard foam insole on top, but when you take it out of the shoe and flip it over, you can see that there is rigid EVA foam in the plantar and heel areas of the foot. It's designed so that when you heat the insole up in the oven, place it in your shoe, stand in the shoe and tighten the upper, the insole will mold around your foot.

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I ordered my pebble via Kickstarter in July 2012 and got it more than one year (!) later. While the watch now is also available via Amazon.com, unfortunatelly enough, it doesn't seem to ship to Europe.The watch itself is a nice, understated piece of elegant technology. It's one of these things that makes life a little easier. Someone calls? You'll get his/her name on the display and a non-intrusive vibration to go with it. You get a short message? Read it on the little display if you want. Bored with your watch face? Get a new one.But there are still a couple of things to be ironed out. My biggest grief is the battery. Yes, the battery load lasts for about a week, also due to the low power consumption design, which is great for a Smartwatch. But the battery cannot be changed. So in two or three years, I have to throw away the watch and have to hope that there will be a replacement which I still like. This is a major bummer and kind of a "rent a watch for a couple of years" concept instead of "buy a watch and be happy".Second bummer might be the SDK 2.0. Yes, great features and all. But of all the hundreds of watchfaces, you will apparently be only able to use the ones that get adapted for SDK 2.0 as it is not backwards compatible. So if you see nice watchfaces for Pebble that are not very recent, you might be out of luck using them on your updated Pebble.All in all, from a functional point, I'm quite happy with my Pebble and hope that there will be a model that looks very much the same soon that will provide a changeable battery, maybe even with a standard Micro USB port for charging as the charging cable is proprietary and doesn't stick well to the watch. And maybe there could be a "Gorilla Glass" update or something as well which is less prone to scratching.
summary: A nice, understated piece of elegant technology

reviewText: Ordered the black Pebble in early Dec 13'. Order arrived within the prescribed time frame promised. It came packaged in a padded envelope and neatly boxed.Construction: Light weight plastic with some metal (buckle and side charging pins). The screen is scratch resistant (according to the website literature). The screen is ~1-inch (corner to corner). The larger button on left above the charging pins is a 'back-button'. There are three buttons not shown on the right. Think of them as scroll up (top), select (middle button), and scroll down (bottom). The band is made of rubber and is very comfortable. Over all the watch is very light weight...I caught myself looking to make sure it was still on it is so light. The watch charges over a standard USB port. There is no literature on the specific type of AC charger to use, so i'd caution anyone in using this method to charge the watch as it may not match the charging requirements of the watch itself.Software/Sync: I own an iPhone 4S with iOS7. The watch came with firmware 1.2 (? not sure if i'm using the correct terms-- firmware or software-not an IT guy!). I down loaded the free pebble app to my iPhone, once connected, it automatically walked me through the update process from 1.2 to 1.3., actually it was pretty seamless and a hands off process. Bluetooth established a handshake with my iPhone in seconds. I then selected the option to send test text and test call. both worked and the watch vibrated almost immediately. Packaged in the box were two short pamphlets, one with basic instructions and the other was all the FCC requirement information.Pebble can only receive data, save one, the music selection, which can start, stop and play music on your mobile device. Otherwise you can't text, email, or call from the watch. Think of it as an 'extension' "to" your phone as a remote control and as a notification system--albeit a limited extension as it can't manipulate apps on your phone--it can only use streams of data from it, e.g. GPS-data.  The phone must be in proximity to the Pebble (Bluetooth range varies) in order to function as a 'smart watch', otherwise it's only good as a watch...it tells time and date. There is tremendous potential here but that's a discussion beyond the scope of this review.Issues I encountered. First, there are other Pebble utilities (e.g. Smartwatch +, SmartWatch Pro, etc.)  that allow you access to weather features, maps, etc. But these are pay-utilities. In other word to really start enjoying the potential of this watch, you need to add these 'foundational utilities' in order to obtain the apps that make the watch more enjoyable to use as a tool. That said, some utilities/apps are pay and some are free, some are OEM type apps (approved for use on Pebble-tested), others are not (not tested or guaranteed). My opinion is that the smart watch needs to come with those baseline utilities/apps or at least make them available through the website. If its a third party vendor app, then sure, you may have to pay for those apps/services--I embrace capitalism, but in the most basic sense, the watch should come with baseline functional apps that showcase its potential. It just makes business sense.I personally ran into issues after the upgrade. My Pebble was constantly looking for a Bluetooth connection and when established, it was constantly in an "updating" mode for weather and GPS for when I ran (didn't work the only time I used it on an outdoor run which lasted for 47 mins), and lastly it never was able to correctly sync may battery status for my phone. So for example, if my phone was 100% charged, the Pebble would show 75% charged.Assuming you don't have a Samsung which has its own watch and assuming Apple doesn't come out with its own line of smart watches, Pebble can only improve in my opinion. It has a lot of potential, but it first needs to work out the basic bugs.5 starts for it potential, 3 stars however for its functionality vis-a-vis the need to purchase additional apps, and its glitchy-ness.
summary: To Pebble or Not to Pebble....Potential

description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I was wary when purchasing this watch because I don't have the smallest wrists and I often find watches very uncomfortable.  The softness of the band is very comfortable and the watch looks much more expensive than it was.  I prefer an analog face versus a digital face because even though I need the military time for nursing, I often have trouble converting back for when I'm with non-nursing folks.  The face is very easy to read even though it's purple and the minute dots along the outside are helpful in being very precise.  Another reviewer mentioned that the screws in the back are not flush with the watch, which is true, but if you wear the watch at a comfortable length (i.e., not cutting off your circulation) there shouldn't be any issues with the screws.  I can't feel them.  The only problem I had the first day was when I hyperextended my wrist the side dug into my hand, but then I just loosened the band a notch and everything is fine.  Washing hands is a breeze and no worries since it's water resistant.  I'm considering buying more colors since they're so cheap.  Will definitely buy again when this one meets its end.

reviewText: A few months ago, I bought the Heritage Extreme Winter Gloves and was very disappointed in them. They were stiff, took a while before they warmed my hands up, and they were too bulky. Last month, I discovered these DuPont ComforMax gloves, and fell in love instantly. These are without a doubt the best winter gloves I've ever worn. They're extremely soft, durable and warmed my hands up within minutes, keeping them toasty the whole time I kept them on. I don't care if these are made for skiing or anything else- if you need gloves for the winter months, these what you need!According to the tag, ComforMax Classic gloves have 4-5 times more fiberfill layers than other insulation. Each layer is just 5-10g/sqm. Seriously, it feels like you're wearing a blanket on your hands when you feel the inside of these things. I've let a few other people try them on and some of them gasped, remarking how soft they are. It might sound dumb to be praising gloves so much, I know. But these things are just too good! The leather exterior is smooth as heck and moving your fingers around is simple. With the Heritage gloves, I felt like my hand was doing more work than it should just to do simple things like reaching in my pocket. Here, I can pick things up easily and even zip up my jacket. For gloves this big, that's impressive. The outside of each glove is very well-padded too. I tried punching a hard wall with them on and it felt just like my old sparring gloves by Everlast. Trust me, your hands are safe with these puppies on.So they're super warm, super soft and flexible...so how come I'm not giving them a full 5 stars? Well, I was actually on the fence with this, and if Amazon let you give half stars, I'd totally give these 4.5 out of 5. There are two small things keeping them back from a perfect score for me. One being the high price and the other being something that's kind of my 'fault'. First, you get what you pay for with these, though I wish Amazon was selling them for a bit less like they do with most other things. When I found these in a store last month, they were 2/3 what they cost here. Chalk that up as another missed opportunity in my life. As for the thing that's my fault, it's the fact that I have, as others have put it, 'piano player hands'. My fingers are thin, and even with the small size of gloves, there's a tiny bit of room inside. I don't know if this is a result of that or not, but there's also some excess fabric around the tips that makes it hard to pick up small things. If you have regular hands though, this should be a problem, and neither of these should prevent you from buying these.I can't say enough about the ComforMax Classics- they're amazing! I can't wait to give them a shot this winter if it snows.
summary: Nearly flawless gloves for cold days.

reviewText: I have had this watch for about 10 years now and was just checking around to see if it is still made, and to my surprise it still is, which is good.  I have worn this watch to work almost everyday on from when I got to about 2006.  I stopped wearing it because my cell phone has a clock and was using that.  My wife took over the watch and started wearing it to work.  Her job involved putting her hands in water and chicken fat daily throughout the day.  I thought well that's it for my Swiss Army watch.  Needless to say about 6 months ago I took on a job where I needed a wrist watch.  I found my old watch, the leather band I had put on it was destroyed and the watch was not working.  I brought to my local watch guy and told him to replace the battery.  At first with the new battery nothing happened, watch didn't work.  I told him, the contacts are probably dirty, the watch has been through hell. He took the battery out cleaned the contacts and put the battery back in. Voila, the watch is keeping perfect time!  While I was there I purchased a new band and he cleaned the watch up for me with whatever they use.  With the new band and the cleanup, the watch looks brand new again.  He only charged for the battery, $5, and a new black leather band, $18.  You cannot kill this watch. If this one every really broke, I would not hesitate to buy another in a heartbeat.

title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: I bought two of these in March of 2011. They both still work, and they are the only two watches I have ever used during this time as a soccer referee. One of the two watch backlights no longer functions, which is odd, because I never actually used the backlights to begin with!The watch (in stopwatch/timer mode) has three lines: the bottom line is the current time of day (which can be set to 12 or 24 hour clock), middle row is the time remaining in the period of play (it counts down, then begins counting up when it hits 00:00:00), top row is an extra timer that counts up (for the purpose of measuring the amount of stoppage time you might wish to add).The only thing i don't like about this watch (and something i would definitely toss these in the trash over, if i could find a watch that remedies this issue), is that, to set the timer, you can only scroll UP through the digits. In other words, if you are reffing back-to-back games, and need to change the watch from 35 minutes down to 30 minutes, you have to press the button 95 times, and watch as the watch scrolls up from 35 to 99, then back to 00, then finally up to 30. Sometimes I just hold the button and start paying attention to something else (who wants to stare at a timer going from 35 to 99?), and accidentally miss the time i was aiming for, meaning i have to scroll through all the numbers again!Please, oh please, tell me there is a decent soccer watch out there that lets you scroll DOWN to the appropriate time?!
summary: Does the job - Wish it would scroll DOWN when setting the stopwatch

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: Before I get to the good stuff, let me first bring up the bad. When I first got this watch, I was initially underwhelmed by it. I encountered pairing issues with my phone. I could not figure out how to install faces and apps. Once I did, I found that some apps caused the watch to lock up and require system recovery. The battery, while extremely good, does not have a "low charge" warning (instead, it has an icon that appears in the menu about 12 hours before it dies).That being said, The pairing issues went away with the last update, and my android phone started actually directing my scanned qr links to the pebble app when applicable. The apps that cause the Pebble to crash are few and far between, and the recovery process is very quick and painless, with no data loss. The screen is very tough, and has no marks or scratches after a month of running it into things. The water resistance is also worth noting, as I have showered with it every day since I got it, and it has been doing fine. I now get emails, texts, and call notifications, complete with vibration, on my wrist, meaning that I can leave my phone constantly on silent without missing anything. Most of the faces and apps are great, and I can change things instantly when I want a different look or feel. I can keep score, follow to-do lists, and if it comes down to it, use the back-light to light my path to the restroom in the middle of the night.Other android apps have also been enhancing my experience. Coffer lets me manage my pebble faces and apps so I can swap out even when my watch is full. HTTPebble gives me wrist access to information such as tides, exchange rates, moon phases, sunrize and sunset times, weather forecasts, and seconds since the Unix epoch. Apps like Glance display my phone's battery and current stock/mutual fund values, while bringing other information together onto one screen.Pebble has some small hurdles, but they are all fixable. I have yet to find a better watch, anywhere, and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone willing to learn how to use it.
