description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. reviewText: This is probably my fifth or sixth version of this watch. They have lasted from two years to about four or five years and are generally quite reliable.I wouldn't have needed a new one except when I removed the last battery, I couldn't get the buttons to work when I put the thing together!Each time I buy this watch, it tends to get a bit better. The exception is that the previous version had small buttons that looked like they would fail (they did) and required you to push fairly hard (they were undersized).Anyway, this version has nice improvements. The buttons are bigger (too big, IMHO) and easier to push. I haven't had any issues with them being overly sensitive as other reviewers have. I wear the watch on my left wrist a little below my actual wrist. The buttons that could prove troublesome are on the left edge of the watch and wouldn't be an issue unless you wore it on your right wrist (and had big hands). I have had to adjust to light pressure on the buttons, though.The alarm is louder than the last version and the indigo light works on the numbers rather than illuminating the entire screen. I have only used the alarm and chronograph (with split times) and both work just fine. I took previous versions diving (they are not diving watches) and they survived. No reason to believe this version would be different.All in all, I am quite pleased with this version!

reviewText: I love this watch. Bought the first one in the early oughts because I needed a sturdy hiking watch. Fell in love with the multiple options for alarms (3), dual time settings (awesome for traveling) timer/chrono function, indiglo option = it was da bomb. When the battery died four years later, I immediately replaced it with the same brand and the love affair continued.Watch no. 2 died just a few weeks ago and I was lost without it. Thought I didn't need to bother now because well, that's what phones are for, right?Well, now I'm trying to get into swimming more and I need a timer. Lots easier to have a waterproof watch around than a delicate phone so I broke down and ordered watch No. 3. Plus, it's so nice to have a basic watch for when I travel that I don't have to take off at security. This is an awesome watch.That being said, an earlier poster was correct. The face is delicate and scratches easily and once the battery goes, it's just cheaper to buy a new one (although I'd really prefer buying a new battery just to avoid waste). And yes, the strap can weaken when you dunk it in water enough so I'd recommend you don't swim with it. Otherwise, you'll have a working unit but a destroyed strap that can't be replaced easily.But overall, love, love, love this watch. Timex, thank you for getting something right and keeping it right.

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I ride a hayabusa, so when I ride it is either with a full-face helmet, or with no helmet, I do not own a half helmet for my bike. I also wear contacts, so regular sunglasses weren't working as any time I went over 25 or 30mph my eyes would start watering really bad, which would either eventually dry my contacts out. Also, with regular sunglasses they aren't impact resistant and if you turn your head to the side, the wind could take them off your face. I also have a smaller than average head, so it is difficult for me to find sunglasses that don't make me look "like a bug/too big" for lack of a better description. These glasses were not only inexpensive, fit my head very well, and had a snug hold around my head (so they are less likely to fly off), but they also performed just as advertised! I was very pleased with this purchase. I also bought the Photochromic pair, but they didn't darken enough for my liking. So I'm either going to buy another pair of the Smoke lens, or maybe the blue lens to match my busa. The little foam pads between the glasses and your face keep the wind out somehow (I'm not an engineer, so I don't know exactly how) but it works very well. I went 60 mph with no problem regarding the wind bothering my eyes. Don't misunderstand, it doesn't stop all airflow, it isn't airtight. It simply diverts the airflow somehow so that it doesn't blow right on your eyeballs, really cool design if you ask me. I went up to 80mph and started noticing the air hitting my eyes. Above 100 mph they were useless. BUT in all fairness I go out to ride with different intentions. If I'm jumping on the busa to tear it up, then I put my helmet on. If I'm going out to enjoy a nice leisurely ride to enjoy the weather or to the store or to a friends place, not intending on riding fast at all then these fit the bill perfectly! 5 stars from me anyway and I will buy another pair in case these happen to break or I lose them, I will want another pair :).

reviewText: The Pebble is absolutely brilliant. It becomes increasingly more powerful with every software update. While its limited memory does limit the number of watchfaces and apps you can have installed on it to a fairly small number, it's been amazing watching what developers have been doing with it (it even plays Tetris).For me, it's been insanely helpful. Most of my pants have very deep pockets and often times I miss my phone buzzing. Thanks to the Pebble, not any more. I push every notification from my iPhone to my Pebble, which while it can mean my wrist vibrating non-stop on some occasions from all the notifications I get, I'd much rather have notification overload - especially important notifications from my computer's remote monitoring - than missed notifications.I also love that the Pebble is highly customizable: tired of a watchface? Swap it out. Tired of the wrist strap? Swap it out. Tired of the border around the screen? Slap a new face over it. The Pebble never gets stale.Battery life is also very impressive. While it's advertised at lasting about a week, I've consistently gotten two weeks out of mine with an average of 30 notifications a day plus displaying the weather (which drains the battery on my iPhone faster than the battery on my Pebble). The only downside I can think of is the proprietary charging cable, but given that I just keep it in my laptop bag, I haven't run into any issues with not having it when I needed it.Bottom line, I love my Pebble. I wouldn't trade it for an iWatch nor Google Glass. The only issue I've ever had with it was a stuck update, which I quickly got help fixing on Twitter. The Pebble is solid proof that crowdfunded technology works, and in this case, extremely well.

reviewText: Only My 2ND Casio & MAGIC. Had to say it twice. At my age I am an analog guy, always wondered why people ever even wanted anything digital. I mean, Analog gives such a better actual "picture" of time. But then I got old, got crippled, got so I was always around my iPad for reminders, alarms etc just to remember when to take meds etc. Yeah, don't get old.The folks who use these on a regular basis can tell you ALL about how they work, but how important it is to first take the time to SET THEM UP CORRECTLY for YOUR specific region of the world. Well I never read direction in 65 years. But I do watch YouTube videos. Trouble is, nobody has one explaining how to set this particular module up that I could find. Luckily, there were tons of videos last week that taught me how to set up my somewhat similar GShock G7900A Rescue Concept Watch. Being a former surfer who surfed all over the world, oh how I WISH I had these watches before I got crippled. But life & War happen....I wanted an Atomic watch since they were invented. Why? No reason, I am just a gadget junkie and HAVE to have everything. Well if you are like me, THIS is your watch! It did take me over an hour to figure it out. I went to bed depressed since I was unable to do any manual set using the Colorado Atomic Clock. I got the L1 signal (the weakest but at least showing me it was seeing SOMETHING. But then after a few minutes got the dreaded ERR error message. I have bought weather stations before that just never got their signal so NEW it would never work. Had all my alarms set, tides and barometer set, moon set etc. But to be honest, the part of my gadget junkie was just seriously let down when I went to bed. Yes, I read all the reviews on watch forums as well as at Amazon about put them in a window and at midnight that magic Atomic Clock Fairy would make everything all work. Yeah right....Or so I thought. Got up at 5 AM this morning and ran for my watch. OK, crawled to my watch. Sure enough, the trick of placing my watch face down and aiming my big honkin sensor towards Denver worked. I was honestly like a teenage kid again. Dumb as it may be, I am just beside myself that I have every single feature on this watch working within 10% of anything my GPS and weather station confirms in ALL categories. I'll be honest, unlike anyone else I read who wrote any review, I really didn't care much if ANY of it was accurate except that stupid Atomic Clock. I just wanted another toy to constantly play with. I am beyond excited it to discover that mine at least is a surprisingly useful tool as well as being a new toy.This watch arrived direct from Amazon with a charge showing at medium battery level. I played with it for a couple hours last night and all morning inside. I then took a 1 hour cruise in 82 degree bright sunshine on my electric mobility scooter. I got home and it now reads FULL. All my alarms for medications worked, all my features worked, and I could not be happier. I was shocked to find this cheaper and DIRECT form Amazon, and not from one of their third party sellers a the next to cheapest price. I bought it for about a dollar more than that third party seller since THAT gives me the full and REAL factory 1 year warranty. Plus I used my American Express Card to pay so if it dies in TWO years, THEY will pay me in full for a new watch. Been there done that twice now with home surround theater systems whose HDMI pass through's failed on me. Saved me a couple thousand bucks now on free extended warranties.The green tinted face on this does make it somewhat harder for my eyes to see. I regret that and knew/expected that ahead of time over the cheaper black version.with a white face. But I wanted the military green with camo band more than anything. My years in the USMC and all the fun I had getting myself crippled for life and all, well, I just didn't want all that fun to stop:-) Honestly, the way they set this watch up is wonderful! (to ME). The band is very dark and the camo very mild & understated. In other words, you don't look like some kind of deranged GI Joe wanna be out waiting for a flashback...This watch is just a very dark, muted and VERY nice looking, expensive and professional looking watch. It looks like exactly what it is. A tool, a tool that you can use in a pinch to do a lot of various things to help you. And if it didn't do a DARN thing, I would still love it since it just looks so darn cool. Maybe I just got lucky? Mine shows Made In Japan, NOT China. Don't know, don't care. If you are worried this looks too military, it does NOT. It still pulls off looking like a piece of professional equipment (again, to ME). The trade off for the muted green over the black, or other color choices, will be the fact that the face sort of washes out the colors. Yet, it also ADDS some color in doing so. In other words, it is a trade off. I still have mixed feelings on that. I somehow think it would look strange if it had the white face of the standard watch? And it is a very light, almost shaded green that you see. However I end up feeling about it, I wouldn't trade it for the world. And now, I can even play with this thing and see what the time & tides are all over that world I used to go surfing in. I don't think you can go wrong with this watch. In ANY color you choose.  The last point I would make is the size of the face. One reviewer here thinks it is too small. NO IDEA WHAT HE WAS COMPARING IT TOO? Maybe a girls watch?  All I can say is mine is actually BIGGER than on my Casio GShock G7900A Rescue Concept Watch. And that is significant since this watch is actually physically smaller than it! I have a smaller wrist than most so that is another huge selling point about this watch. It is thinner and has a smaller diameter than my bright red GSHOCK model. And there is something else. Pick a screen, ANY screen. I have lived 65 years somehow, yet never found any watch that shows CLOSE to as much information on  EVERY screen as this watch. It is simply stunning, just how much info they managed to cram into this double screen set up they created building this computer on your wrist. Also being former Law Enforcement, I will have my eye out for the Dick Tracy Model I expect any day now:-)UPDATE July 4 2014:  I found that I don't even need to place this watch near any window to sync with the Atomic Clock. Last night it did it's thing at 1:04 AM Pacific Standard Time-using daylight savings time. The prior night with it in the window, facing upside down it did it at 12:03 AM PST. So it looks like for me, here in Oceanside California (USMC Camp Pendleton Marine Corps Back Gate Area), this watch has no issues with the Auto Sync Function for me at least.

I calibrated mine to give readings while I am wearing it.I don't care what the readings are while it is off my arm,I have other things for that.With a little time and patience you can achieve pretty darn good,consistant readings. The alarm tones are loud enough to wake me. The lighting is good, it's not backlit like my G shocks, but it is sufficent. The buttons have a nice feel to them, the screen is large and easy to read.One thing I would like to see improved is whether all the alarms are on. Currently it only tells if an alarm is on, it doesn't matter if they all are on or only one is you just get an alarm on icon. Otherwise this a fine watch that i would reccomend to anyone!

reviewText: My wife saw a woman wearing a hat similar to this one night and thought it was cute. After looking online it seems the name brand version sells for over $100. Due to the nature of "Fads" I just couldn't see spending lots of money on something that most likely will be out of fashion in a year (if not already). This is obviously a knock-off and I certainly didn't expect to get a top quality product for under $20 but truthfully, this really isn't bad at all.What your getting is a decently made inexpensive version of what you could buy for well over $100 by going brand name. Visually it doesn't look obviously cheap and unless your comparing it side by side with the original, or have friends that are fashion snobs most people will be oblivious that its not the real thing. Honestly, I thought the real things were "Cheap" and was kind of shocked at how much they sell for.Appearance:The colors are accurate to the picture. The lining is black and the paw prints are in the correct places. The ears don't always stand up perfect but are even in height and in the right places. It looks like what it is supposed to look like, which is a cute, spirit hood hat thingy.Quality:Seems to be decently made. Although inexpensive it doesn't feel terribly cheap or fragile. That being said, I wouldn't think it would last a lifetime either. If I were getting this for a young girl and she wore it every day of winter I would think she would get at least 1 season out of it before needing repairs. Treated with care would probably last a couple years.Use:Ok, based on some reviews for this product let me make this clear. The main purpose for this hat is to look cute. The secondary purpose is to add a little warmth from the elements when its cold outside. The hat absolutely satisfies the cute factor without a doubt. Because of the material and combined thickness of the lining and outer "fur" it also provides a good amount of warmth, certainly on your head. I wouldn't wear this for any prolong exposure to the elements, but for quick trips from the house to car to mall or from school to the bus this should work fine and in all cases better then not wearing anything on your head.The "glove" parts are a great way to briefly keep your hands from the elements but are in no way a substitute for real gloves.  Again, This is made to be cute and with your hands in the sleeve/pockets it is very cute indeed.Rain, Snow etc - No, this is not appropriate for wet weather. It is in no way water proof or resistant and would be no different then putting a stuffed animal on your head and going out in the rain. If your wearing it and it starts snowing you should be fine, again, better then nothing but I wouldn't put it on to go out in a snow storm, it may keep you warm enough but I fear it may ruin the fur.Overall:I like it and feel it is worth the money. It appears well made (only time will tell), adds some warmth to your head and doesn't look overtly cheap. Also it is very cute and I smile every time my wife puts it on.

reviewText: I love this watch. Simple. Durable. Affordable. Need I say more?I will only because I love this watch. As I train for my very first marathon, it's nice to have a simple watch that helps me train without a lot of figuring out. This watch is a great tool when incorporating Jeff Galloway's run walk methods. It helps to keep track of different running intervals continuously, hands-free. When you do need to stop or restart the timer, the controls are simple enough to maneuver without peeling your eyes off the road.As a first-time runner, it's nice to have found an uncomplicated solution.Update: It's now been two years since I purchased this watch and it's in great shape. I run at least once a week for a long distance and I've yet to experience any deterioration in the strap. Here are a few points: I use this watch only when I run so I don't end up causing undue wear and tear - sure it's waterproof so I could wear it into the shower, but why would I? When I strap it to my wrist, I wear it loose - mostly because my wrists tend to swell during my runs, but perhaps the leeway reduces strain in the resin. Finally, I don't refasten the strap when I take it off. I'm too lazy to do so - maybe this allows the material to dry in a relaxed state preventing cracking?Simply put, I still love this watch to pieces!

reviewText: The model numbers are confusing.  Amazon's product page and Casio's website both call this SGW300H-1AV.  Once you put it in your shopping cart on Amazon, it is referred to as SGW300H-1AVCF.  I did receive the desired product with desired band (resin), and the packaging confirms that it is SGW-300H-1AVCF.I had been considering spending $150 for a barometer watch, and am so glad I discovered this instead.  For about 2-3x the price of a bottom-of-the-line wristwatch, you get a barometer.  But note that unless you live in a complete flatland, you will see pressure changes as you travel up/down even over very small hills.  So, you learn to ignore the pressure changes as you commute, for example.  However, this watch adds value in a few ways.  First, you get actual local pressure -- not that of a city 30 miles away.  Second, having it on your wrist gives you something to think about in idle moments (it's fun to watch the pressure change, watch the direction clouds are moving overhead, and imagine where the highs and lows might be).  Third, it's kind of cool to see how much pressure changes with altitude.  Actually, there's a down-side to this.  Where I live, the pressure has been around 24.8 inches.  Since all the weather reports and books use sea-level pressure, I have no intuitive feeling for whether 24.8 inches is high or low.  I guess I will develop that with time, but for now I'm just watching how the numbers change over time.  Actually, there is a pressure trend section of the watch which shows an arrow near the middle for small changes, and farther to the left or right for larger changes.  It does seem to work in general, but I am not sure how reliable this feature is, since it sometimes seems to show a change that doesn't match my interpretation based on the numbers displayed.  But perhaps it is referencing the original data at higher resolution, while I am displaying the numbers in mmHg, which is rounded to the nearest 0.05.The altimeter reading is merely calculated from the barometer reading, and I will probably place more trust in the GPS-based altitude on my Android device, since that doesn't require accounting for weather changes.  However, it is convenient to be able to glance down at my wrist for approximate altitude while driving.The thermometer, which shows a compromise between your wrist temperature and air temperature, has but one practical use:  To measure the temperature in places where you habitually take the watch off for long periods (e.g. bedroom or perhaps office).  Even when you take it off, it takes a long, long time to adjust to ambient temperature.  I made the mistake of recalibrating the thermometer, because I couldn't believe it was showing 80 degrees in my house half an hour after I took it off!  There is no way to go back to factory calibration (although you can obviously re-calibrate using another thermometer).  My advice is to be patient, and trust the factory calibration.The other aspects of the watch are just what you would imagine if you were to pay $15 for a non-barometer Casio watch.  The displays are perfectly visible from all typical angles.  The screen does not scratch from normal wiping with finger/shirt but I'm sure it will when it hits a rock.  The watch is about 1-7/8 inches across (perpendicular to the band), not insanely bulky.The main design criticism I have is that, when you are in barometer mode, if you want to see the altitude, you have to press the Mode button five times to get into Time mode and then press the Alti button.  Since other than the barometer/altimeter it's just a cheap watch, it seems silly not to allow the user to conveniently toggle between barometer and altimeter mode (e.g., just let the user press Alti while in barometer mode -- currently, this has no effect!).  Also it would be nice to have the date displayed all the time without having to go into Time mode.  Also, I would have gladly paid a little more if they could have added moon phase, tides, and sunrise/sunset times!  Surprisingly, there seem to be no affordable watches that combine all these features.  Since the pressure-trend display is blank in most of the watch's modes (or useless in Time mode, where it just shows graphic display of seconds), it would have been easy to put moon phase or tide height there, for example.I was going to buy the version with analog hands added (SGW400H), but was concerned the hands might block the barometer reading, which was the main feature of interest for me, so that didn't seem worth the risk.  I would have bought that if it had a feature to automatically fold the hands down (which some expensive models offer).  Another feature I thought would be cool is a graph-like display of the pressure over time, which some watches offer, but if you are commuting up/down hills that would not be meaningful most of the time anyway.All in all, it's a decent watch and well worth adding just $20-30 to have the barometer.

reviewText: I initially ordered Sloggers Premium Garden Clogs (open-heel), but reasoned that the Garden Shoe (closed-heel) would be better for my wobbly ankles than the open-heel model. I normally wear a 9-1/2 Narrow and I have high arches. The size 9 open-heel clogs were too short and too wide, even with two sets of insoles.  The size 10 open-heel clogs were much too long and too wide. I returned them and ordered the closed-heel Garden Shoes in a size 10. Eureka! These are my new favorite shoes.My new favorite shoes accommodate two sets of insoles (including the ones that came with the shoes) for a comfortable fit. I wear socks because shoes always fit better and feel better to me with socks. My heel comes up with every step, but this really isn't bothersome; it's what clogs do, and the Garden Shoe really fits like a clog that is both secure and comfortable.I tried some beautiful, high-quality, leather dress clogs in a couple of different top brands. But the hard rocker-bottom contour was not a hit with my high, rigid arches. My Sloggers are so comfortable that they beat out the much more expensive competition. I'm thankful to be beyond the need for fashion to override comfort!I find my new favorite shoes comfortable for walking and standing. My original intended use for my Sloggers was to wear them in the garden and walking around in our pasture, wet or dry, so I wouldn't ruin my leather shoes or boots. I don't like the hassle of putting on and taking off sneakers, and I no longer even own any. Sloggers are ridiculously easy to clean with a hose or a wet paper towel.My Sloggers quickly became my primary shoes; I wear them everywhere now, except to bed. :) I've ordered another pair in the Basic Solid Black to have a pair that will go with anything.I think Sloggers are attractive and comfortable and sturdy enough to go everywhere my life requires me to go: home and yard, errands in town, church, and court to watch my (attorney) husband's trials.  I have received compliments on my Sloggers since my first day of wearing them. It occurs to me that cashiers who stand all day would love Sloggers! With the gel insoles I inserted and the thickness of the traction soles, they do make walking and standing on concrete floors less fatiguing. I even tested them on a Wal-Mart trek, which normally leaves my lower back, knees, and ankles feeling splintered. I have fibromyalgia, as well as arthritis in my spine from neck to tail, and in my knees and ankles. I survived Wal-Mart intact with zero pain!I would say that Sloggers are a terrific value and well made in the U.S.A., which means a lot to me. Amazon offers free return shipping on shoes, so there's no risk in trying them.  For me, they're keepers.
summary: My New Favorite Shoes! (An Updated Review)

reviewText: The functions of this watch are great.  Compass works well, barometer works well, Altimeter works well, Solar charger works well and time is correct.  Anyone who claims that Barometer reads incorrectly probably has not taken it off their wrist.  Think about it, how can the barometer get an accurate reading while directly placed on your body heated wrist.  Take it off and allow some time for it to get actual reading.  Read the instructions and follow them, I have had great readings from all functions of this watch.  I take it hiking, hunting, camping, fishing and outdoors mostly and love it.  I have one complaint and look forward to fixing that with an easy watchband switch.  I am not a big fan of the titanium watchband, it easily comes unsnapped and almost caused me to lose this watch on a couple separate accounts.  I finally learned to use a small piece of duck tape when I go on my hikes to strap around the latch (works well).  I will be soon replacing band with a nylon or leather band that is more secure.  Other than the titanium band, I love this watch.  Main thing: If you want correct readings, follow instructions!Update 10-10-12:  I used my pliers to carefully crimp the band connector (or whatever it is called) and it now locks perfectly.  I actually love the band now and have not had a single problem with it.  Another cool factor:  I found a setting that initiates the night light when you flick your wrist......! Totally cool and useful!  I love this watch!  Expensive, but you get what you pay for.

title: Marmot Women's Ama Dablam Jacket
description: The women's Marmot Ama Dablam is named after a Himalayan mountain, and is designed to keep you comfortably warm -- while traveling light -- in just such a setting. The durable down jacket offers maximum warmth with minimum weight, with enough urban style to transition to the city streets.FeaturesLightweight, super-warm down jacket100% polyester DWR ripstop main material100% polyester embossed WR lining800 fill goose down insulationAttached, adjustable down-filled hoodVertical front chest pocket for quick access to small essentialsInside zip stuff sack pocket allows you to stuff jacket into its own pocketElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherZippered handwarmer pocketsAdjustable Velcro and elastic cuffs for comfort and adjustabilityAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion in arms without jacket riding up28.5-inch center back lengthMarmot DownMarmot often says that "down is in our DNA." The company was founded in 1974 as a manufacturer and seller of premium down jackets, vests, and sleeping bags, and continues to use fine quality goose down for its insulated outdoor products. Mountaineers and outdoor enthusiasts the world over rely on Marmot down gear for warmth, comfort, and sometimes survival.Down quality is determined by fill power and durability, which is dependent upon the age and maturity of the bird and the processing of the down. The best down comes from larger, more mature birds and goose down is generally better than duck down. More mature goose down has larger filament clusters than less mature goose down and these clusters, when grouped, provide many more trapped air pockets and therefore provide better insulation. To maximize the effectiveness of the down clusters, proper processing of the down -- sorting, washing, and drying -- is required to open them up.Higher fill power means higher loft, better insulation, lighter weight, and greater durability. Marmot tests all of its down for content, cleanliness, species, and fill power, guaranteeing minimum fill power for all down clothing and sleeping bags.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

title: Suunto Men's SS014809000 Core Outdoor Matrix Regular Black Watch
description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. Also features a digital thermometer. Menu-based user interface in English, German, French and Spanish. 2 year warranty.

reviewText: I've worn Timex Ironman watches for the past 13 years. They are very decent watches for a relatively inexpensive price. I prefer the resin strap watches because they don't retain odors like the cloth straps do.I can take or leave the Flix technology, it activated itself sometimes when I didn't want to, and wouldn't work when I did. I just relied on using the normal Indiglo button.These watches typically last me about a year and a half, and it is always the same piece that gives out. The small retaining band for the strap breaks inexplicably in the middle of the night, and I end up with the excess end of the strap flapping and catching on my clothes and falling off. The new watch straps are about half the price of what a brand new watch costs, and I find I prefer just to pick out a new watch because after the year the paint on the face has started to chip and it looks ragged. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

Also, PA does not charge tax on clothing, but Amazon charged me tax.  When I questioned this, Amazon's help desk did not refund the tax.  I am disappointed but it is always tough to buy clothes without being able to try them on first.  I ususally avoid doing so and will be very careful in the future.  I think the shoes could be improved with a higher heel and a wider, tighter elastic band around the ankle (the black part).  But I won't be buying them on line.....

I do hope to wear them while on my standup paddleboard as I really don't like being barefoot, but still want to feel the board under my feet (which real water shoes are to clunky for), I think these will be great for that. They won't make good traditional use water shoes though, as I think over time the roughness of a pool, or sand and rock will wear them out fast, especially so for anyone who drags their feet a little, or runs in them. The seams look really well sewn on my pair, and I think they will also hold up well under normal use. The material itself is also pretty thin neoprene, I would guess only 1 mm thickness. This is great to get the feel of being barefoot, without being exposed to the nasties on the floor.. Highly recommend as a travel slipper to wear in hotels!Size wise: I normally wear a 7.5 womens shoe, though I like to size up with sneakers, I bought these in a Large and they are perfect. They are not tight, they do not slip off at all, and are not stretched out on my foot. IMO, this size would not be comfortable for someone who had a shoe size larger than an 8.  I bought them prime, so free ship and a decent price, they are worth the $10 if you are looking for a thin sock like slipper that let's you feel barefoot but adds traction. In regards to smell, they are neoprene and neoprene smells, I can see how this would bother some picky people, but it does not bother me, I don't really smell them when they are on my feet. Plus I am used to neoprene products/familiar with them, so I expected this.I actually like them enough I will be ordering more, I do think they will be ideal for me to wear paddle boarding. I will update on this use once it's warm enough to get into the water.I give a full 5 stars, because they were exactly what I was looking for, barefoot feel that I can use on my paddleboard, plus good traction from the grippy footprint design on the sole.

I wanted to buy a red bezel and a green one.  The lady from customer service was very polite, but told me Wenger does not sell bezels separately and there is no chance that they will anytime soon.  Period.......______Received my new Wenger AquaGraph 72235 at the office today (8/28/2012) and have been wearing it for the past six hours. I like the white rectangle around the date window which makes it easier to find and the lume is much better than the Victorinox.In reading other reviews about this watch, I've found mine to be no different. How hard can it be to exercise a little extra quality control?  Also, the rubber strap is almost too short for my wrist (I had to use the second to last hole.)  I've since retired the Wenger strap to the box and have replaced it with a plain rubber strap with a deployant type clasp.  Again, I like the simplicity.At first I thought this watch was too heavy, but after a few hours I don't even notice the difference.  I'm pleased with my purchase and feel I've gotten good value for my money.12/30/2012 Update:  Still enjoying the watch! reviewText: Pros:- For a waterproof athletic watch, very attractive/slim/sleek.- I have had no problems with the waterproofing.- The loop that the watch strap goes through snaps into place, to keep the watch secure while racing.  Nice design feature, not visible in Amazon photos.- You can set multiple time zones, and select which one you want to be the primary one in use.Cons:- Indiglo is practically nonexistent (only visible at night/in the dark), as compared to other Indiglo watches I have owned.- The "tap" feature doesn't respond no matter how hard I whack the watch.  However, it seems to work when my wrist hits the water's surface.  As a result, I often finish my swimming only to find out that it thinks I have done hundreds more laps than I actually have.- If you start the stopwatch (a/k/a "chrono" mode), it counts it as a workout.  The only way to reset a workout (e.g., if you accidentally start the stopwatch), it automatically saves the workout.  You cannot delete a saved workout.  Every saved workout is averaged into your time.  Given that the "tap" feature seems to have a mind of its own, you will have numerous unintentionally "workouts" recorded because you accidentally hit your wrist on something.  As a result, all the progress tracking, average times, and other special features are practically useless.- Alarm is subtly quiet / discrete, not loud enough to wake me up, and it stops after only a few seconds.  Not functional as a wake up for people who tend to snooze.  OK as a daily reminder (I use mind to make myself leave work and go to the gym).Overall: Great for a waterproof, daily-wear, travel watch.  Not so great as a way to keep track of your triathlon training, or as a way to wake you up.  I am glad I did not pay the MSRP for the watch.
title: Timex Mid-Size T5K288 Ironman Sleek 150-Lap TapScreen Watch
description: Whether you're pushing yourself towards a qualifying time or a new personal best, the Timex Ironman Sleek 150-lap sports watch allows you to access information without breaking your stride. The cutting-edge performance watch includes everything a sports watch needs, including an oversized display, a huge lap memory feature, a training log, and a Target Time Pacer. As a result, you'll have an edge when training for your next sprint, distance run, or triathlon. The mid-size watch's primary distinguishing feature is its TapScreen technology, which helps you keep your eyes on the trail while you run or cycle. When TapScreen is active, a simple tap anywhere on the watch face will activate the lap timers, so you don't have to fiddle with a bunch of buttons to get to the proper screen. In a sport in which every second counts, the TapScreen function is a vital tool. The watch also includes a convenient Indiglo night mode, which makes early-morning and late-night training even easier. By holding down the Indigo button for three seconds, the watch face will automatically illuminate each time you press any button.Athletes who want to monitor their workout progress can turn to the watch's Lap Management System, which stores multiple workouts by date. The system keeps records of every lap/split and target time, along with records for your best lap and average lap speed. It also automatically stores workouts from the chronograph, letting you recall, for example, 150 one-lap workouts, one 150-lap workout, or anything in between. Perhaps the most important feature, however, is the Target Time Pacer. This feature helps you maintain your desired pace in a workout or race, so you can achieve your overall time goal. With every lap or distance segment, the watch provides audible and visual alerts to indicate whether your pace per lap is too slow, too fast, or on target. Without even a glance at your watch, you'll hear whether you're on track to meet your goal. As a bonus, the Lap Management System also recalls workout information from the Target Time Pacer, showing how much faster or slower you ran each lap and calculating your total workout time.Other features include a 24-hour countdown timer; three interval programs, each with up to 16 interval timers with user-selectable interval labels; three alarms, with daily, weekday, weekend, and day-of-week setting options; an easy-to-read display with three lines of text; open vents in the strap to minimize skin contact and increase breathability; and hydration and nutrition alarms, which remind you to refuel at regular intervals to top up essential reserves.SpecificationsChronograph: 100 hours, with lap and split timesMemory recall: 150 lapsOn-the-fly lap or split recall: YesLap counter: 199 lapsCountdown timer: 24 hours, with stop and repeatInterval timers: 16, with repeatAutomatic interval repetition counter: YesAlarms: 3 daily, weekly, weekday, or weekendTime zones: 2Case: ResinStrap: Co-molded resinWater-resistance: 100 meters

reviewText: This is the third running watch I've had and it's my first Timex.  I've owned to Casio's before (one being a g-shock), but after finding my g-shock to bulky and cluttered, and loosing my other Casio I picked up from Walmart, I decided to look around to find a new durable running watch.I run cross country and track so going from a generic stopwatch to a 30-lap chrono watch has been sweet.  The lap timer is easy to use and the display is big enough to take a glance and see my split and total time side by side.  The recall feature works perfectly and you even have some room to adjust the settings to configure your lap display how you like it.My favorite thing about this Timex, is its ease of use.  The only time I've had to look at a manual is when I first got the watch.  The display updates as you go through the various modes to show you what the new buttons mean so there is never a question on how to set the time or recall your laps.This watch is extremely  durable.  It has already taken a few shots and I've swam with it on several times.  The screen and body have held up nicely and I don't foresee any problems with them in the future.  The strap is great also.  I really like the notch that keeps the excess strap in place.The countdown timer and the alarm both work as expected.  The timer has some different settings and is easy to set up.  My only disappointment with the timer was that you can't set different intervals.  Like if you want to run for five minutes and walk for two your going to have to invest a little more for a watch that allows different intervals.  The alarm works well too, and the beeping successfully wakes me up in the morning, but I'm not a heavy sleeper so some may find it too quiet.Overall this watch is durable, easy to use, and can track splits really well.  The watch is a little bulky if you are used to a more minimalist watch but for me the weight was perfect, and for the price you can't go wrong with this watch.

reviewText: I'll start with an easy pros/cons:Pros:Easy to setupEasy to useBacklight is the perfect brightnessCrisp display is easy to read most of the timeLong enough lasting batteryCharge connector is easy to useCons:Not a "smart" watch.  More like a "clever" dumb watch.Limited usefulness overall- no touchscreen and only 4 buttons limits the future applications- no real easy way to add apps and faces to it, convoluted process to say the leastThey could have used the middle button to advance to the next notification (both the left and right-middle buttons dismiss the message), but they chose to make you scroll with the up/down button.  Sometimes you end up scrolling into the next message then have to go back and scroll some more.Looks and feels quite cheap... Watch is very expensive compared to the build quality- you can see where the sealant they used squeezed out between the halves of the case.  Don't believe? Look right above the watch strap where the glossy cover meets the textured back.Impressions:After receiving the watch I almost sent it back.  There was quite a bit of glue around the edges of the case and the general overall vibe was that this is an easy to scratch, cheap, hastily assembled watch for the money.  But after trying it  for a few hours it grew on me.  I still think the watch is worth, at most, $50 based on build quality and limited functionality.  But it's convenience makes up for the poor quality and lack of any real beneficial apps.  I have not gotten it wet yet, so I can't speak to its 5 ATM WR rating.I also have a Martian Victory, which is also overpriced for its build quality.  The Martian is great for looks (I use it for work).  The Pebble is good not great for play (water resistant -- i hope --).  I would say the Pebble is great for play, but I don't think the plastic front will withstand some types of play and at anything over $50 in price its a real stretch to call it "great for play".Conclusion:So far there is no truly great "smart" or "clever" watch available for iOS.  If you were hoping for the Pebble to be the first, keep waiting, you will only be disappointed with the Pebble.Update March 8th, 2014:The 2.0 update is out...  Didn't help my Pebble feel any less cheap or plastic ;).  I still don't think this watch is worth $100-$150.  Its now a $69 watch in my mind, up from $50.  The metal one MIGHT be worth $150 if its' vibrate feature doesn't sound like its tearing the phone apart.On the topic of vibration:Since wearing it at work a few days and leaving my Martian at home, I noticed that the vibration notification is so violent that it rattles the buttons and actually causes more of an interruption in a meeting than just leaving the phone's ringer on.  It sounds like it is actually rattling inside too since I can hold all the buttons gently and there is still a rattle noise during notifications.  So I had to set the Pebble's do not disturb to 22:00 - 17:00 so there is only 5 hours a day that the vibration isn't going to be an annoyance to anyone but me or my wife.  Discrete notification is NOT this watch's forte.Software:Version 2.0 is where this watch should have been on 1.0.  Its still sad that all the useful in-watch apps require the purchase(more often)/free download(rarely) of a "helper app" instead of Pebble making a real effort to integrate more functionality into their own app's back end to allow developers the freedom to do it all in one place.  At least there is a single place to go now to find apps/faces for your watch, so I guess that is progress.  Pebble's 2.0 app is kind of flashy graphically, but VERY clunky in operation.  It doesn't remember where you were while browsing the available apps/faces so if you want to check out the details on an app/face you have to resign yourself to going back to the search, typing in your query again, and scrolling to where you left off (if you can remember).I think that gets to the root of the problem with Pebble.  The company seems to have many dreamers, artists, and creative types, with only a few engineers.  Those engineers have no concept of UI design or usability (nor do the artists) so everything kinda comes out looking good with a bunch of quirks that really take away points from the overall experience.  Everything about this watch still feels half-assed and rushed with NO sense of apology about that or any other redeeming qualities.If you've not bought a "smart" watch yet, I'd keep waiting to see what the 3rd generation holds or, if Apple makes one, the 2nd generation after people start copying that.This watch is still 3 stars, just based on the physical appearance and build quality.

reviewText: I am a watch junkie and have always been a fan of Seiko kinetic watches for their affordability as well as their reliability.  I did not purchase this watch via Amazon because it wasn't available here at the time of my order so I picked it up locally from a Seiko Authorized Reseller to ensure I would have the Seiko Warranty in effect.This is a Kinetic watch which means it collects energy from the motion of your arm throughout the day and stores it.  On a full charge, this watch will run approximately 1 month without movement.  This Velatura also features "Direct Drive" which means that you can hand wind the crown to build up a bit of a charge.  While this feature is cool, it's a little more gimmicky than practical.  Picking it up and giving it a few shakes side to side is enough to build up enough charge to get things rolling.  Trying to hand wind this to any sort of power reserve is going to take FOREVER making it extremely impractical.The face is well organized, the gentle arc on the far left of the face is your power reserve meter.  At the top, the "M" represents a Months charge, in decending order you have "W" for Week, "D" for Day, and then 12 & 0 for hours left on the charge.  At the bottom of the face, in the 6 o'clock position is the date.  On the lower right side between the 3-5 position is the Day of the week display.  This makes for a beautiful design that is also extremely functional to read in my opinion.The face is black vertical lines that add an element of depth to the face with rose gold accents on the hands, power reserve dial, and day of the week dials.  Each of the primary hand positions (5,10,15, 20 etc) are luminescent circles with a ring of rose gold accent.The only flaw this watch has, as I see it anyway, is the band.  The band itself is fine, but being a silicone/rubber type it seems to be a little prone to failure.  I had to replace the first one when the strap guard snapped off for no reason (no damage just snapped off when putting it on one day).  I think the Seiko replacement set me back $60 which seems like an awful lot for what it is, considering it only last a couple years.  This was before Amazon started to carry them, and while they are less, they are still about $40 here.  I do prefer metal bands for their durability, but the rose gold on this watch makes that a little difficult to find a good match.  I've purchased several third party bands that are supposed to fit, even had reviews from people saying they used them on this watch but I couldn't ever get them installed.  Even after taking it to a few local watch-smiths here locally, they couldn't get them on right.I wear this as a daily driver since it dresses up and down so well.  Looks great with a suit or jeans and a t-shirt.  This is a larger watch that may look a little out of place on an extremely skinny wrist.  Be sure to check out the pictures online of people wearing them to get a feel for it or better yet, find one locally so you can try it on.At the end of the day, I love this watch.  I always get complements when I wear it and it's comfortable on the wrist.  It also keeps great time.  If I had one wish, I would love a Seiko replacement metal band in black with a rose gold accent on the safety clasp, but I don't think that will happen.  I'd definitely pick up another one if anything were to happen to this watch.  Couldn't go without it now!

reviewText: Well.  I contemplated for some time if I should write a review for this ultra affordable watch or not ... after some thoughts, this Casio deserves every bit of my highest recommendations so I decided to go for itIf you are reading this ... either you stumbled on the F91W-1 by looking at some of the cheapest Amazon stocked watchesOr you read from Wikipedia, or some watch forums, or other sources that this Casio is the favorite among the terrorist group.Well regardless what your motivation is ... this watch is worth every penny.Some background information.  I been collecting mechanical watches for about 16+ years.  And right now I own over 50 watches... From this humble $11 Casio to a few Rolex, Zenith, Omega, JLC that cost 500 times its price.  I also service some of my own mechanical pieces.  Although I do not have much experience with quartz watches.  I do know quite a bit about material, design and many aspects of a proper horological machine.And the down right truth is, there is nothing this Casio can't do.  As far as a practical machine, it can beat up your datejust/ submariner any day of the week.  (Although this might not be that big of a deal in todays cell phone oriented world)Pros:It is designed to be simple and intuitive, the trait of most Casios.  Button placement and functions are down right instinctive once you use it for a day or two.It is deadly accurate (duh), its quartz.The battery life is an amazing 7 years (given you use certain functions only once or twice a day.) Although some "upgraded" version has 10 year or solar battery.  The battery life is more then reasonable for any practical purpose.This is the most comfortable watch I own, due to one reason - the weight.  It feels like you are wearing a feather or nothing at all. 20 grams to be exact... or 0.7oz.  Crazy how light this thing is.The retro styling is another plus .. it may not have been cool in the 80~90s.  The nerdy black resin square case is now hip again...The construction of this watch is very well thought out to simplify the manufacturing process.  Which, btw, is done in Thailand.  Case is a single piece resin with slightly protruding plastic crystal.  All the electronics are on a one piece of ic board.  The case back is made from stamped stainless steel, secured by 4 screws, and the interior is where the alarm speaker goes.  A rather large rubber gasket surrounds the movement.  Light weight rubber strap with some mysterious reflective inclusion.ConsWater resistance:  The case construction does not allow any serious form of water resistance... as a matter of fact, in the Casio manual they do not recommend anything more then hand washing.  The real problem is the pushers, they lack any gasket so water will pour in when use underwater.  The tolerance of the case and SS back is decent.  But the gasket sits too low so a 100% secure seal will not be possible.  Crystal seems to be glued into place, so no problem with water there.  I think degrees of water resistance is how Casio separates their cheapest products from the slightly more expensive one.You can hear something rattle when you shake this watch ... it is nothing major howeverIf you are used to today's super large watch... namely, Graham, Panerai, 44mm, 50mm or the likes.  This watch will look puny to you at 35mm.  But if you like most watches in the 70s or 80s ... this is just the right size.The bottom line is ... this is a hell of a watch for the money.  As utilitarian as it could be yet possess some of the funk from the past decades.  It also carries a good amount of interesting back stories if you tell people about its popularity among the terrorists.  A great watch! And the best $9.99 I spend on a watch.

reviewText: This time piece rocks with accuracy in the mountains of + or - 10 meters it is very useful for expeditions in unchartered territory.Short of having maps programmed into it, it can be used in confidence in conjuction with a map to more easily work out where you are located and the compass is beneficial to assist in getting from point A to B.Coupled with this accuracy its robust design means at can be taken anywhere without damage or breakage.Additionally the barometer functions assist comprehensively in predicting weather patterns as well as adjustment to altimeter settings.Their are two quams however with this instrument:1. Approximate directions can be taken when the watch is on the wrist but the equipment is far more accurate when in its horizontal and still state.2. When operation occurs in certain weather patterns (e.g Cyclonic and rain depression or Anti-Cyclonic conditions)when the barometer is at both extremes of the pressure scale requires adjustment to reset correct altimeter conditions and hence changing weather conditions will affect the accuracy of the altimeter.Overall, a fine timepiece for any outdoorsmen who requires accuracy, consistency and reliability.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I think I'm on my 6th one of these watches, NOT because they are poorly made; on the contrary - they have to stand up to 24-hour-a-day use and abuse and, oh my goodness! how they do that! I actually keep an extra on hand just in case I manage to destroy the one I'm using. I have never had a watch so amazing before, and if they ever stop making this model, I am going to be seriously lost since I can't imagine going a day without it. I rely upon it so much that I find it almost impossible to exchange it for a dress-up watch - even for my own wedding - and I was the bride!!!The 3 alarms are vital to my lifestyle, as are the 2 timezone settings. The Indiglo light is essential because I am often working in darker rooms, and I love that it shows not only hours and minutes, but the day of the week, month and day, and seconds. I don't own a bedroom alarm clock; my watch has done that duty without fail since the first one I purchased. The description says the strap is leather and nylon, but it seems to me that it is entirely leather except for possibly the 2 cross-bands which hold down the tail end of the strap.Sometimes the Indiglo button will stop working and the setting-knobs will become difficult to push in. I have found that, in all cases, this was caused by an accumulation of dirt and lint under the bases of the knobs. It is almost impossible to access these areas without cracking the plastic ring around the face, so have a jeweler clean those places when he replaces your battery. (The batteries last for years but, as a warning, be aware that 2 of my watches were completely ruined because I made the mistake of getting the battery changed at Wally World, and the employees broke the 4 setting-knobs when they misaligned the backs before replacing them on the watches. Use a professional jeweler instead. You can also request a yellow Timex return-box from the jewelry counter at Wally World, and probably other places too. Then you can send the watch to Timex to have the battery replaced or any other problem resolved.)

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: I’m a production engineer in Venezuela and travel across time zones every month.  For years, I’ve been searching for a quartz analog-digital watch that included world time with a user defined time zone, plus a countdown timer longer than one hour for long flights or production runs, and of course, also the usual day, date, stop watch and alarms, chime and beep on or off, digital displays and luminous hands.  Format 4 has all that plus a screw in crown (as in my 45 year old, fine working Rolex) for 10 atmospheres water resistance, screw in back plate, second hand,  rotating bezel, not too big a case diameter, and is also solidly made and reasonably priced.Momentum read my mind! Format 4's case is made of Titanium, thus lighter compared to steel watches.  The print work on the face is sober (unlike cheap or toy watches.) The olive green digits on black display are highly readable (the more light the better) and good enough in the dark. I was also pleasantly surprised to find a user defined long term alarm, which I set and labeled for my next year’s wedding anniversary, a date I always forget.Format 4 allows for Daylight Savings Time adjustment for each time zone, important because countries differ in policy. Curios about DST, I wrote a question on Momentum’s website.  I received a phone call in less than 24 hours, plus a follow up email.  With this level of fast and motivated customer attention, and their renewable 2 year warranty for up to six years, I’ll wear Format 4 long term.Momentum does not make their movements.  But neither do almost all brands except for Rolex and a handful more! Most watchmakers, including the well know high priced brands, buy movements from mostly four specialized makers in Switzerland and Japan.  Format 4 has two movements from two manufacturers.I added to the black rubber strap a Hadley-Roma 20mm butterfly push button deployment clasp.  It upscales the Format 4’s appearance and comfort, and adds safety putting the watch on and taking it off.  The clasp, part BKL150W, available in Amazon, is brushed stainless steel, indistinguishable from the case’s slightly darker titanium metal.Momentum got it perfect with Format 4!
summary: Momentum got it perfect with Format 4!

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet.
