Based on the reviews for these Sloggers, I ordered a pair that I have been using now for several weeks.  They have solved my problems because they do not have air holes...no pine straw getting caught or sticking my feet, clean-er feet, easy to put on/off.  I haven't been aware of their being much hotter than the Crocs but I try to garden early in the morning before the summer heat settles in for the day.My only reservation is that for some climbing up/down a few hilly places in my yard, the Sloggers slip a bit but I'm learning how to wear them safely.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I really, really want to like the Pebble smartwatch.  I've been using it for three months now, almost on a daily basis in conjunction with an iPhone 5s.  I am running the most current firmware/software/etc.  It's just incredibly annoying that it loses connection with my phone so often.  Generally, twice a day I will have to go through some process that I still haven't completely figured out that includes turning bluetooth off and on for my phone; shutting down the pebble and restarting; restarting my phone, etc.When it works, it's enjoyable to use.  When it doesn't, it isn't that attractive of a piece of jewelry to wear.  I like that it has integration with things like map my run.  90% it works.  Sometimes it just freezes in the middle of a run.  They now have some other interesting apps like integration with evernote.  It's nice to look at, but in reality, I would always pull my phone out for something like this.I have one other problem that comes up from time to time.  For some reason, when it is paired with my iPhone, my iPhone can no longer make an audio notification for any app.  I've checked all the settings, etc and nothing seems to be wrong.  The only thing that works is unpairing the pebble and restarting the phone.  Not sure which device gets the blame for this, but it is annoying.So overall, I give the idea of a Pebble smart watch 4 stars and the execution 2 stars, giving it my total score of 3.I really hope apple eventually comes out with something that works better with an iPhone.I've paired the device with my wife's S4 for a couple of days.  It seems to work ok, but still loses pairing at least once a day.
summary: I like the idea of it more than the actual product

reviewText: This is my first time buying a "scrub watch", with its silicone band being my priority for purchase.  I wanted a watch that was easy to use and easy to clean while working in a hospital.  I just received my watch.  The watch is very comfortable.  The band is smooth and nothing pinches or pulls.  If you like your watch really tight or have really small wrists then this band may be too big for you.  I can wear it on either the tightest or second tightest setting, and I think I have fairly average female wrists.  The silver color complements with the white and is easy to read.  The red "milliary time" and seconds hand are really easy to read.  This is not a sweeping seconds hand (which I do prefer), but the tick is not excessively loud.  The watch is a bit bulkier then I am used to but is not heavy.  The diameter including the silver and white trim is 1 and 10/16 of an inch.  The diameter of just the dial where the numbers are is 1 and 2/16 of an inch.  I have not tried cleaning watch or washing my hands, but I don't suspect any problems.  Even though the watch is "sporty" and casual looking because of the clunky band, it is not overly cheap looking.  I hope it lasts!  Overall, I am happy at this point.

reviewText: (Please note that I did not buy this through Amazon.com or from the current seller, so this is not a reflection on them.) This "pattern" is a single sheet of paper that someone just started writing general directions on.  There clearly was no editor, nor did they take the simple step of having someone actually try to use this "pattern" with no previous experience.  The primary factor in writing up the instructions seems to be that everything had to fit on a single 8.5x11-inch piece of paper.  In fact, the first sentence is "Use the leftover material from your Bow n Go Bag..."  At the top of the page in extremely faint, teensy, tiny print it says, "Companion Pattern to the Bow n Go Bag (sold separately)."There are alternative instructions for making a piece of quilted fabric to glue onto the flip-flop instead, but if you want to make the pretty pictured flip-flops that match the bag, you are simply out of luck.  I paid a staggering $12 for this when it was new, and felt that it was frankly a case of theft when I received it in the mail.  I bought some of the required items, but calculated that after buying the pattern, fabric, the Craft-tex Plus, the heavy-duty fusible foam batting, the Shoe Goo Glue, and a nice pair of flip-flops (it is too much work and expense to apply to a pair of old, worn-out flip-flops), I would have been out nearly $100, when you take into account five different shipping & handling charges.  (I could not get very much at one place, because when I bought this stuff, many of the items were new and had only one manufacturer and not many sellers.)  I wound up using what I had already purchased on something else (heavy fusible interfacing and batting are great on bags) and just skipping the rest, as it would have been throwing good money (that not yet spent) after bad (money spent on this "pattern").

reviewText: The main attraction of this watch is that it provides ballistic calculations for precision shooting with a rifle.I've found it to be quite useful for making bullet drop and windage corrections.  The software seems to be comparable to other ballistics software I've used, as the resulting corrections appear consistent with results from other ballistics software programs.I have two complaints:  One is that the analog watch hands tend to obscure the digital read out.  When inputting and reading ballistic data, the hands often get in the way.  I solve this problem by simply putting the hands in "set" mode, shutting down the hand movement, and leaving them at 3 and 9 o-clock positions, so they are out of the way.  When I'm done shooting, I reset the hands using the digital time read out (the 2nd time zone reading.)  Only problem with this is that the watch is not waterproof when in set mode (because the crown is unscrewed.)The other complaint is smaller, and that is that the input options for the balistics data is not as precise as it could be.  Temperatures are entered in 10 degree increments, altitude in 100 foot increments, etc.  It probably doesn't make that much of a difference, as my inability to shoot straight introduces a greater level of error into the system than does the rounding effect of the input data, but still, it would be nice to have more precise increments of data.Haven't had the watch long enough to comment on long term durability, but it's held up fine so far.

reviewText: The watch design style and functions are the best for the money. It runs on a high end Swiss ETA movement and is highly accurate when compared to an atomic clock or watch. This watch has not gain or loss a second in 2 weeks when compared to atomic clock time. Unlike expensive 100% mechanical chronographs, winding or self-winding (automatic), this electromechanical watch with its stepping motors can provide stop watch accuracy to 1/10th second or 100 msec. One draw back is that as a stopwatch, it cannot keep track of elapsed time beyond 30 minutes. There just isn't enough space on the dial to add another one hour or 12 hours subdial. Two features that make this chronograph stand out against comparable ones. One is the cockpit instrument design which allow easy reading in low light conditions and legibility of the hands and numbers (both very large). The other feature is the chronograph function buttons which do not protrude from the watch case but yet can be pushed in with ease with your finger tips and not so small like other chronographs that you need to use your fingernails.

reviewText: Used to have a T.H.E. wallet that I loved, unfortunately it disappeared when I completed a military PCS move.  Thankfully all the contents were elsewhere at the time.  Ordered this one as a replacement- one of the metal grommets was chipped 50% of the way through, the other almost entirely.  Also the stitching on the shark bite closure wasn't as good as the last.  I mean all the stitches were there, but there wasn't as much 'slot' to tuck the 'flap' into so it sticks out more.  I returned it because I'm accepting what should be a factory second.I currently use the J.R. version (ACU).  I would say T.H.E. wallet is better than the J.R. for most people.  Don't be frightened by the size, they are both big and noticeable in the rear pocket.  The original wallet will be more comfortable to sit on because it lies flatter.  It also can hold a passport (or some index cards).  The J.R. really can't hold that much more than a regular wallet (except it holds large checks/boarding passes neatly).  It's probably not worth the extra thickness you are taking on... so I'd say stick with the original and use it as a travel wallet.For now I'm going to keep my J.R. and look for a different travel wallet.  For what it's worth it seems like the ACU wallets have more symmetrical stitching on the sharkbite section.  My last T.H.E. was ACU and it was perfect, unlike this one.  I've also owned a black J.R. which had the same issues with the sharkbite section not being sewn right, as opposed to the one i'm currently using which is perfect.

reviewText: I bought this jacket because I am allergic to down but need to stay warm during Boston winters. Overall, I am happy with this jacket although the sizing is weird. reviewText: Let me start by saying I like the look of the watch.  It is clean and simple, which I like.  I wish they had a metal band for this watch as the rubber strap is a little thicker than I like.  My dislike comes from the service.  Five weeks after receiving this watch, the time was way off one morning.  I thought maybe the stem had come out and caused the time to get off, so I reset the watch.  The next morning the same problem, the movement was sticking.  I went onto my Amazon account to request a return, but it was past the 4 week period that Amazon will take a return, so I had to go through the Manufactures’ warranty.  I went on the Wenger Web site and that site points you to a very simple .pdf page with instructions on how to get the watch serviced.  They do not have an on-line request for a return authorization, nor do they have anything in place on-line to track the status of your repair.  So, I called the toll-free number and the person on the phone said something like “Manually fill out the paperwork and just mail it to us we will process the repair, no need for a return authorization.  Be sure to insure it if it gets lost”.  That was the return process, just mail it to a black hole in New York.  The .pdf document says it takes 3-5 weeks for repair.  After six weeks, I called the warranty people “Precision Time” and asked about the status of my watch.  A friendly lady found my order in their system and told me they had been moving facilities and were backed up on repairs.  They couldn’t tell me how much longer it would be, but she hoped for 2 weeks.  She said I would know when they got to it, because they would call me and tell me how much the shipping would be to get the watch back.  I expressed my displeasure on the time and having to pay again for shipping.  She said it was out of her hands, they only do the repairs for Wenger.  She then gave me the Wenger Customer Service number.  I then talked with Wenger Customer Service and she was helpful, but it was out of her hands as Precision Time is a separate company.  She said she would call and ask for expedited service and a waiver of the return shipping fees.  I asked for a new watch and not a repaired watch as it was only 5 weeks old.  She then asked why I didn’t take it back to the place I bought it and I told her that Amazon would not take it back after 4 weeks.  This is when I found out that  Amazon is not an authorized retailer, so she could not replace the watch as it might not be an actual Wenger watch.  I was left to the mercy of Precision Time.  I did receive my watch three weeks later with no shipping charge.  Point of the lesson of this sad tale:  Be sure who you buy from is an authorized retailer if you are making a significant purchase.
summary: Watch is OK, but watch out for the service!

reviewText: Use in dishwasher top rack only is why I gave only 4 stars. Do not put in a washing machine. Should be a disclaimer that using in an actual washing machine is at your own risk. Otherwise, I use Dawn Liquid Dish soap (extra strength) because Dawn is a good degreaser of sweat on the inside of our company logo baseball caps. I use a SOFT toothbrush to scrub the greasy sweat areas on the cap, then put it into the Ballcap Buddy and put it on the top rack of an empty dishwasher (NO dishes and NO dishwasher soap present!) and start the dishwasher. Before it gets to the dry cycle, I remove the cap and keep it in the Ballcap Buddy to air dry. The Ballcap Buddy won't come apart in the top rack of the dishwasher. The instructions said not to leave the cap in the dishwasher's dry cycle so we air dry the baseball hat right in the Buddy. Comes out perfect every time. If the instructions said to use the Buddy in a dishwasher top rack only and not in an actual washing machine, I would have given it 5 instead of 4 stars.

reviewText: Rugged, easy to read, and it keeps pretty good time too. I read somewhere that someone was having trouble with "recessed" buttons. Well, I have no idea what watch they were reviewing but these buttons are not recessed. Even the "set" button, the one you'd expect to be recessed, protrudes enough to be easily operable.As a watch if functions pretty much like any other watch out there. It displays the time with seconds and the date with the day. It has an alarm, a timer, and a secondary time function (which I have never used). The only thing that differentiates this watch from most of its competition is the Indiglo feature. I'm not sure how it works, I suppose I could look it up if I really wanted to know, but when this button is pressed the entire screen lights up with a pale, uniform glow making the display extremely easy to read in the dark. This is the reason I keep buying Timex.There is just one real design flaw.Over the years they have changed the layout of the display and even the design a bit but for some reason the clear plastic face of this watch is a convex dome that bulges out beyond the rim making it extremely easy to get scratched up. It's better than it used to be, but it still a problem. Fortunately the display is large enough to read even if the face is a bit dinged up.Overall this is a good watch.

I'll be using them as slippers, dog and cat walkers, and knock-around shoes, as well as rain shoes.Update the next day:  I took my dogs for a walk in these Sloggers, and they do require some getting used to.  For one thing, they ride a bit low in the back (probably because of the padded insert that raises your foot up) and they tend to slip up and down when walking. Not a big deal for me.  They're flexible and easy to get your foot into--nothing to tie--and nothing hurts.  They do make my feet sweat a bit.  So far, no piercings, but I did notice that one of my cats seemed interested in pawing at them (I stopped her in time).  If you have pets, be careful where you store these.I also like the whole recycle vibe about these shoes, so that's a strong selling point with me.Additional notes, 6/20/2012:  I've been wearing these Sloggers pretty regularly all spring, and one thing I should mention is that they smell pretty bad inside because they're plastic and rubber, my feet sweat, and there's no air circulation.  You need to wash the insoles and the rest of the shoe from time to time.

reviewText: I was really excited to be part of the Kickstarter campaign for the Pebble.  When I finally received my Pebble, I was really excited.  The packaging was extremely well done and made the unboxing part of the experience.  Once I charged the watch with the included magnetic connector, setup took about 3 minutes.  Everything was great.  Daily friends and even passersby asked for a look and a demo.  I ran, biked, and swam with the watch as well as wet and dry saunas with no issues in watch performance.  Everything was great...until bumping into a wall in my house after stumbling over my dog in the dark.  I literally bumped the wall without fall or full bodyweight press.  The backlight came on and I noticed the telltale sign of broken screen:  large blotches of dark area and spiderwebbing.In an effort to fix my Pebble, I tried to contact the manufacturer.  Figuring out how to contact them was really hard and eventually I had to use the app to try to connect that sent an email with all of the functional stats from the watch.  After explaining the damage, I got a response that implied that maybe it was a minor scratch.  I'm still working through what to do for repair or a replacement with the Pebble team.  To be continued...wish me luck!Pros:+ Really cool to not have to pull my phone out to quickly read a text or email+ Easy setup and updateCons:- A little bulky but understandable as a 1st gen product- Case cracked within 2 weeks with a pretty minor bump into a wall; too fragile!- Customer service is a bit difficult to work throughI love the idea; Apple would be crazy not to release their own version or improve the Nano as a watch to interface with the iPhone.

reviewText: I admit my fascination for watches is a weakness. I just need one - but I have several. If it were only about telling the time I should have been satisfied  long ago. But as I said, I have a weakness.Up to now I have aspired to Swiss luxury. Pressing my nose on the jewellers window along with other noses beside mine - contemplating what might be - with a small mortgage.But then came the Timex Ironman. Inexpensive, practical and with all the functions anyone other than an Astronaut / Pilot or Deep Sea Diver would need - it caught my eye, my curiosity and my wallet.The idea was to buy a watch that would serve for outdoor knockabout stuff free from the fear of scratch, bang or bust. That was the idea.The reality is a timepiece that works - at work or play. It is light, it is functional and it is accurate. Some reviewers here have complained about the side buttons which they say are easy to set off by mistake. To be honest I haven't found this a problem. The timer is useful for eggs and the alarm is helpful for life. It's waterproof and the beep is good too - if you like that sort of thing, (which you can switch on or off), like an electronic cuckoo chirping on the hour through the day. (It doesn't do it at night so as not to disturb). So far, it has proved to be robust and easy to wear - which is why it's become a easy companion. It isn't too large and it isn't too tacky. In fact it has a smooth and smart black finish - with a clear and visible screen - which works well for the city and the park.All in all, it's an easy recommendation. Tick tick. Tick.

reviewText: This could be a fantastic product and my husband loved it when we first got it.  He loved seeing his pace, and he loved uploading his workout to the Nike+ website and seeing the graph of his run/pace, and making one of their "goals" they have on there.  He was more motivated to go out and run with this.  It's easy to use as is the program needed on your computer.The piece with the time on it comes right off and plugs directly into your USB.  THIS IS WHERE THEY FAILED!It's somewhat loose in the usb port, and the piece itself is curved, so with a laptop I had to have the computer near the edge of the table and remember not to move the laptop back or else the sportband piece hit the table.  A bit of a pain and potential for damaging either electronic!The sportband was a bit touchy in the usb port (had to wiggle it just right sometimes for the program to launch itself) and this got worse over time.  After about 2 months, give or take, it STOPPED WORKING when you plug it into the computer.  It worked fine with your run and everything, but the computer/program no longer recognized it.  It would charge and say that it was fully charged while plugged in, but we couldn't get the runs off it.  It only shows you info for your most recent run and then your total mileage, so if you're like my husband and only uploaded after you've done more than a couple runs, you lose your run data.Nike support was good, and they sent us a brand new sportband.  We used this for 2-3 months and then the EXACT SAME THING happened again.  They do not do refunds, so once again we traded in for a brand new sportband - and sold it on ebay for 30-40 bucks.We considered the GPS watch instead, but that connects to the usb in almost the exact same manner, and we didn't want to waste our time/money/sanity.  So save yourself the trouble and just don't buy this.Nike needs to improve this product.  Make it water/sweat proof and provide a seperate solid usb hookup!We now have a New Balance GPS watch, and while you don't upload your runs to the computer, at least you can save multiple runs and view all of the info for each run.  Distance/speed/pace/calories/date.

reviewText: Once I decided to get a HRM I decided on three main criteria:  I wanted a large display so it would be easy to read; I wanted it to have a decent interval-training option; I wanted it to be reasonably reliable.I couldn't find any good master comparisons of all the current watches, so I decided to start with the large display.  I figured it would be easiest to get large numerals on a vertical display, so I did an image search and tracked down all the HRMs with vertical displays.  I read reviews and manuals on these, and checked the reviews at various sites.  I also did searches for reviews which mentioned interval timing just to try to ensure I hadn't missed something.  A different (more recent?) version of this watch, the T5K545, came out on top.  The proportion of dissatisfaction in the reviews is at the lowest end of the range for this price bracket, and it had the best interval setup I could find with a large display as well.I didn't notice the difference and bought this version of the watch (the main difference seems to be in the type of chest strap it comes with).  I have had the watch for a month and am very happy with it.  The HRM works exactly as described.  The watch is easy to read and has good flexibility in terms of setting up what is shown on the display.  The interval timer includes 2 programmable workouts, each can be set for up to 8 intervals with beeps at the change, and the workout sequence can be set to repeat if you like.  These intervals can be set for specific HR zones, and if the HR alarm is on, the watch will give distinctive beeps for being above or below your target for a given interval.  I have found the HR recovery timer to be very useful as well.  At some point I will probably program my own HR zones rather than use the watch's built in zones which are set up according to the standard percentage of max HR.I found the watch easy to set up but I read instructions and don't usually have problems.  I can think of people who wouldn't want to mess with it, so factor that in if you're not comfortable playing with gizmos with a lot of options.When I first got it the tap feature did not seem to be working, but after setting it to the highest sensitivity and learning to touch it with 2 fingers and a quick tap it's working fine--it almost seemed to need to loosen up a bit.The watch is huge.  If you don't care what it looks like it works fine even on very small men's wrists.  Due to the fixed angle of the band coming off the case it's not going to look fully at home on even the largest wrists but that's something few will notice on the large wrists.A note about heart rate zones.  Although the idea of training according to zones is very appealing, finding out your real maximum heart rate in order to set those zones is problematic.  The common age-based formulas give you an average which may be as much as 20 beats off your actual MHR.  Timex has a 'Tools for Success' brochure with an exercise-based process for figuring out your MHR which offers a nicely different approach.  Ultimately, unless one wants to use a doctor or try one of the radical strategies found on the web, one has to watch for things like how your workouts affect you, how well you recover, etc., and adjust accordingly.

reviewText: I know I'm not the only one who somehow always has a few Christmas gifts hanging around that never get delivered over the holidays.  I could save them for next year but it can be more fun to surprise someone with the spirit of Christmas Every Day.  Well I've seen Winter Santa's and Tropical Santa's and Summer Santa's for Christmas in July.  I couldn't imagine what to do to kick off a Springtime visit from Santa and lo and behold here it is - a "Spring" Santa (pa rum pa).  Maybe I'll pin a red silk tulip, a yellow daffodil or a daisy chain to the brim... I agree the fit could be snugger but I don't think the issue is size or diameter.  The cap is shallow and my guess is that this was deliberate because, just perched on the crown of a head, it could accommodate a wide range of head sizes.  If you're just using it as a momentary gag joke, it'll probably perch just fine on its own but for longer use I'd agree that a sewn or pinned on elastic or ribbon wrapped around it could help.  I'm not letting that stop my fun because this thing has a really tall, bouncy impressive spring to it, and even just sitting on a table, a windowsill, atop a doll or stuffed animal on a shelf (or perched on the top of a Christmas tree?), it's sure to attract attention and invite some whimsical play.

reviewText: Disclaimer: I am a devoted Amazon fan, however I purchased my Pebble at BestBuy, where the price was $150. This is one of the only geek gadgets this year I have purchased outside Amazon, but saving $69/watch (I bought 2) was hard to pass up.Whether you have an iOS or Android smartphone (or tablet - it works with those too) to pair with the Pebble will probably directly relate to how much bang you get for your buck. I have a Samsung Galaxy Mega smartphone with a 6.3" screen which fits comfortably in my purse, however, I don't like constantly taking any phone in and out of my purse every time to check it when I get a text or email (and I get a lot.) This watch not only notifies me who is calling,  it also notifies me who is texting (and what they're saying), who's Facebookin' me, and who is emailing me personally to one address, and emailing me at my separate work address.  For both my personal and work email, the subject and part of the message is displayed on those alerts. Using the Pebble smartwatch app and the 3rd party Pebble Notifier app (both available from the Playstore), this watch frees me up to pull my smartphone out when I want to, rather than have to.The install of the app and upgrade of the firmware thru Pebble's app on the Android o/s is fairly easy - however it isn't straight forward, consistent or user friendly when installing the app or upgrading the firmware for the watch on the iOS 7 o/s.  In fact, the iOS version of the Pebble install/firmware update can be downright annoying: it took twice to install the app and firmware update on the iOS device for the Pebble to finally install the firmware, reboot and reconnect. I can only attribute this to the fact that iOS 7.0 was recently released by Apple and as per their usual modus operandi, they've also released at the same time the SDK's (software developer's kit) necessary for OEM's like Pebble to develop their corresponding AppStore apps. So in short, using the new iOS 7.0 with the Pebble smartwatch app is more buggy than that of the Android version and may continue until developers for the product further their knowledge of the new iOS 7 operating system. It bears noting that extending the inherent watch and Pebble app capabilities via 3rd party apps is more mature and plentiful for Android users vs those with iPhone or other Apple devices.The battery life is terrific - even with heavy use. The watch has a large face - on men this is insignificant, but for women with slender wrists it's noticeably significant. The watch band, thankfully because I'm not much into rubber, can be changed to any 22mm band.All in all, provided you recognize that this device is a first step toward emerging smartwatch technology and the capabilities are different between Android and iOS smartphones/tablets, you shouldn't be disappointed with your purchase.

reviewText: Sometimes, when you're the first out of the gate, you end up not having all the features and flash that your followers do, but considering this was kick-started and is in turn kick-starting the competition, I still stand by my little Pebble.It's come a good way since i purchased it, with the community providing great apps, and the Pebble team working on keeping the official Pebble app for iOS updated and increasing functionality.It's been rocky at times, but in the end, I have exactly what i want in a smart watch—a way to see the time, date, weather, and any alerts WITHOUT having to reach into my pocket. And because you're not constantly turning your phone on and off, you're saving the battery life for more important things.Sure, I'd love a color display, and maybe a speaker built into it—but unlike it's followers, which may have some of those things, it's Platform Agnostic and Brand Agnostic—you can pair it with Android or iPhones and know there's a great community further tweaking and exploring the limitations of the Pebble Marketplace—it's not done evolving.There are also a wide variety of ways to customize the look, with snap-on faces, adhesive wraps, and band swaps.And it's waterproof, so you can shower with it.  (I've heard they no longer recommend it, but I think as long as you don't keep it in super-hot water for 30 mins, you're probably fine.  I shower with it daily and have never had a problem.For the money and how far it's come, it's a great SmartWatch for those who want to dive in and not worry about being locked into a brand or platform.

reviewText: this will be a rough review of pros and con of the watch, features that are included and what makes it great compared to other abc watches.When I first got in to these type of ABC watches, there were so many choices. I didn't know which one to get. There are known brands such as suunto, garmin, casio, etc. but Timex is reputable definitely.However I chose the WS4 based on how clean looking it is, compared to other watches. Everything you need at the moment is on the screen.Functionality, compared to other ABC watches, they do what they do. Thermometer, altimeter, barometer, compass, time keeping, dual time, timer, stop watch, activity log recording.One thing I noticed is that there are features included in this watch that are not included in other watches, and other features from other watches are not included in this.Ex. storm alarm is not in this, separate log keeping is not, sun rise sun set. - well to me these are not the most deal breaker of all.What WS4 have that is not on other watches includes a big 36 hour graph from altimeter to barometer to temperature, big analog clock on screen all the time in any menu. The weather forecast indicator, thermometer, ease of access in switching readings on barometer, altimeter. separate dual time including 24 hr format for each. Repeating timer to the seconds.  Altittude alarm, chronograph for above certain altitude. interchangeable separate view for chonograph - overall time and the time splits. compass calibration is good with declination level to get you where you wanted.final awesome setting is the multiple altitude reference point setting. the altimeter may drift like every other abc, but you can easily readjusted from known location with specific altitude reading.I notice this watch has an anti- fog, grease coating on the glass. oily and sweat smudges dont easily stick to the screen compared to the suunto watches. on the suunto i had to constantly wipe smudges off from finger prints.No wonder timex nailed it with these function making it one of the most ease of access abc watches I've ever come to try.Switching between menu is clean - altitude menu, barometer menu, chronograph, repeating timer, alarm, log recording (just hit up the stopwatch) keep track of every detail from altitude height, difference,max, min, barometer, high-low, temp high-low, to averagesHowever what I found that was most important was reading visibility and readily function, even in the roughest situation such as a heavy rain storm, dusty, night time. I can still read the screen and operate with ease. I've tried other ABC, but this one has the smoothest transition while operating the buttons. Not to mention one of the brightest looking illumination when the metal indiglo button is pressed. you can hold it until it beeps and then every button pressed will activate the lighting- very useful in darker places.The time keeping is superb, I'ved test the time keeping and accurate to the seconds is on par with very very very little split second time drift. Over the course or 2-3 month, the second only drifted off by 1/4 of a second. the quartz mineral is high quality. forget the radio-sync actomic time solar power time keeping shenanigan from casio. One single cell battery for 2.99 on the ws4 will last for more than a year. It does not justify the extra 100 dollar for a constant needed to charge solar power watch.Compare to Suunto watches, believed me I used both, although they are lighter and cool looking, their durability lacks in terms of watchband and scratches. I've used ws4 for nearly half a year, no scratches and marks on the screen or the metal casing. I had more trouble with the suunto in reading the small font and operating the flimsy buttons. I know for sure the heavy duty resin band on the ws4 will outlast the band on the suunto.in terms of water resistance, rated at 50m this is better than suunto- consumer price range watches which is only 30m. I've read about condensation problem in suunto watches. But with the ws4, I've not had any problem, I let it get splashed in the rain, wash it in the showers,put in tub of water to clean, the sensor were still working 100%. Although I know for sure Casio has the better water resistance in term of 100m rating.Overall, this watch is tough as a brick, I can accidentally bang it in hard surface and it is left unscathed. I would say the ws4 is for people with bigger arms, stature, or else you will stand out. But people complimented me and was curious about what type of watch I wore. I notice it's a bit bigger and tat heavier than other ABC watches I've test.only some minor problem I had was the thermometer reading when worn, but like all other abc watches, requires you to take off watch and wait a while to get accurate reading.the weather forecast is accurate 95% of the time after getting it calibrated from very high barometer reading ( meaning super sunny and clear weather) but it is set to go after that.But the choice to invest in abc watch is up to you, the timex ws4 is well reputable and quality to me. just make sure the guy next to you dont wear the same watch.

reviewText: The Nike SportBand is a great companion for running.  I am a pretty small person; therefore, wearing a huge GPS watch tends to get in the way and looks pretty ridiculous.  This is a great option for when I want to go on a run and don't want something bulky on my wrist.  It does a fairly descent job of getting a correct accuracy on your runs once you calibrate it.  I found that I had to calibrate it every few months depending on how conditioned I was during that month since my stride seem to change.I have had this product for over a year and it has been great to take on trips with me instead of my GPS watch.  However, you have to understand that you will not get an exactly accurate measure of distance (at least I don't).  However, you should come pretty close.My only gripe about it is that sometimes it has software/hardware failure in which it does not upload your last run to the website.  There are some ways to fix this, but whenever I fixed it, it ended up deleting all of my runs on the watch and I was not able to upload them onto the website.  I was pretty frustrated because I had gotten back into training for a marathon and I lost several of my runs.  I came across this issue once but other people have commented that it has happened several times.I really enjoy the Nike+ website because it is very user friendly and has a lot of training options.  I wish it would be more customizable though but I will take it for now.
summary: Easy to use with some flaws

description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. I did check and John Wayne wore both suspenders and a belt with his cavalry uniform in "She Wore a Yellow Ribbon", so it is ok.Second, I always get ones with weak clips. reviewText: I love the appearance and how comfortable it is.  I have a small wrist and have had trouble with other watches, but this fits well on the second to tightest position.  The band end reaches all the way to the outer side of my wrist, but is held securely by the well-designed little loop.  The watch came with mostly clear instructions, and most features are fairly easy to operate, though I find the buttons a little hard to depress.  I love having the day and date available all the time, and how easy everything is to see.  The main drawback for me is that the alarm and timer signals are so quiet that I often cannot hear them, especially if there is a sleeve covering the watch, or a small amount of noise in the room.  I doubt very much that I would hear the alarm if I was sleeping (I mostly use the alarm for reminding me of appointments).  Other negatives for me: I found it very difficult to use the multiple alarms, and eventually kept myself to using just one of them, which works easily; I have no experience with chronographs, and was unable to figure out from the instructions how it works; Recently (around 3 months since I got it) I discovered that the Indiglo feature which allows you to see the time in the dark, is no longer working.  I'll be sending it for warranty service.Update 4/27/14:  I got the watch back awhile ago from warranty service, and I believe it is a new replacement.  It looks identical to the original one I had, but the buttons are easy to press, the light works, and the alarm is much easier to hear (though I still doubt I would hear it in a noisy room or if I am sleeping).  I'm very happy with it.  (FYI, for warranty service you need to send an $8 check to cover postage).

description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: I bought the Pebble Smartwatch on release weekend to use with my iPhone and from day one have been more than satisfied with it.  It doesn't have as many features as some other smart watches, but what it does, it does well.  My primary use is to see caller ID or Text ID when I am driving to know if I need to pull over to answer/return a call or text for work.  This watch eliminates much of the potential distraction that a phone can cause when driving.  No fumbling for the phone in your pocket or on your hip.  The watch connects to the address book in your phone and gives you caller ID.  It will also show you the content of texts.  It actually works with pretty much any notification on your iPhone.Although I have downloaded one or two Apps for the watch, there are few that are well done so far.  Buy the watch for how it interacts with your phone and phone apps, not for any standalone apps.  The couple of fitness apps that I have for my iPhone display well on the Pebble.The watch works over Bluetooth, so your phone battery does drain more quickly when using the watch.  This issue is much less noticeable on the iPhone 5s than it was on the iPhone 5.I am totally satisfied with my purchase of the Pebble.  It is great at what it does, but don't expect hundreds of uses yet.Pros:Works great for notifications.  Never has missed a notification that should have come through.Caller ID checks address book on your phone and displays name of callerCan read iMessages and texts entirely on the watch.Cons:Proprietary charger.  Micro USB would have been easier.Plastic over watch face scratches pretty easily.  Probably like most watches, but this could be improved in future.Pebble Apps are not plentiful yet.

title: Marmot Women's Ama Dablam Jacket
description: The women's Marmot Ama Dablam is named after a Himalayan mountain, and is designed to keep you comfortably warm -- while traveling light -- in just such a setting. The durable down jacket offers maximum warmth with minimum weight, with enough urban style to transition to the city streets.FeaturesLightweight, super-warm down jacket100% polyester DWR ripstop main material100% polyester embossed WR lining800 fill goose down insulationAttached, adjustable down-filled hoodVertical front chest pocket for quick access to small essentialsInside zip stuff sack pocket allows you to stuff jacket into its own pocketElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherZippered handwarmer pocketsAdjustable Velcro and elastic cuffs for comfort and adjustabilityAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion in arms without jacket riding up28.5-inch center back lengthMarmot DownMarmot often says that "down is in our DNA." The company was founded in 1974 as a manufacturer and seller of premium down jackets, vests, and sleeping bags, and continues to use fine quality goose down for its insulated outdoor products. Mountaineers and outdoor enthusiasts the world over rely on Marmot down gear for warmth, comfort, and sometimes survival.Down quality is determined by fill power and durability, which is dependent upon the age and maturity of the bird and the processing of the down. The best down comes from larger, more mature birds and goose down is generally better than duck down. More mature goose down has larger filament clusters than less mature goose down and these clusters, when grouped, provide many more trapped air pockets and therefore provide better insulation. To maximize the effectiveness of the down clusters, proper processing of the down -- sorting, washing, and drying -- is required to open them up.Higher fill power means higher loft, better insulation, lighter weight, and greater durability. Marmot tests all of its down for content, cleanliness, species, and fill power, guaranteeing minimum fill power for all down clothing and sleeping bags.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

reviewText: First of all I'd like to say that the delivery for this item was great! It shipped the day after I ordered it and came in only 4 days, 3 days earlier than it was supposed to. It was in perfect condition and is genuine Vera Bradley. One Little Box (the seller) is a reliable vender, and i got it for $12 cheaper than on the Vera Bradley website (mine was $29.99). This wristlet is extremely cute and very useful. I loved the slot so you don't have to fold bills, unlike in the all -in one wristlet wear you have to fold bills to put them in the wristlet, and the awesome little coin pouch behind the card slots. Very functional! I also personally enjoyed how the id/ license slot was on the inside of the wristlet, because I personally don't like having my photo and information facing out for anyone to see (not photogenic!). I prefer having it inside where I can just as easily open it up and show it when I need to. Now for the phone pocket, this is for SAMSUNG GALAXY S3 users. I have the galaxy s3 and it will not fit with a thick case, it will barely go in and if it does there is a chance you could rip the fabric. Without a case, or with an extremely thin case the phone is slim enough to fit into the pocket pretty easily, BUT it is to tall and the strap is not long enough to fit over the phone and magnetize into the button. I personally fix this problem by simply tucking the strap into the pocket with the phone, because even though it is not long enough to reach the button its supposed to click into, it reaches the top of the pocket so i just tuck it in and that solves the problem for me. Another solution to this problem I found was that you could put your phone into the interior of the wristlet and zip it in. reviewText: Interested in knowing where you are going? How about the current temperature? Are you just the slightest bit interested in what your current altitude may be? GO BUY THIS WATCH! 'Course for those Suunto enthusiasts, this ISN'T a watch, its a Wristop Computer that just so happens to be able to tell time. Unlike the Suunto Observer which is about half the size (and more than a little extra spendy), this baby will do all that and still look great doing it. From the 3 different Suunto models I personally own, I must admit that they make a great wristop computer, or for the picky out there, watch. I mostly use mine to tell simple time, but I must say that as I drive over the mountains up to Montana or over to Oregon and Washington, it IS handy to know a few extra details just by looking down at my wrist. Oh, I almost forgot the barometer! It tracks the barometric pressure and helps you track and even predict the weather! I must say that I haven't been able to figure out the finer points of how to do that just yet, but I AM working on it.
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. reviewText: I really love this watch band. It was the most inexpensive full-metal band I could find, appears to be very quality, hasn't gotten any scratches on it yet, and ultimately appears to be just what I was looking for. If you don't, every time you wash your hands you have to be extra careful not to let water and soap run down your wrists and directly into your iPod ports. The construction of the watch's mounting plate forces you to keep the iPod clipped on a certain way so you have to actually flip the band itself around. Alternatively, if you don't want to have ANY chance of that happening, you can buythese silicon plugsthat go into your ports to keep them shielded when they're not being used. They detract somewhat from the aesthetic appeal of the all-metal body though. reviewText: I got these in the 3" option and am so glad I did. It's the perfect length to go around the bottom of my foot and clip under my ankle bone. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I picked up a pair of these after deciding that I shouldn't wear flip flops while driving. However, these are great for walking. They give an uncanny feeling of being propelled forward with every step, almost as if one is walking downhill. I do feel that I'm using muscles that I normally don't, but I haven't been walking in them for very long. I expect to get used to the feeling. Once they are adjusted, the side snap closure makes them easy to take on and off. They look like they will last for a long time, too.I had never heard of MBT, and came across these by accident while looking for sandals on sale at a large online shoe retailer. I was able to get these for $70, including tax and shipping. I checked other sites, and you shouldn't have to pay more than $100 for them. That's a lot for a sandal, not even counting the $235 price on Amazon, but the fit, comfort, and quality are commensurate with the price. They're definitely worth $70. That figure may have been a mistake, as they were back up to $180 a day later.One reviewer mentioned a seam in the middle of the rear strap. This must be referring to a different model, as mine has a single piece of material with no seam, and nothing on it other than the label. I've owned other sport sandals that made my feet bleed from how the straps cut into them, but these are extremely comfortable, even barefoot. In shoes, I wear a size 11 EEE, so since these sandals come in only one width, I had to go up to size 12. The front strap is elastic and despite the adjustment, if you have wide feet, a smaller size can be too tight.Be aware that this design is intended for walking, not standing. The convex sole works great as long as you're moving; once you come to a stop, there's no flat surface to stand on. You either want to roll back onto your heels or forward onto your toes - the place in the middle where your feet would be level is unstable. The design isn't appropriate for anyone who is on their feet all day, unless they're moving continually. It would work for a mail carrier, but not a cashier.Highly recommended if you can get them for a reasonable price.

description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: This is your standard rubberized outdoor watch. It seems to be able to handle some moisture well (ie., sweat from running as well as precipitation during games).It is multi-function, but in practice you're not going to use all the fancy features when you're on the field.The watch claims to have a beeper, but mine never makes any noise (thankfully! I don't want my soccer watch to beep). However, the documentation says it's supposed to beep (maybe with an option to turn the beeping off), so it just casts doubts on the overall quality of the device if the documentation & the product don't match up.The LED isn't very bright, but I haven't ever needed it - I don't use the watch for anything but refereeing and you don't play without lights now do you? However if you wanted the light at other times you'd probably be disappointed with it.It is relatively easy to read the watch when I'm on the field, and the buttons have to be firmly pressed to start & stop the timer, so I haven't yet had a case where the timer has accidentally started or stopped on me.The soccer timer works well - it resets to 45:00 when you hold the timer button down for a second, otherwise the timer button starts the countdown. When it hits 00:00 it starts counting back up so you can see how much added time has been played. The watch comes with a 2nd "added time" timer, that you use whenever there's any play stoppage on the field for which you will add time at the end of the half. The theory is, any time you think you're in a situation that calls for time to be added, you trigger this 2nd timer to count up, then when you get near the end of the half you can look at your watch and see "oh! that's 2:37 of time we've wasted, so I'll add 2 or 3 minutes of added time to the game." Whether or not you use the 2nd timer is up to you, but it's nice to know it's there.This watch is functional but not stellar - surely there has to be a better ref's watch out there? I'm giving this watch 3 stars out of 5 due to the shortcomings I've mentioned above.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: An awesome watch. From looks to function, this watch is a must for you outdoorsy people. Got mine from the seller OUTSIDE24, who shipped and packaged the watch excellently. Right out of the box, this watch glows, and your wrist begs to get this watch on it. Fits a variety of different wrist sizes, my wrist is on the slimmer side, and this watch has no problem fitting it. Setting it up was so easy, a caveman could do it. I was a bit skeptical buying it at first due to some of the reviews I've read, so let me go over some problems that I've heard that other people have had.The compass: From many reviews, I've heard that it's not dead on accurate, but for me that's ok. I'm not in the military or anything where accuracy is needed. After testing it, that assessment is correct, it's off by a few degrees, so for those of you who NEED accuracy, the compass on this might not be for you. Easy to calibrate, but not clearly told on the instructions. Go to Suunto's YouTube channel where they show you how to calibrate it.Altimiter/Barometer: Also not dead on accurate. Always a bit off, but considering this is a watch, the fact that thsi function is even on there is nice.The bezel: Many people have said it scratches up easily and that it's the most fragile area. Due to it being made from plastic, it is the most fragile. I wouldn't agree with the fact that it scratches up easily, just be careful with it. I've banged it up already a few times (got this watch 2/7/2014, ordered 2/5/2014), and no scratches. The overall build of this watch is exceptional and as long as you're not careless, this should last a while.Rubber strap: Looking at the build of it, it seems that with time, the rubber will start to age and crack. Many reviews say that you have to replace it after 1-2 years, and looking at it, that looks like it's the case.Visuals: A lot of people have been saying that it's hard to see the time on the watch sometimes, and that they need to shine it under a flashlight to see it in the dark. In the sun or even low light, it's honestly not that hard to see the time, you just have to angle the watch right. The light is also bright enough to see the time in complete darkness, I know there has been complaints about how the light is not bright enough. The light, however, is a bit glitchy. When I'm on compass mode with the light on, the light blinks on and off. Might be a battery issue.Overall, this watch is great and looks sick as hell. Although it's not dead accurate, it's a great watch to have.
title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I bought this watch mostly for long range rifle shooting.  It has every environmental input I need except wind speed/direction.  The temperature is off (usually 8-10 deg high), but my anemometer that I use to get the wind speed gives accurate temperature.  So that was not a problem to me.  Below I rated each feature 1-10:CLOCK  - 10: it works.2ND CLOCK  - 10: cool feature, especially if you travel to different time zones from home.TIMER  - 10: convenient compared to using a chronograph backwards.CHRONO  - 10: works as advertised.ALARM  - 10: works as advertised.WEATHER  - 8: cool feature and as accurate as a watch can be, I'd still check the weather channel though.THERMO  - 2: don't buy for this feature.  I guess it gives you a ball park idea of the temperature.ALTIMETER  - 9: big buying point for me and is pretty accurate.  It changes +/- 2-5 feet from day to day standing in the same spot in my house.  But 2-5 feet isn't a big deal.ALT TRACKER- 9: cool/useful feature (I set it for the altitude I zero'd my rifle at).  Same small problem as the Altimeter.BAROMETER  - 10: I haven't checked the accuracy of it, but it seems to be close.  For my application, I don't care about if it's off as long as it's consistently off (bc I only care about changes in barometric pressure, not the actual value).COMPASS  - 10: VERY accurate.
