reviewText: You may be saying to yourself...why do I need a smart watch when I can just pull out my phone? or...Why should I get a Pebble when there are more fancy smart watches out there?For one, sometimes pulling your phone out can be rude or not allowed. If you are on a date, in a meeting, at work, etc...or your phone may just be in a bag or in another room. The Pebble is also waterproof, which means you can swim with it, you can shower with it. What other way can you say you can read texts in the shower? You can also use the music controls to change songs if your phone is hooked up to a stereo or dock remotely, and with third-party apps you can adjust the volume as well. I also find that the vibration on the watch is always noticable, whereas sometimes moving around a lot you can't feel a phone vibrate in your pocket.The e-paper display means you won't need to be charging it by the end of the day like color-screen smart watches, and it only needs a charge every 5-7 days. Of course if you have a lot of third-party apps, you may not get quite as much so keep that in mind. The e-paper display also means that your watch face will always be there, unlike other smart watches that auto-shutoff to conserve battery. What's the point of wearing a watch with a blank screen? Another point about the battery is that I now silence and disable vibrate on my phone and rely solely on my watch for notifications now, which means I'm saving a little battery on my phone, surely enough to make up for the 5-10% battery usage that the bluetooth connection draws in a day.Along with multiple color Pebble watches, there are countless watch face designs to suit everybody: digital, analog, modern, classic, abstract, video game themed, etc and they install in a snap.By default you can read sms, email, phone call, Facebook, Google Talk/Hangouts, and calendar notifications, but with third-party apps you can get every notification from any app on your phone and with texts you can even send customized preset texts back. You can control music, and with third-party apps also volume and more music providers. There are also other apps for weather stocks, and more and half the fun is discovering them and tweaking everything.The fact that it's only $150 dollars doesn't hurt either. And BEWARE of people looking to take advantage of you. The Pebble is sold out on the official website but Best Buy has a TON of them. Don't give these people twice what the watch is worth, just head to your local Best Buy!The one thing I will say is that if you have an iPhone...you may want to pass on the Pebble. The iPhone is just not as compatible like Android phones are and you'll find you are missing some features and compatibility.

title: Marmot Women's Ama Dablam Jacket
description: The women's Marmot Ama Dablam is named after a Himalayan mountain, and is designed to keep you comfortably warm -- while traveling light -- in just such a setting. The durable down jacket offers maximum warmth with minimum weight, with enough urban style to transition to the city streets.FeaturesLightweight, super-warm down jacket100% polyester DWR ripstop main material100% polyester embossed WR lining800 fill goose down insulationAttached, adjustable down-filled hoodVertical front chest pocket for quick access to small essentialsInside zip stuff sack pocket allows you to stuff jacket into its own pocketElastic draw cord hem for adjustability in serious weatherZippered handwarmer pocketsAdjustable Velcro and elastic cuffs for comfort and adjustabilityAngel-Wing Movement allows full range of motion in arms without jacket riding up28.5-inch center back lengthMarmot DownMarmot often says that "down is in our DNA." The company was founded in 1974 as a manufacturer and seller of premium down jackets, vests, and sleeping bags, and continues to use fine quality goose down for its insulated outdoor products. Mountaineers and outdoor enthusiasts the world over rely on Marmot down gear for warmth, comfort, and sometimes survival.Down quality is determined by fill power and durability, which is dependent upon the age and maturity of the bird and the processing of the down. The best down comes from larger, more mature birds and goose down is generally better than duck down. More mature goose down has larger filament clusters than less mature goose down and these clusters, when grouped, provide many more trapped air pockets and therefore provide better insulation. To maximize the effectiveness of the down clusters, proper processing of the down -- sorting, washing, and drying -- is required to open them up.Higher fill power means higher loft, better insulation, lighter weight, and greater durability. Marmot tests all of its down for content, cleanliness, species, and fill power, guaranteeing minimum fill power for all down clothing and sleeping bags.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, "very puffy jackets" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

Hemp is also a "greener" product as it requires no pesticides, which would be a drawing point in the ever-increasing consciousness of natural, eco-friendly alternatives to petro-fabrics. It would also be great if you could offer your (hemp) pants in some sort of patterned design that hides inevitable stains, perhaps like a digital camo, rather than solid colors (I don't think I'm ready for tie-dyed work pants, though... :o)The quality of your pants is high, I'd just like to encourage you think a little further outside of the box in the materials, colors and pattern departments.~~~~~~~~~~~~I called the U.S. customer service line for Blaklader just after sending the above note to them, to ask about some features I was unfamiliar with.  When I introduced myself to the rep she recognized my name and said that she was just reading my email (so they actually do read emails!) She was friendly and knowledgeable enough about the pants to answer my questions (pertaining to a steel button and extra loop on the right leg, which is made for fastening and securing a special utility knife used in Sweden, which features have been phased out of the current U.S. versions of these pants... I'm sure sheetrock dust would contrast well with the black as well. Just something to be aware of, as everyone else will be, too.UPDATE: July 2013After over two years of use the knee pad pockets finally wore through and there is a minor bit of fabric wear above the knees. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Sad to say I'm getting older.  My eyes aren't great.  My memory is less than it once was.  My patience for technology is limited.  Sorry to take away any "cool factor,"  but this is the most practical everyday watch for me.  The display is large and clear, including the date.  The back light button is big and right in the middle of the watch.  The Indiglo back lighting is excellent.  The controls are clearly marked and intuitive.  Unless I intend to go really deep sea diving (I don't), the water resistance insures I can be absent minded and do dishes or jump in the shower while wearing my watch and it will work.  The velcro strap is easier to manipulate than a standard buckle.  I am a thin man, so I'm very happy this isn't an overly thick and/or wide watch, which would look ridiculous on my small wrists.  Still, it's clearly a men's watch.  Finally, it's a fairly inexpensive watch, so I don't fuss over it getting a little banged up.OK, two notes worth considering:  First, the crystal does get easily scratched and scuffed, which can ruin the display.  This could easily be a deal-breaker for people.  I don't mind, because the scratches are easily buffed out with some polishing compound.  Second, with heavy use, the velcro on the strap will wear out fairly quickly.  Mine lasted about a year.  It wore out before the battery.  A replacement strap is, maybe $7-$10.  Again, I don't mind, but remember $10 is about a quarter to a third of the price of the watch, so it's something which should give a consumer pause.It's not the best looking watch.  It's not cool. It's not fashionable.  It just gets the job done better and more affordably than any other watch I've ever owned.

description: The original Neoprene Eyewear Retainer -- patented in 1978 -- remains one of Croakies' most popular models. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. The accuracy is only as good as your calibration.  As long as your pace is consistent with the pace you calibrated it at.  If you run faster than the pace you calibrated it will record a slightly shorter distance whereas if you run slower than your calibrated pace it will record a slightly longer distance that what you actually ran.  It will get you in the ballpark though.The biggest draw backs are the absence of a light to help with night runs and the fact that it is not water proof although it is water resistant.Good Job Nike and thank you for the wonderful customer support I received over the phone this morning.

reviewText: Here's what you get when you buy a watch designed by guys who never actually refereed.  This thing is somewhere between awkward and stupid in it's design.  It counts down ONLY, not up.  Kind of counterintuitive to the game of soccer.  It has a LOUD alarm that goes off for the final 15 seconds of any period you're timing.  Plenty of time for every player on the field to hear it and turn to you and yell "end the game already!"  So much for adding extra time.  Oh but then a second timer goes off and counts UP - for extra time only.It is not easy to program.  Took me weeks of carrying the instructions around in my bag.  Never did figure out how to make the backlight go on, which was more than a small problem reffing at night.  And, minor but SO annoying, for some reason the start button is NOT in the upper right.  It's in the upper left, unlike any other stopwatch I've ever used, which means you have to reach your hand over the face of the watch to stop and start it, blocking your view.But best of all - I purchased this watch in April of 2013.  Return warrantee ended May of 2013.  It is now December 2013 and the watch is DEAD.  Took it to a watch shop to replace the battery, and they informed me that it was not the battery; the watch is defective.  Well it is now a defective piece of junk cluttering up the bottom of my referee bag.  I'll wear it as my backup watch this weekend hoping that none notices one of my watches doesn't work, and I'll rely, as usual, on the trusty Timex on my other wrist to do a proper job of keeping time until I have time to replace this waste of money.

reviewText: I've had this watch for 2yrs+ now and have just changed the (user serviceable) battery for the first time, as the compass had stopped working.  This is to be expected as it uses more power than the other functions (but it does have auto-off in the compass mode after a time to save energy).  There is no bubble level on this model as it has a mineral crystal glass instead of the usual plastic.  I have knocked this watch so many times against things and there are many surface 'threads' you can see given the right light, but no truly visible damage, like big gouges or cracks like the plastic would show.  The logbook feature is a great asset.  Based on a rolling record (oldest record deleted when the memory becomes full), the logbook records Altitude and can be set to different sample rates (e.g. depending on whether you are walking, climbing, driving, etc.) and includes a record of greatest height.  The logbook cannot be deleted (but as stated records over itself) but the max height can be reset independantly.  The backlight is a little dim, but fine to keep your night vision, and the temperature does not compensate for being on or off your wrist (like some Casio models can).  For a large watch (you won't lose it!) it is quite lightweight, with an aluminium case and carbon shell it also looks great.  The new Ti models do not have the same clarity of display though so I would say stick to this screen size, but maybe get the heart rate monitor (HRM) model if you also exercise (cycle, etc) - it's only a small premium and it *is* a Polar model!  I imagine the batteries might last less time due to the HRM receiver, but this at least is user-serviceable (and retains the watches environmental integrity, unlike changing a Casio battery).  The only sad thing is the screenprinted/anodised(?) graphics for the points of the compass rose are wearing off - Suunto take note, laser etch/engrave them next time!!  Sighting grooves in the bezel would be useful too, for taking bearings, but at least the bezel stays smooth as silk on this model as it has ball bearing detents rather than the friction-based ring the plastic housings have which stiffen up so you can't use them.A few minor details aside (like a strap not long enough to go over your coat - just get an velcro Animal strap - and the print wearing off, and maybe the price), this is a cracking product, rated up there with the Garmin eTrex Legend GPS :-)If you want a barometer, altimeter, compass, thermo & HRM in a decent, reliable, user-friendly package, this is it!
summary: Reliable, rugged, clear and easy to use
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Casio has been making similar watches for a long time. They have not listened to the complaints about the wristband pins coming loose. The rubber wristband suggests a water resistant watch, but none of the current batch are listed as such at the Casio web site- and the rubber band just looks & feels cheap. Some still have problems with lettering rubbing off. Casio has made only (and few) trivial changes over the decades. After what Apple did to the cell phone industry you would think that Casio would want to move quickly into the 21st century. An iWatch would crush Casio Databank sales.But if you want info on your wrist today what other options are there? I've been generally happy with mine over many years. I swim & shower with them (though I'm not sure if that is possible with the new one I'm going to buy). The glass crystal on my last one has only one tiny scratch while the plastic case is pretty beat up. I can still read all the printing on my old 300. The protected memory becomes very important when you have a lot stored in there. My 300 was waterproof until I changed the battery the second time. The rubber seal loses its shape and probably should be replaced and lubricated with each battery change.I agree with another reviewer that the weekly reminders at the top of the window are a waste of real estate- the important info should be much larger and easier to read. And why are they still using the crude seven segment display characters when we've had proper LCD displays available for decades? Information could be presented with more flexibility on a high res display.I recently purchased a similar Casio model which has no name- it is simply called 'Module No. 2888'. It has calculator and a bigger display of useful information and a 10yr battery life but it has many flaws- not water resistant, plastic crystal that will scratch badly, no alphabetic input buttons... I will return it and buy another 300 model unless Apple produces an iWatch in the next few days.Here's a tip: switch immediately to a twistoflex type wristband for your Databank. I believe that occasional pulling stress on the (unflexible) rubber band weakens the holes that hold the pins. My Speidel band has been on all my Casios for around 25 years and the pinholes are in good shape. The alternative is to set the original rubber band very loose which you may find uncomfortable.

reviewText: This is my first pocket watch. After extensive review I decided on this one (I love the two-tone). The watch has a solid feel to it. It looks nice and gets plenty of compliments. Mechanically the watch is sound. For mechanicals/price you cannot beat the movement on this watch. The old railroad watches were required to keep time within 30 seconds per week; this does not meet that standard, never-the-less, it does keep good time; on the order of 5 to 8 seconds per day. If you think that is bad, please note that that equates to a 99.98% accuracy (rounded to the hundredths). I am a stickler on watch accuracy, but owning a mechanical that keeps time to within +/- 1 minute PER WEEK has a sense of pride to it that a typical quartz cannot produce.I highly recommend this watch to anyone with a pallet for both character, and personal nostalgia.

reviewText: I got this watch as more of a dressy/stylish type watch. The quality of this Wenger watch is even better than I was expecting. It comes with a nice leather strap. The face and details all add up to an attractive Swiss Made watch. I would not really consider it "rugged" or a watch the I would "swim, bike" with as the other reviewer mentions. That would ruin the leather strap and the shiny silver surfaces would scratch easily under any type of rugged conditions. This is a very nice casual/dress watch for about $100.My one major complaint about this watch, why it did not get 5 stars, is the glow paint used. I also wear Luminox watches which are real sport watches that are made to stand up to rugged use. Luminox uses a glow material that is made to last and will glow bright under any circumstance, like night sights on a gun, making it easy to read at night. This watch uses a thin layer of light activated glow paint that needs to be exposed to light before it will glow and does not even last long enough to make it through one evening. This is the one major drawback. It can make it very difficult to read at night. You can hold the watch right under a bright lamp and it will glow brightly but only 10 minutes later it dims to a point that is unreadable if you are in a dark bar/club. The Luminox watches, you do not have to worry about this, they will always glow bright. This is more of a stylish watch and is very attractive but -1 star for using cheap/thin glow in the dark paint that does not retain light long enough to last through the evening.Other than that, I would definitely recommend this watch if you are looking for something nice to wear, made by a quality Swiss company, but don't want to spend much money. If you are looking for a rugged sport watch, I would recommendLuminox Men's 3001 Original Navy SEAL Dive Watch

description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). reviewText: It seems like every time I need (or want) a new watch, and, I try to sort through different brands, I always end up with Nixon.  They're reliable, fair priced (for the quality) and just damn good looking watches.  This one in particular model is really cool, with just enough features to keep it sensible, and not over burdened with buttons and functions that a normal person in normal situations would have their head explode.  If I had to complain about one thing, however, it would be the temperature gauge.  It is not going to read the exact same temperature as your house thermometer; it will probably show about 8 - 10 degrees higher (or lower at times) because of your body temperature added in.  the manufacturer suggests taking it off and let it sit in it's surroundings for about 10 to 20 minutes to adjust - sorry, but I'm not going through all that every time I have to move from one location to another.  This particular feature is merely a luxury to me, and, I could live with out it and still enjoy this watch.When I visited Nixon's website to do further research on this model, it had the watch listed in both the men's and women's category (much like some of their other watches).  When I was shopping this watch around, some sites had it listed as strictly a woman's, while others had it listed as a man's.  I would say it should be categorized as unisex (maybe)?  I know it is the smaller version of The Unit (being that I have slightly thinner wrists than the average guy, which is why I decided to give this one a shot);  let me tell you - it looks just like any other man's watch (as far as thickness and size).  And, just like the previous Nixon watches I've owned, fits just how I like it.All in all; you can't go wrong with Nixon.

reviewText: Timex is known for affordability and quality so I was looking forward to trying the Ironman Road Trainer. But as much as I wanted to love the Timex T5K722F5 heart rate monitor I feel it has a lot of drawbacks.As noted in the product description this is a strap on heart rate monitor. It includes a black strap, pink watch and thick instructional booklet. The first issue I found was with the strap. Other resin Timex watches have a soft feel to them but this one is stiff making it harder to strap on and to unstrap.The booklet it comes with tells you how to workout within your optimal heart rate, however, it does not tell you what that heart rate should be. Instead it tells you to refer to another online digital booklet to get this information. It shares this at the beginning of the book under resources and that section was easy to miss. In fact, I did miss it and had to thru the book several times to figure out where to find this information. This should have been included in the booklet.Next the Ironman does not share calories burned. It simply gives your heart rate and beeps if you go over or under. This would be fine if the unit was simple to operate but it is not.  I also did not feel the light up "indiglo" feature worked well. Sometimes it lit up when pressed, other times it did not. And when it did light up the face was hard to read. The buttons to set the watch were hard to press.As a watch, the Ironman's face (when not lit) is very clear and easy to read so it does get a big plus for that. And though I prefer black others will love the hot pink Ironman strap.Overall, I feel there are better choices for a heart rate monitor with more features at this price point.

reviewText: As other reviewers noted, the "adjustable tap shoes" are NOT adjustable, and they are so loose that they pose a hazard to little tap pupils. The elastic which is meant to hold the tap shoe onto a child's regular shoe is`sewn in such a way that makes it impossible to shorten the shoe for the snug fit necessary for safe tapping. The shoes made it hard for my 5-year-old to follow along because they kept flopping off, and after we nearly had a disastrous spill I tossed the shoes.As for the video, it seems the camera person kept forgetting that kids would need to see the dancers' feet rather than their smiling faces in order to follow along. And though Bella is cheerful and a great tap dancer, she only VERY briefly demonstrates the basic steps and provides almost no commentary.  Most of the video is filled with corny segments with the rest of the cast (including an odd animated pair of tap shoes who block the video profiling famous dancers) and a couple of dances which moved too quickly for my daughter to really figure out what she was supposed to be doing.  Perhaps if she watches the video a number of times she will get it - the problem is she doesn't seem that interested in watching it again.I really wanted to like this video, but there just isn't enough content that explains or shows exactly how to tap along with Bella.  No wonder it was so cheap!

title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: The FEATURES of this watch are great, which is why I've bought several of them.  HOWEVER, like "clockwork," (pardon the pun) this watch breaks after 11 months.  The center button that turns on the Indiglo light and turns off the alarm stops working.You might think I just got a bad model.  It happens.  HOWEVER, every single Expedition I have purchased has had the Indiglo button go bad after 11 months.  Just how foolish am I?  I've purchased 5 of these things.  EVERY SINGLE ONE has had the button go bad after 11 months.  Shame on me for being so gullible as to buy 5 of these.  I've essentially paid $150 for a $30 watch.Forget about getting any service from Timex.  By the time you've paid for shipping and repair, you could just buy a new one.  (which I did, 5 times)  Alas, the FEATURES and design of the watch are great, just what I wanted, but SHAME ON TIMEX for intentionally building obsolescence into a watch that COULD have been a great value and recommendation for the company.  Instead, Timex has abandoned their old mantra of "takes a licking and keeps on ticking" and replaced it with poor service and the intention of bilking their customers.Soon I will be making a video of my shameful watch collection and posting it on youtube.  Amazon should change the purchase price on this watch to a RENTAL price.  Obviously I will be searching for a different, more reliable watch brand that has the same features as the Expedition.Shame, shame.  Ironically, my 90 year old father is still wearing a Timex he purchased in 1960, and it still works.UPDATE: My last one croaked, right on time as usual.  The indiglo light doesn't work, and now there's no sound on the alarm.  Caused me to miss an important meeting.  How is it, that others here haven't had the same problems??  I'm a writer, so I don't mistreat my watches AT ALL.

reviewText: I owned one that I purchased almost two years ago and it was starting to look worn and I decided I needed another purse as I like them to look nice.  I really love this purse, people (who do not know it is a concealed carry purse) have complimented me on it several times and a woman who usually carries a Coach bag even asked where I bought it.  It is roomy, has an outer zipper compartment for a cell phone and car keys.  The concealed carry area is good for my Ruger SR22.  I like that you can move the holster and it has Velcro so it can sit exactly right and you can move it for left handed (me) or right handed quick action.  If you are alone in a parking lot at night heading towards you car, it is a comfort to just unzip that compartment rest my hand in there while I walk to the car.  There was a car jacking in the mall near us and one in the supermarket parking lot where I shop in the last couple of years.  You just never know.  I like to carry when I am at the bank as well, as there truly are bank robberies, though the ones in my area have all ended peacefully with no shootings.I like the feeling of having my firearm concealed with me.  I wish the purse wasn't quite so heavy, but that is mainly what I keep in it instead of the purse itself.I now own my 2nd one, in the exact same color and style.  I hope they continue to make this one as I'll probably need another in a few years.  The color is a good one, neither too light or too dark, so I don't feel I need a summer vs. winter purse.  I am donating my old purse to the NRA trainer who taught me how to shoot and worked with my family on personal safety.  I had this purse with me when he trained us and he trained with me how to use this while the boys in the family worked with holsters and other concealed carry methods.  His eyes lit up when he saw this and he was delighted with it too and said he was going to have to tell his female clients about this purse.  Now, he will have a demo one to use for training.This works well for me and I hope I never have to use my Ruger on anyone, anywhere, but I am prepared and thankful for this purse that is always over my shoulder.  I would take someone completely by surprise, I'd say, as no one would ever suspect this purse to have my firearm inside.  I have confidence that I wouldn't be the unarmed victim in a mass shooting, I would be able to at least have a chance to save myself, loved ones or children.  There are crazy people out there and those of us who have CC permits might be the only thing between a lunatic and everyone else's lives.  I highly recommend this.

reviewText: After a few years of not having a watch, I began searching for a watch that met my visual and feature requirements.  This Timex T48042 watch fits my desires perfectly.The watch screen is large enough to easily read, and the layout of it is also very good.  It shows the time in large digits, while also displaying the day and the date in smaller digits.  It has a stopwatch/lap function with a 99+ lap function.  When the 99th lap is reached, the lap counter resets to 0, but the timer continues to time accordingly.  It has a large "Indiglo" button directly below the screen which provides ample light in darkness to read the entire screen with ease.The watch band is very comfortable and has 9 holes for fitting.  The inside of the band (the part that touches the wrist) has a very soft material, I'm guessing that it is nylon according to the product description, stitched to it, which makes the watch quite comfortable.  The outside of the band is a combination of brown leather and black nylon, which gives it a very nice look and feel to it.  The watch head is a forest green and the buttons are a greenish-tan color.  Overall, the colors work beautiful together and was one of the reasons I was attracted to this watch.The watch is not waterproof, but it is water resistant to approximately 100m.  So be careful if getting near water with this watch as water may manage to get inside the watch.  I have not has any problem, but I am relatively careful when near water with this watch.I, personally, have not found any cons or problems with this watch.  It is well built and should last quite a while if taken care of.Overall, I am very satisfied with this watch.  The functionality, colors, and feel work very well together, and it is a pleasure to own and wear.  I fully recommend this watch.

reviewText: This is a great watch.  I had never heard of Sartego watches when I bought this watch so it was a bit of a leap of faith; but everything else about it said buy it and now I'm glad I did.Firstly, the watch was just what I was looking for: simple, elegant, sleek.  Even dress watches these days tend to be chunky, covered in bezels and chronograph dials. This must be great for mountain climbers and divers but for me it just gets in the way of reading the actual time. This one is simple and uncluttered which makes it easy to see the time.  The one feature it does have on the dial is the day/date calendar, which was a mandatory requirement for me as I find myself using the date feature quite often.Second, it is made of stern stuff.  It has a titanium case and band which combined with its sleekness makes it a really light and comfortable watch to wear.  It also has a sapphire crystal face, which is superior for resisting scratches to the mineral crystal normally used on watches in this price range.Finally, it has one trick up its sleeve which I didn't expect.  The adjustment knob on the side has a thread so you have to unscrew it before pulling it out to change the time. I would never have known how useful this feature was except that my last watch was rendered useless because the adjustment knob kept slipping out by itself, which stops the watch.  A tiny but very clever feature.The only negative is that this watch comes without a battery, so you'll need to buy one as your first order of business. But you'll probably have to take it to the watch guy anyway to fit the band, so it's not so much an inconvenience as a small extra expense.UPDATE: (January 2014) Three years on and unfortunately I had to replace my watch, but I like it so much I bought another exactly the same. It's ultimate demise was due to me somehow smacking it on the edge of my bedside table in a very uncoordinated attempt to catch something falling off the table. This separated the band from the watch body. I could have gotten it repaired but there was another issue that it had developed, which appeared to be a problem with the battery connection. The watch stopped dead for a week, I assumed the battery was flat but when the guy at the shop tested the battery it was fine, and when he reinserted it the watch started ticking fine. Six months go by and the same problem happens again, with the same fix. So when I totalled it a few months later I decided a new one was in order. Hopefully it was a one off problem. Given the price of the watch I was not unhappy with three years but hopefully the next one lasts for much longer.Also I originally said it doesn't come with a battery. My new watch did, so I guess on my first one it had just died before I got the watch.

reviewText: I purchased my Pebble through the original Kickstarter campaign, so I have had the watch for just about a whole year at this point.I do have to say I really love this watch. It gets a lot of attention, people are constantly asking about it. This isn't a motivator for me really, but it does show there is a real market for smart watches and the Pebble team had great timing.The Good:-The watch is easy to use-It is comfortable on your wrist-Easy to read indoors and out-Decent battery life-the battery usually lasts at least 5 days for me when I forget and let it run out of energyThe Bad:-You do need to remember to charge it-I have had some corrosion where the battery charger attaches, it wasn't too hard to clean it, but this really shouldn't have happened, this may be because I was a VERY early adopter and one would hope the refined manufacturing process would have addressed this by now-A kind of bad/but kindof my fault, I have one scratch on the watch face, which I felt when it happened, Gorilla Glass would be nice!The Could be better:-After a year the Pebble Team have just put out a new version of the software (Winter 2014) that is approaching what was promised upon creation of the project. Having developed software myself, I am sympathetic to how these kinds of projects can take longer than expected, but it sure would have been nice to see it move faster.If you are considering the Pebble, please be aware that it is a device designed to show you information on your wrist and there is no point in getting it you don't have an Android or iPhone to connect with. You can do a few interactions with it directly , but it is really more for showing useful information: one of my favorites is being able to read text-messages on my wrist and not need to reach for my phone unless they need a response.Many people who see it on my wrist ask if it is has a touch screen: no it is not, just the four buttons for interaction.I love the watch, I tend to abuse watches fairly severely and the Pebble has stood up to a fair amount of abuse, other than the single watch face scratch which was my fault, it appears pretty much brand new almost a whole year later! Highly recommended.

Designed specifically for the adult at-risk market, the new Freedom GPS Watch is the only wandering Prevention & Emergency alert solution with both fixed and portable Safe Zones in and outdoors. Freedom allows a high degree of safe independence for those that are prone to wandering (i.e those with Autism & Dementia) while giving caregivers and loved ones greater peace of mind.

Freedom uses both RF (Radio Frequency) and GSM (Cellular) technology to communicate an individual's location.  When the Freedom watch is within RF range of the portable RF Receiver Base, up to 30m indoors or 100m outdoors depending on obstacles, the watch is considered in proximity of the safe zone.  If the Freedom watch and Receiver become separated by exceeding this user-controlled range the watch will then be considered out of proximity of the safe zone.  An alarm will sound on the RF Receiver and the Freedom watch will connect to the GSM cellular network and begin transmitting its position to pre-determined recipients via email and SMS.  While the watch is out of proximity a care giver or loved one can send a "Where Are You" request to the watch by texting "WRU" from their mobile phone.  The system will then respond with a street address, if available, or the wearer's latitude/longitude.  When the watch and receiver are back in proximity the GSM is disabled.

A secure customer portal is available via the internet. Since the Freedom technology involves the use of a hosted mapping site and cellular service, a monthly subscription plan is required.  There are three monthly plans to choose from:

Basic Plan  - $9.99 per month (will transmit email alert notifications only),
Basic Plus Plan  - $19.99 per month (will transmit email and SMS text alerts),
Call Center Plan  - $34.99 per month (includes both alert types as well as a 24/7 HIPPA and e911 Certified central monitoring station).

**First year of basic service is included (a $119.88 value) and can be applied to any plan.

reviewText: This watch is branded after the famous 'Swiss Raid Commando' military competition held annually in Switzerland and France since 1986 of which Wenger is a sponsor. The watch features the SRC logo on the obverse in color along with the French language motto "Vouloir, Croire et Oser", which translates in English to "Want, Believe and Dare". This branding may be important to a special ops soldier, military veteran or collector, but it should be understood that such branding comes with a price premium.PROS:Overall the watch has a heft and feeling of quality and refinement, it should prove quite satisfying for those looking for a unique style military piece. The stainless steel case is coated in black via Physical Vapor Deposition, or PVD which bonds to the steel on a molecular level, meaning no chipping or flaking and high resistance to scratching (as are the crown and two activators). The mineral crystal is slightly domed and without flaws. The screw back is non-coated stainless with the SRC color logo inset at center and encapsulated in what appears to be mineral crystal. On the back is also the lightly etched Wenger logo and specs.*The face of this watch is the draw for many; a large clean, crisp dial in "nuclear green" with three sub-dials in the same hue. The watch is quite readable at most angles although the rather large arrow point hour/minute hands can obscure the sub-dials. If you want something strikingly clean and purposeful, this is it.*The luminance of the dial at night is astonishing! Every detail is visible in the dark after just a couple hours of sun. If the watch is exposed to sun (even overcast, winter skies in the Northeast US) it will be visible throughout the darkest, moonless nights. I have never owned a watch with this ability.*The rubber(*) strap is substantial and comfortable.*The 30 minute/12 hour chronograph is intuitive and accurate. The lap time feature is easy to use.CONS:You can easily buy a watch with the same quality and more functions for less money. Without the SRC branding, unique style dial and Swiss caveat this watch would be priced $100 less.*I am a fan of the accuracy of battery-quartz watches, but there is no excuse for selling one at this price point without a solar recharging system similar to Citizen's Eco-Drive. I purchased this Wenger despite the fact that one day in the near future I know it will stop working and I will have to take it to a jeweler for an expensive battery replacement/resealing. The Japanese have figured out how to do this, why haven't the Swiss?*Lacking a screw down crown and only certified to 10atm is a bit lackluster for a $220+ watch branded to a rigorous military competition. I would be highly dubious of jumping into a lake or snorkeling with a watch lacking a screw-down crown. I own two Citizens (one titanium) rated to 20atm with the same features plus solar and screw crowns costing $100 less. Once again, the Swiss need to catch up.*The crystal is neither sapphire nor non-reflective, add to that its slight dome and I wonder how long before an unsightly scratch? A rugged military time piece of this price should have a sapphire crystal.*While the rubber(*) band is comfortable and thick, it's also quite gummy. Time will tell how durable it is but it seems as though if pulled too hard over time it might harden and separate. Once again I feel a military branded piece such as this should have been given a more durable band.SUM UP:While this Wenger is a quality watch and has some collector appeal, its main selling point is appearance, not function or economy. There are dozens of watches which perform the same functions with similar or better quality at a much lower cost. But if you're a sucker for a striking "nuclear green" on black watch which will perform perfectly until the battery runs out, then you'll buy one just as I have and enjoy it in the dark!(*)It is unclear whether the band material on this watch is organic rubber or silicone rubber. The Wenger site states that the band of this watch is "rubber" while using the term "silicon" for bands on other watches. This is an important distinction and one which Wenger should clear up.

reviewText: I researched ABC watches to no end to make sure I got what I wanted. If this watch had a depth guage that worked to scuba dive depths, it would really be the perfect outdoor enthusiasts watch.That said, I did buy the early s/n watch and as expected, had the typical problems. I bought it in November '08 and summer of '10 it started eating batteries every week or so. Luckily I saved my receipt. A week and a half after sending this watch in, a brand new unit was on my door, no questions asked from Suunto, not a dime out of pocket so congrats on the good customer service Suunto. Oh, my bezel fell off on a scuba dive too. I've had this watch to about 105' several times and no problems with that.My band also broke after a year or so. $12 gets you a new one at any department store so no big deal.For those of you that are looking for the perfect outdoor enthusiasts watch, check out the Citizen Aquamount. Out of production, but it has all that and a depth guage.Storm alarm works great which is actually one of the biggest reasons I bought this watch. Tired of going to sleep  under the stars to wake up in the rain without the tent set up.Compass saved my butt in the fog while elk hunting in the cascades. I wouldn't call it a life saver, but at least I got to sleep in my tent that night.Overall very happy with the watch while it worked and I'm excited to get a brand new watch two years after the fact.As far as digital ABC watches go, it's either this or the Suunto Observer, or the ani-dig Tissot ABC Touch, or like I said, the Citizen Aquamount which I would probably try to buy first. My Core goes scuba diving, dirt biking, mountain biking, hunting, fishing, backpacking and overhauls my house and has held up pretty well. Overall a very good purchase.

description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. Also features a digital thermometer. Menu-based user interface in English, German, French and Spanish. 2 year warranty.

reviewText: I've had this watch for around 5-6 months. My previous watch, a Timex, lasted a few years but eventually died due to water seal failure. I can't yet comment on the long-term durability of this watch as I haven't used it much in water/outdoors. Anyway, here's the rundown:Hardware- Very cool, perhaps even futuristic-looking body and digits. Main reason why I bought it and I'm satisfied with it.- Color is nice and looks almost identical to the picture, although the strap is slightly darker than shown.- Strap is hard but not stiff. It takes a little getting used to and if worn super tight the buckle will bite into skin. So I wear it looser, and it doesn't usually slip.- This is a small watch. Both the strap and face are small. I have a thin wrist so it fits me fine but adults with thicker wrists will have trouble keeping it on.- Button placement is unconventional but I like it. My gripe with the buttons in that the top and bottom buttons -- start/stop and lap, respectively -- are difficult to push. These are used for other functions, namely cycling through hour/minute so it can be frustrating when setting alarms and such.- The light is possibly my biggest gripe with the watch, second only to the buttons. It's an okay light -- kind of greenish -- but lasts for just two seconds... what!? Massive inconvenience when trying to set up a stopwatch or timer in a dark area. This would not be a good watch to get if you expect to use it in dark locations often.- Good water-resistance, although testing was limited.Software- The watch display is broken into three compartments, designated by two horizontal blue lines. Check out the picture to see what I'm talking about. What this means is that features are displayed in the top two compartments and the time is displayed in the bottom compartment. This is GREAT. So I can be setting my alarm and still know what the current time is. The only section the "universal time" is not displayed is when I'm flipping through pace records (see below).- There are six "sections," if you will. Sections can be navigated by pressing the bottom left button and a beep is heard. When I finish cycling through, a beep of a higher pitch is heard to signify that I've reached the first section. This is a great, subtle feature.- Sections are (in order): Time/Date/Year, Stopwatch, Records, Timer, Alarm, Time (same as first but no date/year)--- Time/Date/Year: What you'd expect. Watch supports both 12-hour and 24-hour. No apparent support for multiple clocks, which is kind of irritating but not a big deal.--- Stopwatch: Noticeable beeps for starting (three fast beeps) and stopping (one long beep) which is nice. There's some kind of lap feature but I haven't used it much.--- Records: I haven't used this at all. I'm not a runner. :) Looks like it saves Stopwatch history and orders it by date. It appears to store a lot of records (28 at least).--- Timer: Your typical timer except seconds can't be set, gah! This is a bizarre and annoying restriction. Other than that the timer is fine.--- Alarm: There are five alarms, which is great. When an alarm is activated a little icon is displayed all throughout the watch. The first (and only first) alarm appears to have a snooze setting, but I haven't used it. The alarm sound is a simple beep rhythm: 2 beeps, pause, 2 beeps, pause, etc. When I had it on while I slept I had trouble hearing it. It's loud enough to be heard normally but it was too quiet when under covers. That was easily fixed when I placed it on a counter beside my bed. My only complaint here is that the alarm lasts for a measly ten seconds.--- Time: Looks like this is just a cosmetic feature for those who don't want a crowded display. Personally I think it's silly.Outstanding Pros- Slick appearance, color; neat button placement.- Time is always visible when browsing through watch.- Stopwatch/records could prove useful if I ever take up running. ;)- Beeps are intelligently designed.- Lots of alarms.Outstanding Cons- Top/bottom buttons difficult to press.- Light duration is a joke.- Can't specify seconds in timer.- Alarm noise could last a little longer.Overall: Great consumer watch for the price. I might be irked if it costed more, but $21 is a steal.Hope this review helped! Let me know if there's anything specific you'd like to look at.

reviewText: Forget the other smarthwatches with cameras and color touchscreens (really? a touchscreen that's barely bigger than your fingertip?), the Pebble is THE smart watch. Designed from the start to blend in rather than stand out, it's waterproof, the battery lasts for a full week, and you use it just like a normal watch, with the buttons on the side.But that's where the similarities end. You can control your phone's music, add custom watchfaces, even read texts and see who's calling. And it's that last part that makes it. I can't tell you how much less I worry about missing a text or call with the Pebble. Before, I'd constantly have to switch my phone between vibrate (for classes) and ring (for walking around and at home). Now, I haven't taken my phone off vibrate since I got the pebble.Plus, smarthwatches are still new enough that they're a great conversation starter. Someone will notice you playing with your watch, do a double take, and then their eyes pop!I'll admit, I would like it if the screen was color and a bit higher resolution - but only if it stays as an e-ink screen. Because that's another benefit - you can still read it in the sun, and if it's dark, all you have to do is flick your wrist to activate the backlight!Overall, I love it. Would buy again!

reviewText: I've had my Kickstarter-edition Pebble working with my iPhone 4S for a few weeks now and can add my two cents.  Overall, I love getting texts and call notifications on my wrist.  I miss far fewer messages than in my pre-Pebble, pocket-vibrating days.  Other reviewers are right, though, that the bluetooth connection between watch and phone occasionally drops and then reconnects (usually when they separate by 25 or more feet and then reunite) and that caller ID with contact names rarely works.  I also love controlling music (play, pause, back one track, forward one track); this was really handy on a road trip recently.  And the ability to change faces is just plain fun.  I appreciate all those creative people out there designing watchfaces.  Thank you!!!  There are few apps available right now; the only one I use is a countdown timer.  Email notifications apparently work for iPhones now (post 8/1/13), but I don't want to be bothered with those.I got the Pebble, though, also to get calendar notifications.  Alas, because all notifications (except for texts and calls) turn off in the event of a disconnection, calendar notifications are not reliable.  You can restart calendar and other app notifications by toggling them off and then back on in "settings->notifications" on an iPhone, but I can't count on knowing when to do this or that I will remember to do it.  This flaw is nearly a deal-killer for me, since I really wanted calendar notifications to work.So why 4 stars?  I have a work-around that suits me just fine.  I use Google Calendar on my laptop and Calendars+ on my iPhone.  Instead of setting event alerts to "pop-up" or "alert," I set them to signal me via SMS.  (In "settings" under the gear in the upper-right corner of your Google Calendar, sign up under "mobile setup" to get SMS via Google.)  This means that my Google Calendar alerts reach me 99% of the time.  The one exception so far has been when the bluetooth connection between watch and phone disconnected and did not reconnect automatically; I don't know what happened.  My solution?  Shut down the watch and turn it back on.Early adopters have to deal with such annoyances, eh?  In a few months or years, perfection will arrive, in the form of either updated firmware from Pebble or a watch from some other maker.  For now, I can say confidently that my Pebble makes life a little better, even with its flaws.
summary: Not perfect but fun and useful, as long as Google Calendar SMS is enabled

reviewText: This is one rugged, handsome, and accurate computer.  I will definitely be investing in another if anything ever happens to this one.
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

title: Timex Ironman Full Size 150-Lap Tap Screen Watch
description: It's no longer enough to train hard; you also have to train smart if you want an edge. Enter the Timex Ironman 150-Lap Sleek watch, which gives you the edge when every second counts. The cutting-edge performance watch allows you to access training information without breaking your stride thanks to the built-in TapScreen technology. Simply give one firm tap on the watch face to log split times, then glance at the oversized display or listen to the audible alarms to receive real-time performance feedback. The watch provides dated training logs for your most recent runs, recording your best lap time, average lap time, and total time. The watch also offers a 100-hour chronograph with lap and split times, along with a 150-lap memory recall. And that's just the start of the watch's built-in training features, which also include a target time pacer, on-the-fly lap or split recalls, a 199-lap counter, 16 interval timers with repeat, hydration and nutrition alarms, and an automatic interval repetition counter.The 150-Lap Sleek offers non-training functions, too, with three daily, weekly, weekday, or weekend alarms, a 24-hour time display, and month, day, and date displays. And the watch couldn't be easier to use thanks to the intuitive onscreen prompts. description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: I did not have the bad luck that the other reviewer had. The magnetic charger is pretty cool and the battery life on the one I have is great.The thing that I like the most is while in a meeting or driving the watch displays who is calling or the first several lines of a text.  It's easier glancing quickly at your wrist than to pull the phone out of course (esp while driving).The iOS app selection does need to grow (Pebble said their developers are hard at work on that, but they need to move quickly before the other smartwatch developers launch their products).  I do have an iPhone and I believe there are more available for Android phones.  This is an open-source device, so there is some great potential here for programmers - and it is understandable if Android apps have taken the lead.I will spend a few bucks on a new wristband.  This one is good enough, just a little too utilitarian for my taste.  The watch has been catching attention (not a reason to buy it but it's a conversation starter as they say).

description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. Also features a digital thermometer. Menu-based user interface in English, German, French and Spanish. 2 year warranty.

reviewText: I have owned a few watches but this one keeps drawing me to wear it. Easy to read fonts, hands and dials.- Intuitive and accurate chrono operation, like a standard stopwatch.- PVD black coating is durable, and semi-matte finish.- Very avant garde style, especially in the business world. I get compliments on it all the time. Military-types love it.- Interesting heritage and tribute model. The symbol on the case back is a nice touch for collectors.- Date display without too much additional information like day of week or month.- Easy to set and maintain. Crown increments are easy to hit for setting.Cons:- Price. As others have indicated, this is a *bit* much for a quartz movement, mineral crystal and non-screw crown. If you can find one for a good price, its good quality though, and worth it.- Mineral domed crystal. Sapphire would have made much more sense as this is a "ruggid" model. The mineral domed crystal also distorts the view at an angle, and produces pretty bad reflection.- Silicon/rubber band. Makes my wrist sweat more than anything else I wear, including steel bracelets and leather. It does seem durable though, and the 2 band end slips are a nice touch.- Non screw-down crown. The Wenger manual that comes with this watch suggests you *not* wear this in a hot shower. That is quite inconsistent with the theme of the whole thing.As others have stated, this watch is about style. If you like it, its good quality and looks great. Not a single problem with it so far, and I keep coming back to it over my more traditional "diver" style watches.UPDATE: I've had this for almost a year now, and I wear is semi-regularly. The band is starting to show signs of wear, in the form of shiny spots. Not a huge deal, but something to be aware of. Time is still accurate, and it is functioning well. Would still buy again .

reviewText: I bought these for working in the barn - cleaning horse stalls, sloshing big water buckets and the like. It's just too hot in the summer to wear traditional boots (at least for me). The Sloggers garden shoes are very comfortable around the house and they are indeed waterproof - that alone makes them a worthwhile purchase. They have a really cushy lining inside. I also like the tread on the bottom of the sole - solid enough to walk in mud and slippery ground without sliding around at all.The ONLY complaint I have and the reason I am leaving a four star rather than five star review is the heel & overall fit. I wear an 8 1/2 normally in sneakers and boots and 9 in high heels, so I ordered the size 9. I figured even if they were a tad wider than needed, socks would make up for the difference. They fit fine with regard to actual measurements. However, with every step the heel is very loose and feels like it's going to slide off my foot. They feel like those backless clogs instead of a solid fitting shoe. The height of the back of the shoe is lower than a traditional shoe and higher than a traditional clog. DROVE ME CRAZY for the first few days and now I've gotten used to it & it's fine. Just a warning though if you need the support of a regular back or heel, then these probably aren't for you.************************UPDATE Oct 2011*********************************************After wearing these Sloggers every single day since I bought them I am still very happy with them. They are indeed waterproof - I stepped in what turned out to be a deep puddle, immersing the shoes to the very top edge. No damage whatsoever inside or out. My foot was dry inside the shoe. I was concerned that every day use would stretch them at the ankle area or it would weaken etc - so far it's just like new. I will buy these Sloggers again in the future for sure!
summary: Very comfy interior linging, solid sole, short heel - UPDATED Oct 2011
