description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

It reduces internal condensation and the chilling effect caused by condensation build-up, and -- when used with insulated garments or sleeping bags -- protects the insulation from harsh weather conditions.Lifetime WarrantyMarmot products include a limited lifetime manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.About MarmotIn April 1971, University of California Santa Cruz students Eric Reynolds and Dave Huntley were in Alaska on the Juneau ice fields for a Glaciology school project. This was where the idea of Marmot, originally a collegiate climbing club, began. Reynolds and Huntley soon began making prototypes of down products such as vests and sleeping bags in their dorm room in Santa Cruz. By the spring of 1973, Reynolds and Huntley partnered with fellow climber Tom Boyce to open a modest rental and retail location, named Marmot Mountain Works, in a 100-year-old building in Grand Junction, Colorado.Their first large order was for 108, as the producer called them, ""very puffy jackets"" for the movie The Eiger Sanction, with Clint Eastwood, which helped make down outerwear fashionable. In 1976, Marmot was one of the first companies to recognize the value of a new technology being developed by W.L. Gore & Associates. Marmot was soon producing waterproof Gore-Tex sleeping bags, with Reynolds and Huntley testing early prototypes by sleeping in meat lockers and under fire sprinklers, and later introduced the waterproof/breathable fabric into nearly all Marmot products.From humble beginnings, Marmot and its product line have grown over the years, and today the company is headquartered in Rohnert Park, California, with offices all over the world and distribution in more than 60 countries.

reviewText: It does what I bought it for, and it does it well, so it gets 3 stars.  I bought this watch so I could wear earplugs and still wake up to an alarm.However, the design is not elegant. However, it doesn't seem like I can accidently hit this button, so it is forgivable, though worrying.An example of the rough design is function of the button that changes vibrate/beep/silence modes.  It has four settings: beep, vibrate, beep&vibrate;, and off.  When cycling through these modes, the watch vibrates & beeps for vibrate & beep mode, BUT ONLY WHEN TURNING THIS MODE OFF!  It would make sense (and I believe this was the intention of the designers) if when you turn on vibrate mode, it vibrates to confirm this.  But it only vibrates to confirm that you have just turned vibrate mode OFF.  Fortunately, there is a visual indicator to indicate the mode, so this is only disappointing, and not disastrous.There are other annoying things that standard digital watches have had right for many years, like:After using a different function (like stopwatch), mode button takes you right back to time display.When I turn on the light, it turns off as soon as I press any button - so forget about trying to set the watch in the dark - EVERY button turns the light off.I'm guess they were first to market with this concept, because I couldn't find any competitors at all.Bottom line, without competition, I would still buy this watch.

reviewText: I have owned three Timex Expedition watches over the last 5 or 6 years and I really like them.  When the display on the latest one decided to let go, I decided to try the Ironman instead.  After a couple of weeks, I have decided I like the Expedition better.A definite "pro" on this watch is the display has excellent contrast and is very easy to read, especially when using the Indiglo backlight.  The opposite is true of the Expedition.Another reviewer complained of overly sensitive buttons, and I have to agree, especially compared again to the Expedition.  The slightest pressure on the buttons will activate them, often causing an annoying change to a different mode or a switch from T1 to T2.  The top button will change T1/T2 when held down, and this will happen even for innocuous actions like putting your hand in your pocket for a few seconds.  On the Expedition, the top button turned on the Indiglo, so it wasn't as big a deal.On the other hand, if you actually use the lap timers, split times, etc. quite often, you might say this is a "pro" as they are very easy to activate while wearing the watch.Switching between the two models can be confusing due to the different button layouts.This is a good watch, but if you are already used to an Expedition model, you might want to stick with that model instead.  I have to ding this one one star for the sensitive buttons.

reviewText: I would not consider myself an avid climber, but I get out fairly often. For what it's worth, I climb v3 and my redpoint is 5.11B (indoors). These shoes are by far the best shoes I have owned! I have a pair of la sportiva's and evolv's climbing shoes but they both pail in comparison. The anasazi VCS's edge like a boss and smear just as well. I went outdoors yesterday and climbed in them all day while only slipping once (which was probably my own fault) because I was trying to clip lower than I should have. Anyway, in order to get these things to perform well you definitely have to size them right. Suck it up and downsize. Is it going to hurt? Yes. I wear and 11.5/12 street shoe size depending on brand and I went with a 9.5 in these suckers. At first I had to wear super slippery, thin socks to even get my heel in them. Then, once I get my heel in I immediately thought I had made a sizing mistake. However, I wore them while I was on my computer and watching TV for about a week and then they felt perfect. If you size them correctly for maximum performance, you should be able to see each individual toe knuckle curled while the shoe is on. Once the initial break in period is over (which trust me, I know, is miserable), you have the best all around climbing shoe that is comfortably uncomfortable (if you are a climber, you know what I mean). They excel remarkably well at sport climbing, trad, and general top roping all while holding their ground on the tough, overhung boulder problems. Can't be beat.

reviewText: I love the shape of this watch, the color, everything. It's wonderful. But.But the wristband is made from some porous plastic which absorbs dirt really easily. After less than a month, the wristband doesn't look okay. It's darkened into a deep blue/black color along the edges and in certain spots. It's all on the underside of the watch (the face is made out of another kind of plastic which doesn't exhibit this absorbing property), so other people can't see it when you wear it- but it still sucks.I'm not sure if it's because of sweat (I don't sweat that much and have never had this problem before), because the watch is rubbing on colored clothes (I tend to mostly wear white cotton shirts so that'd be surprising), because it's rubbing on my desk when I type at a keyboard, or what. Probably a combination of all of that. Regardless, I haven't found any way to clean it out. I've tried soap, rubbing alcohol, etc. - nothing works. It must be really ingrained in the plastic.So, great watch - but keep this in mind. If you read reviews of other colors of that watch, you'll read similar comments (especially on the white one). reviewText: I spend a lot of time with my phone in pockets or bags that can be inconvenient to get to when I get a text, email, or phone call.  I work and play outside a lot, often with gloves, so pulling my phone out every time I hear it chirp or ring is frustrating.  I use a Samsung Galaxy S3, so I looked at the Samsung Gear watch thinking it would be a great tool to have.  After reading reviews, and realizing that it isn't even water resistant, I decided it would not be a good choice, not to mention the price tag.  I also didn't really like the idea of another touchscreen that I couldn't use with gloves very well.  The Pebble seemed to be a good choice for me, seeing that it is waterproof, and not a touch screen.  I wasn't sure the size and style were going to all that desirable, but decided to give it a try.  After opening the package, I realized the size of the watch wasn't going to be a problem.  It is relatively slim, fits well on my wrist (though the band was apparently designed for people with much smaller wrists than mine), and looks good!  I've been wearing an analog dive watch for 7 years, so knowing that I can still use a traditional watch face is nice.  After getting to know the watch now, though, I don't use the analog face anymore, but prefer to use one that conveys much more information than the time.  For those that like to be kept up to date in places where cell phones are frowned upon (school, movie theater, meetings) this thing is great.  It vibrates on your wrist, so if your phone is silenced, or you are snowmobiling, or on a noisy jobsite, you can easily feel the vibration.Some things I like about the Pebble:It's size is quite reasonable for packing so much into it.The buttons are large and easy to use, even with gloves on.The e ink display is very visible in bright sunlightThe backlight turns on with a flick of the wristThere are MANY different apps for the Pebble.At the time I'm writing this, the Android App Store has just (within an hour ago) opened.....hopefully this is a pro.....Battery life seems to be pretty good.  I'm getting three to five days out of a charge, closer to five.I'm rough on things, and the screen has not suffered a single scratch yet.If you don't like the band, you can swap it out with any 22mm band.Couple things I'm not too fond of:It seems to disconnect and connect pretty often, even when sitting a few feet from the phone. I have a suspicion that this has more to do with my phone than the watch, though.I understand the magnetic charger is used to keep the watch waterproof, but it's just one more power cord to keep track of.....The app installation and use is not the most user friendly around, but I get by.Overall, the Pebble is great.  It definitely does everything I was hoping for , and more.  If you are looking for a flashy, colorful, touch screen, this probably isn't the watch you are looking for.  But this thing gets the job done, looks great, and is actually a lot of fun to use.
summary: Great idea, still learning how to properly use it

Additionally, it can be worn with all attires, even fancy (okay maybe not to a black tie wedding, but you get the point.) It doesn't have the typical "sport watch" appearance and therefore works perfectly for everyday wear. However, if you use a watch this frequently, expect it to last only about a year, which is not bad at all considering the low price you pay for it. My watch is no longer water proof, but this only happened after a full year's use. Maybe it would still be water proof had i not swam in the ocean with it, etc. Additionally, the top silver piece has fallen off (in the ocean) but again, that probably isn't a common occurrence. All of the functions still work perfectly. Overall, a great buy, as long as you are aware you will be buying a new one after a year.

reviewText: I wanted a watch with an hourly chime as a reminder of something I need to do every hour (when awake).I first bought an Armitron, but sometimes I hear its chime & other times I do not.  I think if I were trying to hear it at the time of chime,  I wud hear it every time.  But if I am distracted, I don't hear it.  The Armitron is a $20 watch.  This Timex is more expensive.  I sent the Timex back to Amazon because this Timex is not even as loud as the Armitron; however, the Timex's chime is lower in pitch than the Armitron's.  It is a pity that they don't rate the chimes in dB, pitch, and length of ring.On the other hand, the Timex has 3 alarms in it, and the alarms are loud & long.  The Timex has a button to use to stop the alarm.  I don't know how long it wud last if you didn't turn it off.My Mac Computer is set to announce the time every hour:  "It's 23 hours!"  And it is loud (depending on where I set the computer volume).  I am thinking that maybe an iFone or some hand-computer-cell phone would do this (of course all the time reporting where you are to Apple probably).  Maybe someone now makes a wrist watch computer that wud do this.Otherwise, it looks like I have to go to a store & listen to a lot of watches, if I can get the shop keeper to let me do that.  The process cud take a lot of time.So, if I were not wanting this watch for its hourly chime, I might have rated it 5 stars.

reviewText: I bought this watch 5yrs ago as a way to keep up with my newborn twins nightly feedings.  (which, between the indiglo light and the multiple timers worked very well!) The timepiece still worked, so I bought some industrial strength, sticky-backed velcro and a piece of elastic legband from a craft/sewing store.  I cut out a circle of velcro and stuck it to the back of the watch, stuck a matching velcro circle on the band, and then added some velcro to the ends of the wristband so that I could adjust it to fit my wrist.  It's not pretty, and I have to wear the timepiece on the inside of my wrist so that it doesn't catch on anything, but it's worked beautifully for running all year.  This week the battery has finally died (after 5yrs - not bad), so I will probably break down and buy another one.

reviewText: I have purchased many Timex watches over the years and I am entirely satisfied with this watch.  I always buy the sports watch, as I swim and do triathlons.Things I like about the watch:*Setting the watch is easy and the instructions are clear (although the printed instructions are very small!)* The watch is not too big.  So many watches have too many features and they are large, bulky, and heavy.  This watch is sleek, has a low profile, and has a size that is ideal for average needs.* The numbers are big enough to see easily at a glance.* There are enough useful options, and this watch is not overloaded with too many options.  Too many options are confusing to me.  I like the simplicity of this watch and the ease of use of the options it has.* I like the plastic watch band.  I have tried the velcro strap bands and they wear out after a year or so of use.  The plastic band will eventually break, but is fairly easy to replace.* I like the price.  At less than 35 dollars I have everything I need in a watch.* I like and use frequently the Indiglo feature.  I have even used Indiglo to find my way to the bathroom at night from bed! The light on the dial is bright enough to make your way through the dark for a short trip!Things I don't like:There is not much I don't like about this Timex watch.  I suppose my biggest complaint about this watch and any Timex watch is the difficulty in changing the battery.  The battery will eventually need replacement, and of course one has to take off the back of the watch to replace the battery.  This is tricky and takes a steady hand.  I wish Timex would make the battery more accessible so changing the battery would be as easy as sliding one in or out of a hinged door (like on a hearing aid).Obviously, there is much more to like about this watch than not like.  I do recommend it for a good sport watch.  It will withstand chlorine pools, lake water, rainfall, high and low temperatures, but be careful not to scratch the dial window!  I scratched the main window crystal and ruined my last watch.  Avoid spraying any kind of bug repellant on the window as well, as this can mar (dull) the surface.For me, this watch meets all my needs and I give it a 5-star rating.  My needs are faily simple.  There are certainly other watches that offer more features, but to me, the added features add complexity and are not worth the added bother.The price is good.  The watch is good quality. This is a good buy.Jim "Konedog" Koenig

The ends tightly grip your glasses frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.Details12 inches long (each side), with 3.2-millimeter thicknessUV-resistant, molded MIDDI ends fit medium framesTough woven climbing rope with adjustable black bead91% nylon, 6% rubber, and 2% plasticNo contact above earbowWashableMade in the USAAbout CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. They've even been used out of this world, having become standard issue on the Space Shuttle in 1990.

reviewText: Came as expected, but came with dead battery installed.  Was a little worried the strap was defective.  As soon as I got and replaced a new battery, it worked just fine.UPDATE: after 2-3 times use per week on 2-3 hour bike rides for the past couple months since my purchase, I have noticed the heart rate indicating crazy and random heart rates.  I have very in tune with my heart rate at various exertion levels.  When I am doing a light warm up and am in a low heart rate zone- say somewhere in the 130's, I'd glance down to notice the indicator displaying 210.  And what I notice has happened even more often is the heart rate showing extremely low rates- for example, an hour into an intense ride and during a tough part where my heart rate should show the 180's, the strap is sending off 120 readings.  So it's not even close. And I would guess that when I glance down- its probably way off 25% of the time. The 75% of the time that I would consider accurate- its just my guess that it seems like its accurate. Near my max heart rate but not quite there, but lactic acid building, look down and see 170's which sounds right compared to past experience.  But the 25% off is significant. And its made me wonder about the remaining 75% of the time that I think its accurate- maybe its not. I realize that I may have a fluke/dud, as my past strap that came with my watch was always consistent and accurate- very reliable (no random numbers).  I didn't return during this time because I thought the unit would correct itself or I would try various locations and strategies to make it more accurate. But nothing worked.  Now I can't return or exchange, but I would if I could.

reviewText: ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've ordered this and am waiting for shipment to arrive.  But just FYI -- This CORSAIR MODEL NUMBER SHOWN is for "DUAL CHANNEL" MEMORY - not QUAD CHANNEL memory. TheCorsair Model Number for the dual channel memory is as shown in the title - it has a letter A in the model # . . CMZ-16GX3M4"A"1600C9.  The Corsair Model Number for the "quad channel" memory has an X (not an A) in the model number. The title of this listing sounds like they're advertising "quad channel" memory. This model # isn't quad channel.  It's FOUR RAM DIMMS of DUAL CHANNEL MEMORY -- not the same as single vs dual vs quad channel memory -- which is totally different. I've requested Amazon review and change the title if appropriate to their needs for accuracy.UPDATE Jan 2012Well -- I see that Amazon did change the title of this listing. Good. DUAL CHANNEL MEMORY - FOUR DIMMS - 4GB ea!  Now, to report on the use of this memory now that it's been installed for 1.5 months. Obviously, that will depend on the Mobo/CPU combo you have and probably how it fits with your chosen CPU fan/heat sink. Mine is:  Asus P8Z68-VPRO/GEN 3 and a Intel CPU I7-2600K with a Corsair H80 Hydro Series CPU Cooler.THIS MEMORY WORKS PERFECT WITH MY MOBO/CPU/CPU Cooler COMBO!  FAST & COOL! NO space interference at all.The height of the heat spreaders on this Vengeance series RAM are NOT a problem at all with my CPU Cooler.  Zero overlap on the RAM with plenty of room to spare to help keep DIMMS and board cool. In a HAF X, plenty of good air flow. I've read, however, that the spreaders on the RAM can be a problem with other larger types of aftermarket CPU heat sink fans. So, give consideration to this if you're also choosing one of the larger heat sinks that overlaps the RAM slots.  Just FYI -- with the H80 my CPU is still on 13 degrees C in a 67F room and Motherboard is staying around 20C.  So NO complaints here.  Very pleased with how this RAM works with all components of the board, CPU, cooler, etc.ABOUT BIOS: When you install this 1600 RAM on the Asus Z68 boards, it will install at 1300 speed.  This is a function of Intel Chipset, but you can set your RAM to 1600 if you want in the Asus BIOS or using the ASUS utilities. title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

I shopped on amazon for like 5 hours (still get the emails too damn targeted marketing lol) for watches then remembered smart watches were beginning to exist. title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: Aug 20,2013 I lost the watch on an overseas trip, and promptly re-ordered the same watch when I returned.=======July 8, 2013 Editing my original review below from Nov 2012. The watch has been working just fine. I have no problem with "hair trigger" buttons. And so far the band has held up well. So - I strongly recommend this watch, particularly if you need the "weekly" alarm feature.=========================================I've had Timex digital watches for years now, because I like the styling and I need the Countdown Timer and Alarm features. This time I was particularly looking for a version that has the "Weekly" alarm feature, i.e. can be set for a specific day/time (e.g. every Wed at 11:30); this is in addition to the more standard "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends" alarm options. Many watches on the Timex website mistakenly indicate Weekly when you first look at the descriptions, but on the downloaded PDFs, they says only "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends", and not "Weekly". Some of these watches are similarly incorrectly advertised on Amazon, but I attribute the fault to Timex, not to Amazon.  I actually bought one from Amazon and immediately returned it when I realized the Weekly alarm didn't exist (no probem; thanks Amazon). The only Timex I knew about with the "weekly" feature was another Ironman model T54281. I had owned this once before, but vowed not to buy it again because the band breaks within a short period and is not replaceable; this problem is noted in the many critical reviews on both the Timex and Amazon websites. I was getting discouraged, until somehow, after more web browsing, I found the T5K335, which does have the "weekly" feature (confirmed when I downloaded the PDF from the Timex website), as well as a band that appeared reasonably durable. So I ordered it from Amazon. After a few weeks, so far so good; but still hoping about the strap - seems better than the T5K335, but maybe not as durable as some other Timex watches. The band is "integrated", i.e. it goes all around the watch and is not replaceable. Why does Timex have to chose a seemingly less durable band for its "Weekly" alarm watches. For this reason I deduct 1 star.The following sums up my experience:The right Timex I wanted to seekBut my chances were seeming quite bleakTrue, they all take a lickingAnd keep right on tickingBut few alarms chime once a week

reviewText: Victorinox has made several "resin" watches over the years, and I purchased one of thier first for my young son and he enjoyed it a lot.  Since that model was not longer made, I bought one of these, but for my teenage son.  The watch is only slightly larger than a "unisex" or mid-size watch, so it is still easily worn by women or men with small wrists.  But like the previous model, the watch is rather cheaply built.  It has a glass lense (not mineral or saphire like my higher-end model) which means it chips easily.  Also, since it's plastic, the case obviously scratches easily.  The good news is that if you wear it enough to need a new band, it takes a common size that is easy to put on.  Unless you are a kid, or you don't care if you own this watch longer than the next school year, or, you don't plan to wear it working in the yard or elsewhere, than I would probably spend the extra $50 or so and get one of thier metal watches.

The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. reviewText: When reviewing a merchandise from Amazon, buyers often resort to criticizing the service (usually provided by market place merchants, not Amazon itself) and are frequently and promptly reminded by other reviewers to concentrate on the product, not circumstances under which they obtained it.With this review, I again want to emphasize that the check-out process, communication and promptness of delivery of this watch by Amazon has been stellar as always. The company's performance in this regard worked like a 'swiss clock'. Its attention to what was being sold and how, on the other hand, didn't.Once I held this 'timepiece' in my hand, I first and foremost realized that its crystal was NOT made of synthetic sapphire. As a test, albeit not the most reliable, one can knock the crystal with a nail: if the sound produced is like what one would expect to emanate from a solid rock, it's most likely sapphire. If the sound is more like quiet clinging from glass, the crystal's most likely made of mineral glass - a much cheaper and not desirable substitute. Those who know their watches also know all too well that sapphire is the most expensive part of a stainless steel Swiss quartz watch, once all the markup and pretentious hype is taken out. It's important to the product's reliability and integrity. Further, no one has to pay an exorbitant sum to own such a watch. Many, including some Wenger, Victorinox, Zodiac, and some Tissot watches can easily be found priced under $300.Researching the web, including Wenger's own site, revealed that the crystal of this watch is only 'sapphire-coated'. I shouldn't have to explain the difference.My second close examination found the watch bracelet made out of thin stamped stainless steel sheets, thus making the links hollow and taking away that subjective but wanted 'substantiality', or heft, in good watches. When handled, the 70489 Alpine - especially its bracelet - feels and sounds made of tin.Why then did I ever purchase it, one might ask? Look at the Amazon's page for this product, read through Product Specifications, and see for yourself what's stated there. Listed fifth from the top, it says 'Dial window material type: synthetic-sapphire'. So, it's only $119 with free s/h for a Swiss made, sapphire-crystalled watch with solid stainless steel body and bracelet - after all, the Amazon's description never explicitly stated otherwise, and no one could have thought genuine Swiss-made watches are made of cheap, stamped sheet metal - thus an excellent deal, and good looking too! How can one go wrong!It's currently on it's way back to Amazon, of course...So, with this very review, I give Amazon (Wenger should be ashamed as it is for giving this 'timepiece' - well, it's a piece of something for sure - a MSRP of $200) ZERO stars for such a beguiling description. Who looses here? Amazon, for I sent the product back for a full refund, and I'd hope anyone with self-respect and common sense did as well.On a side note, somewhat irrelevant to the purpose of this review, Wenger seems to have forgotten what the Swiss watch industry stands for in this day and age. No, their watches are NOT more reliable than Japanese- or even Chinese-made ones. Those frequently keep accurate time better. The construction, the materials, the aesthetics of a Swiss timepiece matter the most. Such watch must have some jewel-like properties to its quality, and that quality must be very good overall. It's having the back held by screws (the more, the merrier) and not of the push-in type, screw-in crown for better water resistance. The bracelet can be made of rubber and still be a very good one; however, if stainless steel's involved, it has to be nicely finished, 316L steel used throughout, including on the solid links. Or the watch could be made of ceramics, tungsten, and other high-quality, high-tech materials. And it's always welcome to have a synthetic sapphire crystal, even if that does push up the price.Wenger, if you forgo all the above, where does that leave you and your products that's so different a place in the minds of consumers from where all that Chinese-made garbage is?
summary: Amazon should correct the description or face more returns!

reviewText: I went on a Kickstarter spree for a while, backing anything that sounded interesting. Only a year or so prior, I really got into wrist watches and started collecting. Long story short, I backed this Cookoo and the Pebble smart watch. I'm still waiting on my white Pebble, but received the black/stainless Cookoo months ago and have since resold it.About the watch: It's so big (and very thick) it makes my diver watches look tame. The diver watches are good materials though, so the Cookoo being all plastic just looked tacky and childish at that size to me. There's very little contrast between the hands and dial... one of the MOST important functions of a watch... fail. Why do I feel it was an impulse buy? After thinking it through... this "smart watch" isn't very smart or useful (again, to me). Just lighting an icon to let me know I received an email, text, call, and so on isn't nearly as useful to me as knowing WHO left the said communication, meaning I'd still have to pull out my phone. Furthermore, with my phone in my pocket, I'd already know what kind of communication was left since there are different chimes for different notifications. Audible alerts are more seamless than even glancing at my watch. Yes, you might argue that you may have your phone on silent, but you could still set custom vibration types for different notifications... and still wear a watch that looks good. Finally, the watch frequently and randomly disconnected, requiring jumping through some hoops to get it back on track (iOS 5). What ever happened to "set it and forget it"? The watch does however have a battery that makes it last much longer than most smart watches that need charged, so there's that!

reviewText: The only useful thing about this watch is the ability to read emails and texts without pulling out your phone. I have my phone in my pocket so it's not that much more useful. If you have it in your purse or bag, then this watch might be a little more useful to you. The screen is weak however; I've had it for less than a month and I've already scratched the screen. Battery life is mediocre; it dropped to 20% in 3 days. 20% battery means it's going to die within a couple hours max. The battery life on my watch might have been lowered because I have the "shake to illuminate" on, but it's a design flaw that the shake sensitivity is too high that it causes the light to come on too often. The strap hold is also loose, and comes out all the time, which makes the end of the wrist strap stick out.Just about all the apps that you can use are pretty useless. The music controller app is okay; it doesn't start automatically and the only functions is play/pause and next/previous song...no fast forwarding, no volume control (unless you use another app which requires a paid purchase on your phone).All in all, it's an okay watch but for the usability's worth, I would value it at under $100 for a new one. Would I recommend it? Only if often need to check your phone for messages and access to your phone is limited (you're in class/at work, phone is in your purse/bag, etc.). Otherwise, it's not really necessary for the price...maybe wait a year or two for better ones to come out.

reviewText: So, being the guy I am, I like a good, manly bag.  None of this purse crap, right?  So I did some research, and this is the bag that won.  I've owned a couple messenger bags in the past, but felt like nothing really fit correctly in them.  My laptop bag is the same style as this bag - instead of  the "landscape" orientation that you get with messenger bags, this is a "portrait" orientation.  I've owned this bag for a little over nine months now, and it's more durable than any bag I've ever had before.  When I bring it to work, I can fit any tools I need, a coffee cup, an ipod, and headphones in it, along with various pens, my phone, and a charger.  When I'm out and about, I can carry a sweater, my tablet, a notebook, and anything that I might come across in my journeys.  The bag holds just about as much as I can comfortably carry around in a day without being overly uncomfortable or heavy.  It seems to be the perfect size, and due to its slimmer, longer profile, doesn't seem to get caught on anything or anyone while on an airplane or public transportation. I do have few complaints, though.  One of which is the strap.  It's attached to the bag via the top - and many other reviewers complained about this.  The strap on mine has come off twice.  I took this bag to a tailor, and they fixed it for about $22.00 dollars the first time, and after the strap came off again, they repaired it for free.  My other complaint - the large pocket on the outside of the main compartment, inside the flap has a sharp edge that I have cut my finger on a few times.  There's a learning curve to this bag.Update:  Two years later and the bag is still ticking.  It fits everything. I love it and when fails (not in foreseeable future) I intend on rebuying.Update 2:  This bag finally failed.  The clasp on the bag gave out, and I tried to replace it myself but was unsuccessful. I purchased a new one immediately and received it today.  I believe the first one I received was a knock off - the build quality of the new bag is top-notch and it has Rothco labels sewn onto the inside. title: Suunto Core Black Military
description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. Once the Core senses the change, the Storm Alarm sounds and flashes, letting you know that something unpleasant is fast approaching. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. The Suunto Core carries a two-year warranty.

reviewText: This product does not come with instructions, so it takes some time to get the positioning right.My doctor told me to get this product, and said it would help relieve pressure on the bladder and ligament pain.Here's what i have discovered:This band needs to be worn higher than you would think. I thought it would go under the belly, as to hold the belly up (as in the photo). Instead, it works best to use it on the belly (about 2-3 inches higher than the photo).It does not help with bladder pressure at all. If anything, it makes you have to pee more...but you're already peeing so much anyway, who cares.It works WONDERS for ligament pain. Before getting this, I could not function on my feet at all. Walking around the grocery store or down the street, or even standing and cooking for too long in the kitchen would send me screaming and crying in pain. Like super bad stabbing pain that could only be soothed by getting into the fetal position. Everyone told me it was normal...but it hurt so bad. When i wear the band, I dont have that pain at all. i can go for an hour long walk, go grocery shopping, ANYTHING. It's fabulous!It has helped with stretch marks. I think. I say that because when i take the band off i can feel the pain of my skin stretching, which i don't feel when it's on. i'm not an expert on stretch marks.I haven't noticed that it helps with back pain, but i have preexisting back issues so it may work for the everyday person.I wear mine pretty much all day every day, right on my skin, under my stretchy pants (aren't stretchy pants wonderful? The BEST part of being pregnant...). I have not tried wearing it on top of clothing. My doctor warned not to wear it while laying down and sleeping.I also have never washed mine, because I don't want to have to do laundry without wearing it. That would probably suck.I hope this helps. I would definitely buy it again...and it's SO worth the price. It would get another star if it helped with the bladder or back.EDIT: Also, I bought the L/XL and i have a 7.5 month weight of 250lbs. It's huge.

title: Casio PRW 3000 Watch
description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: So far I've used this on just one winter backpacking trip, and a few times around the apartment.Pros:- Very warm. Lots of insulation, and the cord locks seal in even more heat if you need to, and keep out snow etc. The fact that no snow melted or froze on these shows how well it kept the heat in.- Fabric seems fairly durable (but not the stitching), and water resistant. I walked around in the snow a lot around my campsite, and these were fine. The 'Polar Proven' writing on the sole wears off immediately, but that has no effect on the usability of the product- lightweight- Vegan (most booties are made with down)Cons:- Stitching came loose after a few days! at the front of the toes, right wear the front of the sole meets the bottom of the black reinforcing nylon. Haven't noticed seam tears elsewhere yet, but have seen a few loose threads.- Not compressible. I packed these in a compression sack for a day, but the soles are stiff and so these don't compress much.- Writing on the sole comes off and can get on your stuff- after a few hours in an expensive sil-nylon stuff sack, that sack now has the 'Polar Proven' writing permanently marked all over it, kinda like an iron-on pattern. It doesn't bother me that much, just adds character to my gear, but that writing is just silly and they should get rid of it or make it last longer. I don't think it had any effect on traction when it was there anyway.Note on sizing: I wear a men's 11 - 11.5, and got a large, and found these slightly short. Definitely wearable, but tight in the toes. So I'd recommend a larger size.Bottom line, if these would hold up better, they'd be great. Eventually I will get around to having the damaged sole repaired, or do it myself, but it might be tricky to sew because of the location of the tear. Currently, they are still usable despite the damage, but I haven't used them much. If you get these, realize that repairing these will be necessary and inevitable, and soon after you start using them. As it is, there are few vegan booty options out there, and these are inexpensive, so as long as you're okay with the inevitable repairs, you'll probably like them.

reviewText: Firstly,  this watch did not impress me.  I like watches and at first I was excited to get this one because it is a "smart" watch.  Upon first touch, I immediately noticed that it was comprised of lower grade plastic.  Plastic push buttons, easily scratched plastic face, lower grade band--overall a lower grade build quality for the going price. I was not too impressed.  However, I pressed on and was determined to see what this new device could do once paired up to my Samsung Galaxy S 4.  "Maybe the functions outweigh the cheapness, I thought".To get this watch to work with the phone, I had to download the "PEBBLE APP" from Google .  In the activation process of the app, the user is required to permit a function called "accessibility" in the phone.  There was no way around this requirement.  So, to use the "smart" part of the phone this feature had to be enabled in order to continue with the app installation.  Instantly after the download the program and watch connected and determined that the phone needed a firmware update, which was performed.  So far so good.I was now receiving my e-mail on my watch screen. I could change my watch face. I could control my phone music through the watch buttons.  All of this was pretty cool and this functionality overshadowed the lackluster build quality.Well, here comes the depressing part.  I then went back to my phone to search the web and much to my shock and horror, the phone kept announcing the actions of going back and forward on internet searches.  This was a spoken voice in the loudest volume that my phone possesses.  I could not turn the volume down, nor stop the speach using "settings/accessibility" in the phone.  Upon quick research I found that others had the same problem with this loud, obnoxious announcing every move made on internet searches.  Nobody on the blog pages had a good, solid solution for this problem and how to stop it.  Some suggested unchecking all features of "accessibility/Talkback" on the phone and then removing this app from the phone entirely.  Well, I did uncheck the features and upon finishing, my phone spoke every app, button, etc. on each screen of the phone that I was on.  Then my phone locked up and I could not enter my security code.  For each number pressed, the voice said "dot".  My phone was taken back to the phone store.  The people there new nothing about the problems associated with a Pebble watch used with a Samsung Galaxy S 4. All they could do was to do a factory reset on my phone which eliminated my contacts and apps.So, upon arrival back home I promptly put the watch back into the box and shelved it hoping that the battery would eventually die in it.  I then reworked the phone.This watch has some issues worth investigating for certain phones/devices. For me, to use the watch just as a watch, and with no "smart" functionality just doesn't fit my bill.  It is rather big , for just a watch.  It is rather cheaply built , for just a watch.  Time will tell--maybe by waiting someone will make this watch work.
summary: Poor build quality, limited function, Pebble App requires Accessibility (Talkback)

reviewText: I love my Suunto Core!  It is amazingly comfortable, even more so than my other smaller watches.  It is a great watch and tool.  I love the comments when people see it.  I was a little worried about the large glass face and scratches, but after 1.5 years, there was not a single scratch on the crystal.  The battery seemed to last about 6 months so it has been replaced.  Take note, the symbol indicating low battery only goes on for about a day before it completely dies.  However, there is a big HOWEVER -- the rotating bezel has a plastic ring between the aluminum bezel and the watch base.  Over time, this loosened making the bezel spin more freely and then finally it popped right off.  The plastic ring sort of creates a snap fit for holding the bezel to the watch that can wear out.  So, I would suggest getting a version without the rotating bezel.  On the plus side, I was pleasantly surprised that a real live person answered my customer service call on the second ring.  Right now, my watch is being shipped to Suunto to hopefully be covered by their 2 year warranty.  I had hoped that Suunto would simply send me a new plastic ring, but I was told that 1.  No, I had to send it in, and 2.  This was one of their most common issues with the watch.

reviewText: Very pleased with this mount! I've got a Polar RS100 heart-rate monitor and this mount fits it perfectly.  The similar Polar branded bike mount requires zip-ties for mounting, which means it's a semi-permanent installation.  The Timex mount is great in that it just flexes apart and pops on or off, so if you don't ride with the monitor all the time (or want to switch it between bikes), it's no problem. I'm using this with 31.8mm handlebars on a Cannondale Six carbon road bike, and the grip is just right (I don't have to tighten the wrist band on the watch too much, but I can imagine with smaller diameter handlebars, you might have to).  Some of the other mounts at Amazon require a 'large' size for the thicker road bike handlebars, but this seems to cover just about every size. My only possible complaint would be that it might look better in black, as opposed to the vaguely military looking green, but it's mostly concealed by the watch and looks pretty sleek. I've now got a wireless Cateye speed/cadence computer on my stem, and the Polar HRM beside it on the handlebars when I'm seriously training, and the combo works perfectly.

reviewText: I purchased this for a little more than 8 bucks after seeing it mentioned in a "dealzmodo" post on gizmodo. For what it is, it's a nice little watch.It's very small and light. You will forget you're even wearing it as soon as you put it on your wrist. It has a very thin profile so it won't catch on your pocket or other things when reaching into tight spaces. The band is a little on the shorter size. I have about a 7" wrist circumference and this is about the largest the watch will accommodate comfortably. I usually wear it on the 3rd or 4th hole from the end. It's pretty tight for me when wearing it on the 4th. It feels better on the 3rd but then the little band that slides over the the excess strap after it's buckled doesn't have much to hold on to and slides off very easily. If you wear it on the 1st or second hole, you won't even be able to utilize the little band the the end of the watch strap will always stick out from your wrist. The band quality is also not the greatest. I'm sure it would break within a couple years if you wear it regularly. However, you can't really expect more for the price.The mineral display is very clear and easy to read. Since the bezel is flush with the screen, it would probably be pretty easy to scratch if you rubbed it up against a wall or something. There is a small green LED light on the left side of the display that can be activated to view the time in the dark. It could be better, but it lights up the screen just enough to be able to view all the characters in the dark.It's rather light on features but has all the main ones you would need in a basic digital watch. Time (12 and 24 hour), date,  stopwatch, and alarm (with hourly chime option). It keeps great time too.Overall, this is a great watch for the money. I bought it to wear in situations where I don't want to risk harm to my G-Shock MTG-900. You don't have to be careful with this one. It can be abused and if it breaks or is lost, you're only out about $10 and it can easily be replaced. 5 stars easily.

The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). reviewText: I recently ordered this watch from Amazon as a companion for a LTt Observer to wear in the field.  While the Observer is a more updated model they both share very similiar features and ease of operation.My first recommendation is that you do order this from amazon.com and be wary of the same item offered by "market place sellers".  At the time I initially placed the order amazon.com was out and the wait was estimated to be 3 to 5 weeks.  Since the item was also offered by another seller in amazon's referral system I placed an order and wound up with the wrong watch; turns out the market place seller didn't carry the black face model.  Fortunately amazon got a supply in and shipped my watch within 24 hours....good service.  The black face is a little hard to come by.Now then, to the watch itself.  First of all it IS big...but very light; almost as light as the titanium Observer I have.  The larger face makes it easier to read and Suunto has apparently gone back to the leather (waterproof) band, which I prefer.  Functionally, the watch is a full blown time keeper and (non GPS) navigation system including stop watch/chronometer functions, an accurate altimeter, a barometer and digital compass.  Both the compass and the altimeter are as accurate as I've found in analog portable units.  The alarms are sufficiently loud (unlike the only chink in the Observer) and my only criticism is that the back light is weak compared to the Observer, but that fault doesn't draw anything away from the 5 star rating.  Add the user replaceable battery (Suunto makes a kit that includes the battery, a water/dust seal and a new cap), the intuitive operating system and you have the ultimate back country time piece.Suunto was the first to offer this type of time piece and, in my opinion, still offers the best.  I've used their diving computers and field compasses for years and am a fan of the company's many products.  I don't think there's a clunker in the catalog.
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Initially I wanted a multifunction watch that didn't cost an arm and leg and I researched many products before settling on the Casio SGW400H-1B, it looked like just the ticket for less than $70. It's a handsome watch and fairly easy to read because of decent contrast in normal lighting conditions and it is not as bulky on my wrist as a more sofisticated and expensive multifunction watch would be.The main reason for my 3-star rating stems from the hour hand being significantly misaligned, especially noticable at the 6 o'clock and 12 o'clock positions. I accept the fact that an inexpensive watch can't be expected to provide accurate barometric pressure or altimeter readings and I know accurate temp readings must be off the wrist for a few minutes. But the lack of quality control is immediately obvious because of the misaligned analog hands and the alignment is not resolved by following the instruction manual.Such is the nature of mass-produced consumer level products made in third world countries. I got what I paid for. I still plan to buy a higher quality Casio multifunction watch (near $200) that doesn't have analog hands that won't detract from it's beauty and functionality. Until then I'll live with my choice.

reviewText: I got these for recovering from running/cycling workouts, because I had read a lot about these new "Recovery Socks" which cost $30+. These do the same thing at half the price. If I run in the evening, I put them on after a shower and wear them until I go to bed. For me at least, they reduce soreness in the morning. The compressive part of the sock ends at the forefoot, so your toes are not mashed together, which is something I hadn't thought about but I'm glad they did. Fit is important, so make sure you read Futuro's sizing instructions if they're not listed on here. The amount of compression these provide is probably half based on how they fit (how big your calves are) and the socks compression rating. "Moderate" is a good place to start, but I think next time I'll get something tighter. They also lose some compression over time, but its nothing that would prevent me from getting these again.

reviewText: Beats every hi end watch hands down.  I rarely spend over $500 for a watch but have owned several Seikos in that price range.  This Pathfinder is fantastic and beats every brand and type of watch I have ever owned.  In the Army Rangers, I/we used Seikos for accuracy and as a macho thing.  I wish this watch would have been available back then.  It is incredibly accurate, never runs out of power is tough titanium and classy as can be.  I'm retired now and partially disabled so cannot use the bells and whistles like I wish but we have 20 acres in farm and woods and this thing is incredible for the 'survival' tools included.  I have another Casio Sport Pathfinder that I misplaced.  It has almost the same bells and whistles as the Titanium but is made from durable black plastic/rubber.  I wore it when doing the rough stuff as to not damage my 'nicer' watches.  I missed it so much I went for the Titanium Pathfinder and am glad I misplaced the Sport.  I never take off the Titanium even when doing the rough stuff outside.  It is incredibly resistant, never seems to scratch and all I do is wipe it down and my wife and I can go to church or a nice restaurant.  I get more complements for this than for any other watch I have ever owned.  We found my Sport Pathfinder and I feel guilty.  Like I bought home a new puppy that is a favorite and the ol reliable has to sit alone and is lucky to be put by a window to recharge the solar battery.  I didn't mind finding new homes for my pretty Seikos but I can't give up my Sport.  Reminds me to much of the Titanium.If you like the outdoors and NEED to keep accurate time, the Casio Pathfinder is a must.

reviewText: The good:This is not as big of a watch as you might think from looking at the picture. I like that.The LCD is clear with excellent contrast, and has a wide viewing angle. The viewing angle is the reason I was looking to replace my Armitron, which had a narrow viewing angle LCD that required aligning the wrist each time.The display prompts you when you are in the settings mode. This is my first Ironman but I had no trouble setting everything without looking at the instructions. Another bonus is you can set up / down if you miss your mark. Intuitive and well designed!The band is comfortable. In fact the whole watch is comfortable. An improvement over my G-Shock where I really feel that I'm wearing it the whole time.The illumination is superb. You can set a mode by holding illumination for 4 seconds where you can illuminate it with a push of any button, for example the Start/Split on the top. Very convenient.The buttons are easily pushed on purpose and hard to push on accident due to the guards around them and the stiffness.The locking band keeper is an excellent feature that I didn't have any trouble working with as some people have reported here.Stronger mineral glass lens vs acrylic for almost all the other Ironman series.200M water resist vs 100M for almost all the other Ironman series.The beeper is loud enough without being annoying.The bad: Viewing angle! Woe is me, I have purchased yet another watch with a viewing angle problem... the main reason I was shopping for a replacement for my Armitron. While the display is legible at all angles, it can't be seen without turning the wrist due to the high wall where the Start/Split button is and the deep recessing of the display within the face. This is not readily apparent looking at the marketing photos. So disappointing. But its such a stellar watch in every other respect, and the Armitron is really showing its age, so I will keep this. If this watch ever dies, I will try another Ironman but from the models with an acrylic lens that have a lower height. Maybe you will prefer the deep set aesthetic, I don't. Its probably due to the 200M depth and the mineral lens. I really don't need a watch with that level of protection; I would trade it for a wider viewing angle.To summarize the watch is remarkably comfortable and just exudes quality. Almost perfect.

reviewText: People raved about the traction. I guess the traction is okay for people who are using the booties for exercising. For those of us who are in wheelchairs or who, like I, have paralyzed feet, the traction is NOT sufficient. For people such as I, traction means an entirely different thing -- and the issue of traction is more than a slight inconvenience. Lack of traction could mean a trip to the hospital, and it could mean life or death. So when I put my feet on our hardwood floors and they slid, this was NOT a happy thing. I had ordered four pairs, thinking these booties really didn't slide because reviewers said they didn't. I thought I had found a solution to a huge problem, because I had to wear Crocs to bed in case I had use the restroom in the night, and I really did not want to do so. Alas, I still have to wear Crocs to bed. Bummer.

reviewText: I used to have just the best watch ever--it was waterproof and comfortable with a swimsuit-type material band. I lost it and it drove me crazy trying to find a watch I might like as much as that one. I bought this one after perusing all that Amazon had to offer. I am a female with rather small wrists and I have to use either the second or third to last holes but any woman would be able to easily wear this watch. The face is the width of about two and a half to three fingers across.(I always like wearing bigger watches and this one looked bigger than I thought it would when I unpacked it but I am very happy with its size after wearing it for a while) The only negative I've found with it is that you cannot silence the buttons--at least I haven't found a way to do so.It doesn't feel flimsy at all and it is durable. The band is pretty rigid. The buttons are yellow and a nice contrast to the navy band. I've worn it doing just about everything and it always lives up to my expectations. I particularly like the interface with the day of the week and the date on top and that I can very easily keep two separate time zones at the same time.Definitely recommend.

reviewText: For my birthday, our daughter bought me a pair of Sloggers in a size 9 (I normally wear a 9.5).  They fit okay...a little bit short in the heal with the way Sloggers slope in the back, but still not bad.  However, I was worried that if my feet swelled up in the summer heat, or I ever tried to wear socks with them, my feet wouldn't fit.  So I ordered the size 10 along with the "Half-Sizer" insoles just to see which one fit the best and which one I should return.  The "Half-Sizer" insole is really (and I mean REALLY) thin, but you slide it under the insole that comes with the shoes and it pushes up the foot bed enough to make a difference, albeit a slight one. I'm sure one could cut a Scholl's insert (from the store) to fit as well if they needed something a bit thicker. But for me, I live in the boonies and didn't want to go all the way into town when I could have these delivered right to my door.  And the height was just enough to make them comfortable without being too snug.  Att least I will be able to fit my foot inside should I ever have socks on, which I will come late Fall and Winter.  I absolutely love these shoes for going outside and gardening or taking out the trash.  I leave them by the front door and anytime I want to go outside, I just slip them on.  No laces to tie.  So convenient.  I can't tell you how many other shoes I have messed up going out to water plants and have inadvertently ended up standing in puddles of mud. Tennis shoes have rotted. Suede and leather shoes never look the same.  But Sloggers, they are awesome. If they get dirty or dusty, you just hose them off.  After hearing me rave about them, our daughter who just started gardening this year decided to keep the size 9 for herself instead of returning them. She is really pleased with them too.

reviewText: I am just getting my feet wet into the sport of cycling, so everything that I am getting is entry level quality and thus I have nothing else to compare these shoes to, I have never wore other brand or more expensive cycling shoes.The quick review is that these are the biggest bargain you are going to find out there, order your pair before they run out, remember it is May, the beginning of cycling season, so everybody is buying their gear.Now, the more detailed review:These run a little small in size depending if you have a wide fat foot or long skinny feet. I usually ware 10.5 or 11 USA size depending on the brand of shoes, but I had to order these size 44 which is the equivalent of a 9.5-10 USA size. So, if you have a fat foot or have bunions then order the size 45, but if you have skinny feeds, get the size 44.Comfort. I find these shoes very comfortable for their purpose, as long as you on the bike, you don't feel them, the size 44 fits me very snug and it works well for when I am pulling up on the pedals, I feel my feet, the shoes and the pedals as one piece. Note, because of the big size cleat on the bottom, these shoes are not meant to be walking a lot, and you better be careful on tile floors because you will slip due to the plastic cleats.Quality. These look great, they are not leather, but they look very nice. The craftsmanship is perfect, I don't see anything wrong that could give me a sign of any trouble, except the they only had them in white and they will get dirty soon. But, then again I am gentile with my equipment. I am sure there are people out there that even if you give them steel shoes they will find a way to ware them out and destroy them. But if you careful with your equipment, these look like they can last a very long time.Features.Part of the shoes are mesh opening to keep your feet cool but you can hardly tell. The two bottom laces are velcro, but the top lace has a plastic belt with a nice ratchet mechanism that works really well, and again, as long as you treat it with respect, I don't foresee any trouble there. These use the LOOK system, the cleats attach very well to the shoes and hold very secure to the pedals. Although, the LOOK style has bigger size cleats, it still is a pain to click into the pedals, so shoes with cleats are not meat for high traffic city riding, for that just get regular pedals to be safe.Conclusion.This is the best deal out there for the new comer. Excellent quality for being entry level. I love the LOOK system. The kit includes the shoes, the cleats and the pedals, everything that you need to start riding. These are more expensive then mountain bike version, but are very well worth the extra $20 not only in terms of the LOOK system which is better, but also in terms of the overall quality of the product as a whole.Last but not least, let me school those who like me, have no clue about the difference between a mountain bike vs road bike shoes difference.The cleats, the piece that attaches to the bottom of the shoes is much smaller for the mountain bike type of shoes, and I find two drawback about this style of shoes, first I find it much harder to click into the pedal because one has to be more accurately since the cleat is so small. Second, because the cleats are so small, it doesn't cover a big portion of the shoe sole, and you can feel that when you pulling up on the pedal.On the other hand, the road bike style shoes which these are, use the type "LOOK" system, this style has a much bigger cleat piece that is much easier to click into the pedal and because it is a big cleat, it attaches to a bigger surface of the shoes sole, so when you are pedaling up, the whole shoes come up, it doesn't feel as if you are going to yank the shoe from the petal. In short, the conclusion is for you to go for the LOOK type of shoes, not the mountain bike type.
